Something passed over them, casting a shadow- Rune was floating away on her hand-slab, batting desperately at the clouds of insects harrying her. She suddenly shot upwards, shedding most of the bugs.

“Seems like the fight’s going well,” Tattletale added over the sound of battle. There was an explosion, a crash, and a roar of pain that suddenly cut out.

Fog suddenly erupted out of the alleyway, rapid clicking sounds coming from within his cloud form. Butcher leapt out after them, a huge flail in one hand and a nightstick in the other. She looked different than the Empire’s surveillance photos; less bulky, less shiny, and the cape was back in a darker shade of blue. She roared as Fog surged towards her, and then disappeared. An answering bang came from inside the cloud that made Fog’s Changer form swell and ripple- Theo saw a flash of light that briefly cast a shadow of something inside. Something with a lot of legs.

Metallic clangs and gristly thuds and inhuman screeches came from inside Fog as Butcher and Night thrashed about, Fog moving around to keep them both covered. Theo saw deep gouges in the asphalt left behind as they fought back and forth, the boom of Butcher’s teleport sounding again and again. Each time, Fog’s cloud shrank a little; as if the heat and force of the explosions was disrupting him.

Then Night’s cloaked form abruptly flew backwards out of the cloud, tumbling across the asphalt. Cerberus whistled, and one of her monstrous dogs thudded over and placed a paw on Night’s back as she struggled to rise.

Fog surged after her, but another explosion came from within, and the cloud wavered, then suddenly condensed back into Fog in his grey cloak, with Butcher standing over him. She jabbed stiff fingers under his chin, then chopped him in the side of his neck, and he collapsed.

“No,” Night hissed as Butcher strode over. “No-”

Butcher jammed the end of her baton into Night’s back. “Lift the paw,” she said. Cerberus whistled another command, the paw came up, and there was a clicking sound from the baton, like a taser. Night spasmed a few times before going still. The paw was replaced, pinning her down.

“Kaiser’s down, Jotun’s down, Rune’s out of my range,” Butcher said, collapsing the baton and tucking it into a compartment on her shin. “Tats, you called the PRT?”

“They’re on their way now. Extra security for Kaiser- Armsmaster’s bringing his tranquilisers.”

“Good to know,” Butcher said as Theo saw his avenues of escape close off one by one. Then she turned towards Theo, insects streaming out of her armour and from all over the street, and he felt cold fear drip down his spine. He took his free hand off Aster’s head and stuck it in his pocket.

The lower part of Butcher’s helmet opened up, revealing a pale jaw framed by steel mandibles, small fangs poking past her lips. Metal eyebrows popped up on her forehead. “Are you okay, Golem?” she asked. The insects around her peeled off to plant themselves on Night and Fog.

“Wait, Golem?” Tattletale demanded as Theo struggled to speak. “Seriously? Holy shit, that’s incredible.”

“The guy from Lord of the Rings?” Cerberus asked.

“No, that’s Gollum,” Butcher said. “A golem is an old Jewish legend- a rabbi sculpts a statue out of clay, writes instructions on a scroll or on its forehead, and it will obey commands, usually to defend the Jewish people. Very interesting choice of name,” she finished, glancing at Theo.

Theo said nothing, even as Aster screamed for soothing, smearing snot across his shirt.

Butcher held up her hands, eyebrows lowering. “Okay, fair enough. Look, even if you don’t believe me, I’m not going to hurt you two. It can’t have been easy having Kaiser for a father.”

Aster was still wailing, thrashing about in the baby carrier. Theo couldn’t make himself take his hands away from the asphalt pieces.

Butcher glanced from Theo’s face to Aster’s little head, and then back to Theo. “Okay,” she said with a sigh, taking a few steps back.

Theo didn’t relax, exactly. But it felt a lot easier to breath.

“I’m going to go drag the rest of them over here,” Butcher said, thumbing back towards the plaza. “Stay or go, it’s your choice.”

She turned and walked away, leaving Theo with space to think, with Aster still screaming in her carrier. What now? Butcher had seen enough of his face and powers that she could find him again. And with Armsmaster on the way, the PRT would know too. If Kaiser really was down, then the PRT would know his identity as soon as they got his helmet off, and then they’d know Theo’s.

“If we beat the Empire, does that mean we get their bounty money?” he heard Cerberus ask from behind him.

“I don’t think it works like that,” Tattletale answered. “Probably the PRT and the cops will take it, since it’s criminal assets now.”

Theo managed to pull his hand out of his pocket to start stroking Aster’s head, making shushing noises. Aster continued bawling, so Theo freed both hands, pulling her out of the carrier to rest her against his shoulder, bouncing her gently. Aster quieted down a little, though she was still unhappy.

“It’s okay,” Theo said with a soothing tone he didn’t believe himself. “It’s all going to be okay.”

Metal scraping preceded Butcher’s return- She was hauling Kaiser by the back of his dented armour, his feet dragging along the ground. Jotun was slung limp across her shoulders, dripping blood from his mouth, and she was carrying Theo’s suitcase and backpack. None of the weight seemed to bother her at all.

She set the bags down a few feet away from Theo with a careful look, then took a few steps away to lay Kaiser and Jotun down next to Night and Fog. “Tattletale, what’s the ETA on transport?”

“About a minute, maybe less.”

Butcher started to nod, then cocked her head. “Less than that. Here comes the big guy.”

A second later, Theo heard the roar of an engine as a motorcycle rounded the corner. Armsmaster came to a sudden halt and dismounted smoothly, halberd in hand. “Undersiders,” he said cordially, visor immediately turning towards Kaiser. “Excellent work,” he said in a pleased voice.

“Thanks,” Butcher replied. “Been waiting a long time for this.”

“You and me both.” Armsmaster stepped forward, the butt of his halberd extending a thing needle, that he poked into a gap in Kaiser’s armour. “Looks like you made a clean arrest. Not a scratch on you.”

“Well, yes and no.” Butcher held up a hand. “Fog managed to seep through my gloves. There’s some skin growing back there.”

Armsmaster grimaced slightly. “Ah.” He turned to Theo, and it took a lot of nerve to keep from stepping backward. That would make him look guilty. “And I don’t believe I’ve seen you before.”

Theo scrambled for something to say, even as Aster kept crying into his shoulder. He bounced her again and smoothed her hair for lack of any other ideas.

“Yeah, funny story there,” Butcher said cheerfully. “First Kaiser brought in those Heim idiots, then he tried to pressgang Parian, and I don’t know if you heard the irony about that-”

“I’ve heard,” Armsmaster said with a quirk of his lips.

“And then he tries to get the lad here to join. His name’s Golem. Hilarious, right?”

“So he got two morons on his side, and two wrong choices that lost him everything,” Tattletale said from behind. “He sure can pick them.”

Armsmaster actually chuckled. “That is pretty good.” He gave Golem a thoughtful look. “Are you just starting out, Golem?”

Theo swallowed and made himself speak. “Yes sir.”

Armsmaster nodded. “I’d suggest considering a team. It’s much easier to have support. Especially if you have someone to take care of. Unless you’re spoken for?” He glanced towards Elpis.

“I think he might be better off with a different team,” Elpis said quickly- the first time he’d heard her sound rushed. “I don’t think I’ve got the right resources to help take care of a baby. Your choice, obviously,” she said to Theo, “but I think the PRT could find you a better place.”

Not much of a choice. But Butcher seemed to be giving Theo an out- a better place, a different place than Brockton Bay. The Protectorate might not fully trust him, but now that they knew of him, they could be his best shot at taking care of Aster. His little sister sniffled and rubbed her face against his shoulder, and all of a sudden Theo’s mind was made up.

“Yes, please. Is it possible to be placed in a different city? Uh, I mean-”

“Yeah, even with the Empire beaten, having a name like Golem would make you a target,” Tattletale said, walking up to join the conversation. She winked at Theo with the eye Armsmaster couldn’t see.

“Um. Yes, that’s true.”

“We can certainly arrange a placement for you and your…”

“Sister, sir. She’s the only family I have left,” Theo said firmly.

“Ah. Yes, that’s doable. The vans are 30 seconds out- we can give you a lift to headquarters to discuss things if you like,” Armsmaster offered.

“Yes please,” Theo said.

Faint sirens announced PRT vans coming closer, green and white lights flashing around the corner.

“Well, good to know that’s settled,” Butcher said cheerfully. “We’ll help you load this lot. And Golem,” she turned to Theo with a hand held out, “I wish you the very best of luck.”

Theo stared at the hand for a long second, before carefully taking it. Despite his fears, Butcher’s grip was firm but not painful, unlike the crushing handshakes his father’s followers had usually used. And there was something soft tickling his palm. He looked into the silver lenses in Butcher’s helmet, and saw a very faint shadow of eyes looking steadily back at him.

Theo shook once and then took his hand away, slipping it into a pocket to roll the object in his fingers. It felt like a roll of bills.

PRT vans came around the corner, purple stripes on the side with the winged shield symbol on top. Theo stood back and watched as his father and the last of his supporters were fitted with restraints, loaded into the backs of the vans, and sprayed with containment foam for good measure.

Armsmaster gently guided him to take a seat in the one empty van with a couple of troopers who greeted him cheerily, then closed the door for him. Before it shut, Theo caught a glimpse of Butcher giving him a nod.

Once the van was moving, and once the troopers weren’t paying too much attention to him, Theo carefully brought the object out of his pocket to his side and glanced down. It was a roll of bills after all- fifties and hundreds. A thick roll- there must have been a thousand dollars in there.

Theo shoved it deep into his pocket and patted Aster again, who was finally starting to settle down. He’d think about it later.

Chapter 140: 14.5

Wednesday 15th June, The Lair, The Docks

“The bad news is that your vehicle was spotted driving out of the city limits, significantly modified with armour and weapons. The good news is that we’re now certain that the Teeth have left Brockton Bay.”

“Fucking cowards,” Butcher sighed.

“At least we don’t have to worry about Taylor having to kill them,” Flinch said.

“That’s good to hear,” I said. “Any word on the ABB? Or the Monster Bunch?”

“So far, not much. There’s chatter of Bakuda gathering up materials and tools, but we haven’t found anything about the Monster Bunch. It’s possible that they folded into the Teeth, or struck out on their own.” Director Piggot chuffed with amusement. “You made quite an impression in taking down Kaiser.”

“He made it too easy,” I said, running a finger over the sword mounted on my wall. Kaiser’s last creation before I’d beaten him senseless and peeled him out of his armour like a prawn, now a war trophy in the lair. It felt good.

“Hmm. I’ll let you know if anything else pops up.”

“Thank you, Director. Same to you.”

Piggot hung up, and I tucked my phone back into my pocket, looking at the wall. There were a number of trophies on there now- not just Haemorrhagia’s little clover keychain, but the masks of the deceased members of the Teeth that I’d requested from the PRT; Spree, Vex, Snowblind and Sinister. Kaiser’s sword was mounted on a couple of hooks, and I’d snagged a chunk of the glassed asphalt from what people were already calling Slash Crater.

And all of those trophies were nicely arranged around the big map of Brockton Bay, with the pane of glass over it for me to draw territories and notes on with markers.

There was a lot less colour than there used to be. With only Rune left at large and Othala not yet deprogrammed from Cherish’s power, the Empire had no capes left to field, and the heroes had searched and seized all through their holdings without resistance. Kaiser’s secret identity of Max Anders had been exposed, so his company was being audited for any tricks he might have done with the numbers.

The Monster Bunch had disappeared, their old building vacated; the Boardwalk was secure now that Parian was taking a more active role in protecting it, and I made sure the Undersiders were seen helping with that- and the ABB had been quiet. Bakuda’s bombs were potent, but one Tinker against dozens of heroes was still a bad match up. Pretty soon I’d need to start planning for when the city was villain-free; either new villains would try to move in and we’d have to beat them back, or we’d have to start looking further afield for things to do. There was always Boston and New York- I’d heard that Blasto was acting up lately, more of his creations being seen on the streets.

“So what’s the plan for dealing with her?” I asked out loud.

“We can handle her foot soldiers,” Tactical said. “Unless there’s been a Trigger we haven’t heard about, they’re just normals with guns. Maybe not even guns.”

“There’s bound to be a couple of new capes around though,” Stoneknapper said. “The bombings, Leviathan, then the Nine? Someone will have got powers out of all that shit.”

“Yeah, but that doesn’t mean they’ll be working for Bakuda,” Anchorage countered. “Or that they’ll have a power that’ll work as well with her tech as Oni Lee’s did.”

“There’ll be traps,” Tock Tick said. “And if she doesn’t have some kind of deadman switch, then I’m Doc Brown.”

“All true,” I said. “Not like I was planning on killing her.”

“No, but now that she knows her timestop bombs work, she might want to take a swing at you,” Quarrel pointed out. “And I don’t want to spend fuck knows how long stuck as a snowglobe.”

“Also a point. I could try taking her out at long range. Just dogpile her with insects, a few shots to wreck whatever tech she’s got on her. I’m pretty sure I could smash that grenade launcher she’s got.”

“Assuming it doesn’t blow up when you hit it, and blow her up, and set off the deadman switch,” Firecracker said.

I winced. “Yeah. Man, she’s not making it easy.”

“We could try wearing her down,” Nemean suggested. “She needs to sleep, we don’t. We could just run her ragged until she drops from exhaustion.”

“That’s pretty good. I don’t like how much damage she might do before she drops, but we’ll keep that in mind.” I checked my watch. “Anyway, I should get going.”

I picked up my helmet from the workbench and slipped it on. The plates covering my neck connected to it, and the helmet’s mechanisms locked it into the fasteners on the silk hood covering my hair. I rolled my neck from side to side with satisfaction, and teleported out from the lair.

With the Empire down, we were moving forward with our plans to revitalise Brockton Bay. Tattletale had vetted a couple of people working at Weymouth Mall who she thought we could trust to handle some businesses on our behalf. Several of them had witnessed the Undersiders save them and the people they cared about, so we were confident of their loyalty. Dad and I were also working out a way for the Undersiders to contact the Dockworkers Association to hire them for jobs. I had Grue working on that- he had less of an intimidating reputation than me, and I was still a little worried that some of the people there might recognise me as the Head of Hiring’s daughter.

For now, Weymouth Mall needed seeing to. People had got most of the partying out of their systems, and now they were thinking about the future.

“It’s kind of crazy that normal people are so eager to join us,” Vladimir noted.

“We are not just wandering marauders anymore,” Muramasa pointed out. “Now we are respected heroes, protectors. Also, we are the only faction left in town for people without powers or Asian heritage.”

“We’re also pretty good for people with powers,” Needler added. “We should try recruiting more. Holding this city with only the current Undersiders could be a challenge.”

I absently agreed, even as I marvelled that we were taking it as read that Brockton Bay was basically ours now. Yes, there was the government, the PRT, the Protectorate- but this was still the Undersiders’ city.

Weymouth Mall came into view shortly, Firecracker’s teleport eating up the distance. I could see the construction work had advanced since the last time I’d swung by- but there was something going on at the entrance…

I pulled my bow out of my quiver and nocked an arrow as I came to a stop on the edge of a nearby rooftop. There was a big hairy monster prowling around outside the front of Weymouth Mall- a mouth full of sharp teeth, and a coat of dirty brown fur, with a streak of bright red hair sticking up all the way down his spine. He looked up as he heard my teleport and bared his teeth.

I flicked my helmet open. “Animos, what the fuck are you doing?” I shouted down, feeling dread coil in my stomach.

Animos snarled and folded into himself- fur became leather and denim, and the fang-faced maw became a mask of a snarling beast. The Butchers had made that for him, like they had made the masks of every other member of the Teeth.

“I’m here for the challenge,” Animos shouted back, spreading his arms wide. “You and me, until somebody dies.”

“Oh, you dumb motherfucker,” Dirty Rotter sighed.

I pulled in insects and scoured everywhere in range- the doors to Weymouth were locked, although that wouldn’t stop Animos for long if he wanted. I could see several people waiting inside, mostly members of the O’Daly clan armed with a few guns and other weapons. No signs of the other members of the Teeth, in the mall or in the streets. Bloodsight didn’t show anybody hanging around outside either- people tended to clear the streets when a cape fight was going down. Those that didn’t tended to get hurt.

“Is it just you?” I asked. I could already guess the answer.

“Just me,” Animos snarled. “The others didn’t have the balls- which just means I don’t have to worry about any of them trying to snag the mantle out from under me!”

“Animos, you don’t have to do this,” I tried, lowering the bow. “Spree’s dead, Vex is dead- I killed Jack Slash with my bare hands, man! You don’t want this fight! Just go, find something else to do- Boston’s full of assholes ripe for a beating, that’s why we loved it there!”

“You think that of me?!” Animos roared. “You think I’m as spineless as the rest of them? That I’m going to pass up on being the baddest thing around? No! This is happening! If the Teeth are too fucking scared to stick around and fight, then I’ll do it alone!”

I stared at him for a second. “Is this really what you want, or are you just doing it because you can’t think of anything else?”

“Get down here and fight me!” Animos howled.

“…You heard him,” Bearskin said.

“Wait just a damn minute!” Flinch shouted.

“It’s the way!” Butcher shouted back.

“He’s barely even one of the Teeth if the rest left him behind,” Stoneknapper pointed out.

“He’s still Teeth enough to know how it’s done,” Firecracker said hollowly.

“He’s not going to stop,” Quarrel said simply. “One way or another, you gotta put an end to this.”

I ground my teeth together, but I couldn’t deny it. Animos would either run off and come back when I wasn’t expecting it, or try to attack the people inside the mall and force the issue.

The Undersiders were spread out- Grue and Tattletale were handling business, with Imp at least nominally under their supervision; Whirlygig and Ironclad were clearing rubble downtown, and Cerberus was tending to her dog shelter. I could call in New Wave or the Protectorate, but they wouldn’t get here fast enough for me to avoid fighting Animos myself.

I called them anyway, with the headset built into my helmet. “Animos is outside the Weymouth Mall, challenging me to fight him. Tell the Protectorate to send somebody.” I hung up before the poor operator on the other end could say anything.

I checked all my weapons in their various holsters while I gathered up as many insects as I could, then teleported down, about twenty feet behind Animos. He spun around to face me with a snarl.

“Last chance to back out,” I said. “You can find something else to do. Something else to be. Being stuck with me and all the rest isn’t going to be any fun for you.”

“She’s telling the truth,” Anchorage said, my bugs relaying her words as I formed them into human shapes. “Being stuck inside somebody else’s head, when you don’t get to make any decisions- it’s not good. I sure as fuck wasn’t laughing when I was Butcher.”

“Come on, Animos, you’re smarter than this,” Vladimir insisted. “I mean, do you really think you can beat Elpis? The fucking Siberian and Jack Slash couldn’t manage it, Kaiser and his last goons couldn’t manage it!”

“They weren’t me,” Animos growled, dropping to all fours as his body swelled with muscle and fur. His snarling beast mask became his snarling beast face, and his hands became paws with wicked claws.

Tactical sighed. “Well, if you want to run dick-first to your own death, I suppose there’s no helping you.”

“Do you need a count?” I asked Animos.

Bloodsight let me see the muscles bunching under his skin, and silk tripwires laid out on the ground let me feel his paws shift. When he leapt with a scream, I was already teleporting back to the perch I’d arrived at, drawing and loosing a long steel arrow.

Animos threw himself into a side-roll and tumble as soon as I disappeared, so the arrow missed his back paw by an inch. Insects poured onto him from every angle, stinging and biting, wrapping silk lines around him. He turned and screamed, his nullification power rippling through the air. It only went so far though- nowhere close to me. And having his mouth open let me cram flies down it.

“You didn’t have to do this,” I said through my bugs as Animos threw himself at the front of a building, claws sinking into the brickwork. “I would have let you leave alive. I didn’t want to kill you. I still don’t.”

Animos clawed his way up the building, coughing up bugs as he went. When he reached the top he spun around, looking for me, before spotting the gleam of my armour through the clouds of bugs. He roared and bounded forward, clearing the space above the road to the next building, and the next and the next, gaining speed. I sent more insects after him, throwing silk lines to tangle him, but he kept coming, screaming again right as he clamped his jaws around my armour.

“I honestly didn’t think you’d be that stupid,” I said, loosing another arrow from three buildings over. It hit Animos in his front paw, nailing him to the roof. He screamed, but this time in pain, letting my empty armour drop. I still had the undersuit and the bow, plus a few hold-out knives. Even that was overkill for this.

“I told you that the quick-release systems would come in handy,” Tock Tick said as I fired another arrow. This one hit Animos in a back paw, and he toppled onto his side, screeching in pain.

I teleported back to the roof and grabbed Animos by his mohawk so he couldn’t turn his head to scream at me. Needler’s power guided me to the jumbled-up mess of organs in his Changer form, and I started slamming punches into his kidneys.

“Stop hitting yourself! Stop hitting yourself! Stop hitting yourself!” Dirty Rotter chanted as Animos’s form wavered and collapsed back to human. The arrows fell out, leaving bloody wounds in his hand and foot.

“You’re the one hitting me!” Animos wailed pitifully.

“No Animos, you brought this on yourself,” Needler hissed. I wrapped an arm around his neck and squeezed. Animos struggled still, clawing at my face with his good hand, but he couldn’t do a damn thing to me. I was stronger and tougher, and I had him in a hold he couldn’t break. If he tried to change to get out, I could just hit him with pain and rage.

“Well, looks like this is it,” Butcher said. “Probably the last duel we’ll ever have, but at least the kid’s finally getting her feet wet.” He sounded very pleased with himself.

“Like killing Jack Slash and beating Kaiser wasn’t enough?” Nemean demanded.

Animos didn’t let up, twisting his wrist to try and stick a thumb in my eye. I just turned my head to the side and kept squeezing, feeling his efforts start to falter. This close, I could hear his heartbeat, and I wasn’t sure how it was going to sound when it gave out.

“Just keep going,” Bearskin said. “He’ll stop soon.”

I didn’t want to be the person who did death challenges. I didn’t want to choke a man to death because he was too dumb to surrender. I didn’t want to do this stupid fucking tradition.

“Taylor, you don’t have to!” Flinch yelled. “Why do you have to do what the Butchers want?”

Because…

I didn’t know. Why the hell was I doing this?

Animos’s arms dropped, his legs gave out, and his eyes rolled up in their sockets. I dropped him, and he fell forward with a gasp. I stood over him for a moment, before I shook off the shock and knelt to start tying his wrists and ankles together.

“What the hell are you doing?” Butcher demanded.

“Better question is, what was I thinking?” I said, pulling a knot tight. “Since when do I do things the Teeth way? I named myself for hope - why do I have to indulge Animos trying to commit suicide?”

“Because you’re the Butcher! We’re the Butcher! Now fucking finish him!”

“This isn’t a democracy,” I said, finishing the restraints and picking Animos up by his belt. “I don’t have to listen to you.” The thought was embarrassingly obvious and wonderfully refreshing. I’d been letting the Butchers have more and more of a say in how I did things- but I was still a hero, and I didn’t have to compromise on it.

“You little-!”

I shoved Butcher into the dark, nice and deep, then fired my grappler into the roof and rappelled down to the ground with Animos held like a carpet bag.

“Soooooo…” Stoneknapper said after a long moment of awkward silence, “What’re you going to do with him now?”

“I’ll let the PRT take him to prison. Maybe he’ll go to the Birdcage, I don’t know. He lost- and now he has to live with it. He doesn’t get to make me be worse for him.”

“That almost sounds worse than just killing him,” Muramasa said.

“Glad you approve.”

 

 

Holding cells, PRT Headquarters

Animos was pacing his cell like a caged animal when I arrived to talk to him, fresh off the debrief with Director Piggot. If I were pettier, I might have pointed it out to him. As it was, I’d spent the last hour simultaneously explaining things to Piggot while also shouting down the few Butchers who’d still wanted me to embrace their tradition and kill Animos, and I just didn’t have the energy.

Instead, I folded my arms and looked at him. “They’re sending you to the Birdcage, Laurence.”

Animos threw himself against the reinforced glass door. “I’ll fucking rip you apart!”

“No you won’t. And what exactly was the plan if you did? Track down the rest of the Teeth when they left you behind? Start something new all by yourself?”

“I’d have 16 sets of powers to figure it out!” Animos roared, hammering at the glass with his fists.

“If you won. I don’t think you really believed you’d be able to do it.” I leaned against the wall, still looking at him. “You know I met a precog? She said she saw me at the end, when everything goes to hell. It’s entirely possible that I can’t die until then.”

Animos glared at me, a vein throbbing in his forehead, but I could see him wavering, even if he’d never admit it.

“Look, you lost. I don’t know if you really wanted me to kill you, but it’s not happening. Take my advice and try not to piss people off too badly when you get to the Cage. The leaders seemed fairly reasonable- you could get comfortable.”

Animos took his fists away from the glass, and for a moment I thought I’d got through to him. Then he slammed his palms against the glass, fingers curling like he was trying to claw through it. His forehead pressed up against the glass too, his breath fogging it up as he glared at me with bloodshot eyes.

“Fuck you.”

I sighed. “Alright, I tried. Anybody want to say something?”

“I think we’re done here,” Quarrel said simply. The other Butchers agreed with a variety of grunts and hums.

I turned and walked away, Animos howling after me.

 

 

Friday 17th June, The Lair, The Docks

“Okay, so we’ve managed to slip pretty far into ABB territory with only token signs of preparation,” Lisa said. “No mines, no checkpoints, no patrols.”

I looked at the map spread out over the kitchen table, strewn with figurines to represent important features. There was almost nothing for ABB territory, and that was more worrying than if there’d been literal tons of ordinance.

“Do you think it’s a bluff?” Dad said, peering at the map. “Make things seem easy to lull you into a false sense of security?”

“That’s what I assumed,” Lisa admitted. “But we got halfway to the centre, and there were only token signs. There’s ABB members roaming around, but it’s directionless, like they’re waiting for orders. I got Aisha to plant a few cameras, and nothing’s shown up.”

I nodded absently while I checked the map again. I’d already got the details from Brian and Aisha when they came back from scouting, and they’d gone back to Brian’s apartment. They’d managed to avoid flood damage or looting, and they wanted to kick back in their own place, which was fair. Isabella had gone with them, which Brian had agreed to with an awkward smile while Aisha made vomiting noises in the background.

“That’s siblings for you,” Anchorage said simply.

Tarquin was back at his own house too- apparently he and his parents were going to make an effort to talk things out and discuss his future. We all wished him luck with that.

That left me, Dad and Lisa to order pizzas and figure out a plan of attack for the ABB. Probably the PRT was making their own plan too, but we’d see whose was better when the time came.

“I could tinker up some little drones to check for traps,” I said, taking a sip of my soda.

“What, like bomb disposal robots?” Dad asked.

“Maybe. I was thinking something cheap to set off any mines for us, but something for disarming the bombs without getting close would be smart.”

Lisa scribbled on her notepad. “Bomb disposal robots and sacrificial robots, check. We could also try using Grue’s darkness to shield the bombs from a detonation signal.”

“Worth a go, but we don’t know what Bakuda uses to detonate them. For all we know it could be micro gravity pulses. Or they could be on timers, or set to detonate if they stop receiving a signal.”

“This is going to be a really fucking annoying job, isn’t it?” Firecracker complained.

“Probably,” I admitted.

“Couldn’t the other heroes just send some fliers over to find Bakuda’s workshop and demolish it? I don’t think she’s got an anti-aircraft gun in stock,” Dad pointed.

I nodded. “Honestly, that’s probably how we’re going to do it, but we’ll still need to disarm or remove the bombs once Bakuda’s gone. Wouldn’t surprise me if she set something off just to punish us for arresting her.”

“She’s definitely got the personality for it,” Lisa agreed.

I grabbed another slice of pizza and bit into it. There were so many toppings on it that I could barely see the cheese. Bliss.

“Personally, I’m voting for the drones to clear the bombs,” Dad said. “Actually, you could just toss rocks- or use a long stick.”

“Actually, we could just set off the bombs by shooting them,” Tactical said.

“I vote for that one!” Quarrel shouted.

“Hit the road, Jack, and don’t you come back no more, no more-”

“Classic,” Tock Tick said as I picked my phone up.

“You know, at some point we’re going to get sick of that as our ringtone,” I commented.

“Yes, but not yet,” Vladimir said. “More importantly, why is Brian calling now?”

I tapped Accept and put him on speaker. “Hey Brian, what’s up-”

“Boss, turn on the news, Channel Three. Bakuda sent a message.”

I snatched up the remote and turned the TV on, quickly flicking through the channels. Bakuda appeared on screen in full costume, standing in some dark space that might have been a basement.

“-to panic. As much as I enjoy scaring the piss out of the general populace, this actually isn’t meant to be threatening. Although if you want to hold your loved ones close and pray to your god, go right ahead. But that’s not what I’m here to talk about,” Bakuda rasped. She set one hand on her hip and pointed at the ceiling dramatically.

“I’m here to announce that I’m sick and tired of Brockton Bay. Truthfully, I only came here because Lung made me an offer, and now that he’s trapped in that time bubble, he’s out of the equation. Yes, it was fun firing bombs at the Nazis and watching the heroes run around to clean up after me, but the shine’s worn off.

“Not to mention that this whole city’s got Butcher stink all over it. People are never going to stop going on about how Jack Slash died here, and I don’t want to settle for a place so second-hand. Sure, it’s also the city where my bombs helped kill Crawler, Siberian, and Bonesaw, but,” she shrugged, folding her arms, “I think I can top that.”

“That can’t be good,” Dirty Rotter said.

“So I give your city back to you! You can all unclench your sphincters, secure in the knowledge that you’re now beneath my notice. Pay attention to the news though- you’ll be hearing from me soon.

“Oh,” she leaned in close to the camera, red lenses gleaming, “And for anyone close to the Boat Graveyard, you might wanna cover your ears. I put a lot of my spare bombs in there, and they’re going to go off when this message ends. Bye!”

I formed my empty soda can into a makeshift mask and slapped it on as I teleported onto the roof, orienting myself towards the Boat Graveyard. I could just about make out some of the hulls in the moonlight, a couple of miles away.

“I don’t see-”

Needler stopped as the first explosion went off, sending a fireball shooting up into the sky. More followed, echoing across the entire city like thunder. I saw the rusting hulks torn apart by sheer force, melted by heat, transmuted into liquids that burned and solids that gleamed in the fires.

Six pillars of fire shot up into the air from the inferno, forming into massive letters facing into the city- BAKUDA. They hung in the air for a long moment, before dissolving into nothing, leaving the Boat Graveyard burning. I could already hear sirens.

“Well,” Nemean said as I stared at the chaos, “That’s one way to make an exit.”

Chapter 141: 14.6

Chapter Notes

See the end of the chapter for notes

Sunday 19th June, Downtown

From this rooftop, I could see a pretty good chunk of the city, particularly the Docks and the Boardwalk. Work was already getting started there- Bakuda’s bombs had torn up the Boat Graveyard in all manner of ways. Some ships had been broken in half, some had been crushed into dense blocks, some had been disintegrated into metal powder, and some had been transmuted into various substances. There was one that had been turned into salt and simply dissolved into the sea.

There were more than had been turned into crystals, or metals. There was a huge chunk of graphite at one end of the Graveyard, and another chunk had sprouted metal trees. The PRT was very interested in getting samples of all of it- Armsmaster thought some of the exotic materials could be used for tinkering.

I wished I could be down there, with a couple of Tinkertech cutters, carving the ships into pieces so they could finally be cleared out and Brockton Bay could become a shipping hub again. Some of the Wards were down there, and some of the Protectorate, and Ironclad, who’d wanted to salvage some metal for his armour.

But I was up here on this random rooftop, cape flapping in the wind, because I had a conversation to deal with.

I’d arrived early, so it took about 20 minutes of waiting before I spotted what I was looking for. Multiple figures in white were flying towards the rooftop. Lady Photon was flying point, Laserdream and Shielder flanking her, and Glory Girl was bringing up the rear, carrying her Flashbang by the armpits, who was carrying Brandish’s orange sphere form in his hands.

There was also an enormous bird made of silk and leather, with Parian perched on its back in her little white dress. Her mask and wig were gone, letting her dark curls flow down her shoulders, a tiara perched on top of her head. A needle and thread symbol in silver was embroidered across her front.

“I didn’t know she could make her puppets fly,” Tactical said, impressed. “She’s a lot stronger than she let herself be.”

“I guess pulling her mask off made her grow some backbone,” Anchorage said.

New Wave landed on the rooftop, first the Pelhams, then the Dallons, and then they all made space for Parian to awkwardly land her massive construct with a surprisingly heavy thud. While Flashbang let Brandish go to return to human form, Laserdream created a staircase of forcefields for Parian to step down from.

Vladimir chuckled. “It’s like Gone With The Wind.”

I kept my hands by my sides and away from my weapons as New Wave sorted themselves, and I caught looks of uncertainty from some of them. Probably they were thinking that even with the combination of multiple veteran heroes, I could still take them.

“Hell yes you can,” Quarrel snorted.

I carefully reached up to my helmet, undoing the latches under my chin and pulling it free of the neck plates. Then I tugged the silk cowl off as well, hanging both from my belt, and pulled my glasses out of a compartment. “Good morning,” I said as they came into focus again.

Their reactions were actually kind of funny. Brandish’s eyes went wide, Flashbang jerked with surprise, Lady Photon’s jaw dropped open. Shielder clapped a hand over his mouth, and Laserdream barked a laugh. Parian brought a gloved hand to her lips in ladylike shock.

“God, I thought that name was familiar,” Laserdream laughed. “Holy shit.”

It took me a second. “Wait, you forget who I was?”

Laserdream snorted. “Well, a fucking Endbringer hit the city right after the party, so yeah, I had other stuff on my mind.”

“Okay, fair enough,” I conceded.

“Wait, what about what party?” Brandish asked, confused.

“She’s Amy’s friend from that party we went to right before Leviathan,” Glory Girl said flatly. I saw her fists clench for a moment before uncurling.

“Hold on a moment,” Parian interrupted, waving her hands about. “How old are you?”

“16,” I said. I didn’t tell them that was today- they didn’t need to know.

“16?!” Parian parroted, clutching at her hair.

“I thought you were much older,” Flashbang admitted.

I shrugged. “It’s all the memories and experience from the Butchers. Plus, you know what cape life is like. You grow up quickly.”

“That’s true, I suppose,” Lady Photon stepped forward, folding her arms. “So. You wanted us to clear the air, answer our questions. To start, how exactly did you inherit from Butcher XIV?”

“I lashed out by accident when the Teeth were coming close to my old school. I didn’t mean to kill her, but,” I gestured to myself, “Here I am. I don’t know how exactly my power let me stay sane, but Glaistig Uaine called my power Queen Administrator, said it was noble. That might have something to do with it.”

Glory Girl perked up a bit. “Did she name any other powers, or say anything about how they worked?”

“I’d have thought the Protectorate would have shared things with them,” Stoneknapper said.

“Maybe they were getting around to it,” Flinch suggested.

“She called Butcher the First of Torturers, and she called Flinch a Sentinel. Tock Tick is Crafter of Gears. Eidolon is the High Priest, Jack Slash was the Herald, and she called herself the Keeper of the Dead. She also said they were divided into two courts, and one court was messed up. Eidolon was one, head of the stillborn faerie, whatever the hell that means. She also said that his power was unusually strong, more than it was supposed to be.”

Glory Girl whistled. “Wow. Sounds crazy, but there’s probably a lot of information in there. And she could really hear the Butchers?”

“Yep. That was a hell of a shock.”

“What about Amy?” Brandish broke in. “When did she find out about you?”

Amy had called me after Bakuda’s exit, feeling well enough for a phone call, and we’d discussed what to tell her family in her absence. Still, I hesitated for a moment. “It was after we drove the Teeth out of town. She treated me in the hospital and noticed some power effects in my body. I managed to convince her to keep quiet about it.”

“…that was back in February,” Glory Girl said numbly. “Why didn’t she tell us?” It sounded more like she meant to say, “Why didn’t she tell me?”

“What would you have done?” I asked, spreading my hands. “Would you have given me a chance? Told the PRT? Tackled me when I wasn’t expecting it? It took a long time for Amy to really trust me, and it took a long time for everyone else to trust me. Let’s face it, I had to fight Leviathan and kill Jack Slash before people really started believing in me.”

Glory Girl winced, and I saw Flashbang grimace. Brandish’s frown softened a fraction.

“I suppose that’s fair,” Lady Photon grudgingly admitted. “If we’d found out earlier, we might have jumped the gun.”

“Imagine that fight,” Butcher muttered. I ignored him.

“Amy said that was part of her thinking at first. She didn’t want you fighting me and getting hurt, or other villains coming to Brockton to get to me.”

“How is Amy?” Shielder asked quietly.

“She’s getting better,” I promised. “She’s still a little fragile, but she said she should be ready to talk in a couple of days. Right now she’s getting some more therapy, sorting some things out.”

“Can you tell her we miss her?” Brandish asked softly.

“Of course.”

After a moment, Lady Photon spoke up. “So what are your plans going forward?”

“I’ve got the bounty money from the Nine, and there’s basically no villains left in town. We have a golden opportunity to clean Brockton Bay up and ready ourselves for whatever new group tries to move in. Beyond that, I’m thinking we expand.”

“What do you mean by that?”

“I mean that we can work our way along the east coast. Probably some of the Protectorate will get reassigned, but there’d still be enough heroes here to hold the line while others head out to help in other cities. A partnership between the Undersiders and New Wave could allow us to field a combined strike team, and start recruiting other independents or coordinating with existing teams. An alliance of heroes, properly coordinated, really pushing back against crime and villains.”

“That’s… ambitious,” Lady Photon admitted. “You really think it’s possible?”

“It has to be. We all know something’s coming. We need to work together- not just here, but everywhere- if we’re going to stop it.”

I saw the flicker across their faces, the memory of the prediction. Three years until the end of the world.

“I’m in.”

“Victoria,” Brandish began.

“Mom, you know we have to. It’s not like New Wave is going to survive if we don’t find something to do. And this is what we’ve always wanted- pushing forward, making a difference.” Glory Girl turned to me with determination in her eyes, hovering inches off the ground. “I’m in.”

“Same here,” Laserdream said, stepping forward.

“I agree with the kids,” Flashbang spoke up. “This is what we do.”

Brandish and Lady Photon traded a complicated look, before Brandish nodded slightly. Lady Photon sighed. “We’ll need to discuss it a little more, but it seems like the answer’s yes. Parian? Anything to add?”

Parian gripped one dainty hand in the other. “I still need to protect my family, and I don’t have a lot of experience in fighting yet. But I agree. This is the right thing to do.”

“If any of you need help, just reach out,” I promised.

 

 

The Lair, The Docks

Dad and the rest of the Undersiders were all assembled in the living room when I teleported into the booth. Through my bugs, I could see a few bags tucked away behind chairs, and the kitchen table was set for a meal. There was also a big covered dish on the coffee table for some reason, the lid slightly askew.

“Are we missing something?” Firecracker asked.

“I don’t think so,” I said, stepping out of the booth and starting to strip my armour off. “Hey guys, what’s-”

“SURPRISE!”

The Undersiders all jumped to their feet, Lisa yanking on a cord hanging by the wall. A banner unfurled from the ceiling, bearing the words HAPPY BIRTHDAY!

“Happy sweet sixteen, Taylor!” Lisa crowed.

Rotter cackled. “Hahahaha, oh my fuck! You forgot your own birthday!”

“Shut up,” I grumbled, caught halfway dressed with one boot flopping loose. I kicked it off to the side, breaking into a smile. “I can’t believe you guys managed to do this without me finding out!”

“It wasn’t easy,” Dad admitted with a chuckle, taking the lid off the dish. A big chocolate cake lay inside, candles already lit. Judging from the way the wax had melted, they’d lit it a while ago.

“I still can’t believe you’re just sixteen,” Isabella said with a grin. “Barely old enough to drive.”

“Which reminds me,” Dad said, pulling a card from his pocket, “This is for you.”

The card had balloons on it, and written inside was the message “Happy Birthday Taylor. I’m so proud of you. Love, Dad.” And  folded inside was a coupon- driving lessons booked at a test centre in town.

“I know you probably don’t need them, but this way you can make it official,” Dad  said with a shrug.

I hugged him at once. “Thanks Dad.” I felt my eyes grow hot, and blinked away a couple of tears before anyone could see.

“Hey, we’re going in the wrong order,” T broke in, holding up the dish. “First thing to do is blow out the candles!”

“Make a wish,” Lisa said with a grin.

I laughed and let Dad go to lean over the cake. One big breath extinguished them all and got me a round of applause.

“So what’d you wish for?” Brian asked.

“You know I can’t tell anyone,” I protested teasingly.

“Yeah, Brian,” Isabella said, nudging him in the side. “Basic birthday wish rules, duh.”

“Yeah, Brian, god,” Aisha echoed with a grin.

“This is from me,” Rachel said, pulling an awkwardly wrapped box out of one of the bags and holding it out. “Lisa helped.”

“Thanks,” I said, gently taking it and popping a claw to cut the tape.

Rachel’s gift turned out to be a couple of CDs of new bands I’d been meaning to check out. Isabella got me some comic books, and a little figurine of Elpis that some artist was apparently selling down on the Boardwalk.

“Oh, that’s fantastic,” Tock Tick grinned as I held up the little armoured figure.

Brian got me a big box of chocolates, Aisha got me a huge bag of candy that looked like a couple of pieces had already been eaten. Tarquin’s gift was a retro video game system.

“I figured the Butchers might have some nostalgia,” he explained as I jiggled the joystick experimentally. “It’s got Space Invaders, Tetris, Pac-Man, Dig-Dug, Galaga…”

“How old does he think we are?” Bearskin wondered, aghast.

“I’m willing to try them,” Needler said.

Lisa gave me a big bag of gourmet coffee beans, a taster box of different types of tea, and a cheap mug that said, “World’s Best Boss.” I couldn’t help but laugh.

Dad had dug up all his old records for me to go through, plus an old jacket of Mom’s from when they met in college; it was just about the right size for me. I traced a finger over the patches that said stuff like Girl Power, or had a burning bra in the centre.

My last couple of birthdays had not been fun. Mom’s death, Emma’s bullying, no friends whatsoever. Just a couple of presents from Dad and some hurtful remark from the bullies.

“Thank you so much,” I said sincerely. “This means a lot to me.”

“Any time,” Lisa said warmly.

Aisha clapped her hands. “Alright, let’s cut the damn cake!”

“Dibs on the second slice!” Isabella called.

“Cool, then I get first slice,” Aisha said.

“Obviously Taylor gets the first slice,” T pointed out with an eyeroll.

“I call third slice,” Lisa said with a grin.

“What? Hey-”

“Fourth slice,” Brian said, smirking at his sister.

“I’ll have the next one,” Rachel said with an amused look.

Aisha folded her arms and pouted. “You guys suck.”

 

 

Tuesday 21st June, Weymouth Mall

“Okay, Stacey, seriously, I do need to breath,” I said, patting her shoulder.

Stacey finally let me go, looking me up and down. “I’m so glad you’re okay,” she gushed. “I barely heard anything from you!”

I winced. “Yeah, I’m sorry. Everything was so nuts. Are you guys alright?”

“Hanging in there,” Callum said, scratching his head. “We went to stay with our aunt for a while. Dad was talking about selling the house, but now that everything’s over, we’re back here.”

“It was nice to see Aunt Amaya again,” Ezran piped up from next to Callum. He was dark-skinned and bright-eyed, holding a Rubik’s Cube in his hands. “Her girlfriend’s cool too.”

“Grandma and I made it through,” Frankie said. “The house is a mess though. Right now there’s just cardboard on the windows.”

“Yeah, Bait’s tank is the only big of glass we’ve got left,” Callum said.

“There’s a list around here somewhere where you can put your name down for glass repairs,” Tarquin said. “It’s pretty long, but it might be faster than buying everything new.”

“Seriously? I’ve got to get our name on that,” Stacey said, gesturing to herself.

“Come on, let’s sit down and get something to eat,” I said, gesturing to the tables in the food court.

Even with repairs going at an incredible pace, there were still plenty of people staying at Weymouth Mall, and more dropping by to shop and eat at one of the first places that had got all the glass reinstalled and utilities working again. It took us a good five minutes to grab a table just as another group was leaving, and even then Ezran had to sit in Callum’s lap, though Callum took it without complaint.

“It’s crazy, isn’t it?” Frankie said, lacing her fingers together. “Everything that’s happened…”

“I was really scared when the sirens went off,” Ezran admitted in a small voice. “It felt like the end of the world.”

Callum patted him on the shoulder. “I know, bud. I was scared too.”

“I was freaking out too,” I admitted.

“Same,” Tarquin said.

“I swear I almost peed myself,” Stacey confessed.

“The funny thing is, I fell asleep in the shelter,” Ezran admitted. “I didn’t think I could, but I just woke up in the morning, and talked to this other boy who’d brought his pet lizard with him, and then we went back to the house.”

“Yeah, Echo the Gecko,” Callum said with a smile.

“That’s adorable,” Nemean said.

“Life goes on, no matter what happens,” T said with a shrug.

“So what’ve you guys been doing?” Callum asked.

“I helped out a bit around here,” T said with a wave of his hand. “Mostly moving stuff around.”

“Yeah, me too. And helping Dad a bit with the Dockworkers. They just landed a salvage contract for part of the Graveyard.”

“Cool,” Stacey said. “Did you guys ever meet the Undersiders?”

Tarquin and I traded glances. “Nah, we’re not that important,” I said with a laugh.

“Yeah, they’re too busy cracking heads and kissing babies or whatever heroes do,” T agreed.

“Well, if you do, get me Elpis’s autograph,” Frankie said.

“What, you’re going to stick it on your wall?” I asked

“No dude, eBay.”

Muramasa burst out laughing. “Excellent answer!”

“Fair enough,” I said with a shake of my head.

Callum pursed his lips for a moment. “Uh… So has anybody heard from Amy?” he asked carefully?”

I didn’t miss how everyone turned to me, even Ezran.

“She’s back with the PRT. Seeing a therapist, getting herself sorted out. She’s doing alright.”

“That’s good,” Stacey said softly.

“Let her know we’re thinking of her, yeah?” Frankie said.

“Of course.”

“Soooo,” Tarquin said, blatantly changing the subject, “What did people think of the mayoral debate?”

Eventually we took it in turns to get food, the others holding their seats for them. We shovelled down junk food, Ezran determinedly working away at a slice of pizza the size of his face, while we talking about Christner coming out ahead in the polls, the rumours of parts of the Boat Graveyard getting turned into gold and diamonds, the news about Boston having problems with Blasto’s creatures.

It filled a place in me I’d almost forgotten about- friendship without the weight of heroic responsibility. I was just Taylor Hebert here- as much as I could be anywhere.

“This is nice,” Anchorage said as I finished off my burger.

“Yeah,” I agreed as Callum described to Frankie with exaggerated gestures the pictures of Blasto’s creations he’d seen online. It sounded like Boston’s resident Bio-Tinker was branching out from humanoid homunculi into cruder, more vicious plant-animal things.

“Maybe that could be our first project when we start branching out,” Tactical suggested.

 

 

Thursday 29th June, The Lair, The Docks

“Boston’s calling for aid,” I announced to the rest of the team.

Lisa had made it so we could connect a laptop to the TV. I pulled up Blasto’s PHO page. “This asshole here is Blasto, leader of a group called Blastgerm. He’s what you’d call a wet Tinker, specialising in creating living organisms. That means he brews up minions using raw materials and uses them for muscle. He’s been in control of a decent chunk of south Boston for a couple of years now, mostly dealing weed. Wanted for second degree murder and mass property damage.” The picture was a zoomed-in distance shot of a man in a white labcoat, wearing a mask that looked like it was made out of living wood and moss.

“Sounds like a real charmer,” Isabella noted.

“He’s done some big stuff over the years; extra large creatures or large groups. His most famous was a thing called the Woad Giant back during the Boston Games.” I switched to a different page.

Tarquin whistled, Brian grimaced, Rachel frowned. “What the fuck is that?” she asked.

“That,” I said, “Is sixty feet of plant-animal hybrid standing in Boston’s bay. It mostly just stood around for a couple of days, but it scared the crap out of people. It’s what gave Blasto the reputation to claim territory and sit at the big table.”

“Sick,” Aisha said, leaning forward to get a better look.

“Still wish we could have fought that thing,” Stoneknapper grumbled from the glass box of bugs I’d set up as a speaker.

The mechanism on the front flicked around, flicking from ‘Stoneknapper’ to ‘Nemean’. “For the last time, I’m sorry we missed the Boston Games,” Nemean snapped.

“There’s theories that it had parahuman DNA mixed in,” Lisa chimed in. “It’s the only way something that size could have avoided collapsing under its own weight.”

“Right. There’s been talk of Blasto using DNA samples to give his later creations minor power effects as well- never anything resembling a proper clone, but still dangerous.”

Dad rubbed his chin. “So what’s happening now that Boston’s asking for reinforcements?”

“Thanks for asking. The answer is that Blasto seems to be making a push for territory, or maybe just lashing out.” I switched to a third page, a news site showing pictures of the aftermath of an attack by Blasto’s creations. “They’re popping up far from his usual territory, causing lots of chaos and disruption. The local heroes are just about keeping a lid on things, but they’re struggling- these creations seem like a new generation. Stronger, more intelligent.”

“And you want us to pitch in, help out,” Brian said.

“Pretty much. We’ve talked about expanding, building connections with other teams, other cities. Brockton’s still safe for now- we’re monitoring possible threats, and it’ll be weeks before any of them are ready to make a move. We can afford to leave Brockton Bay to the Protectorate or New Wave to look after, and start building our reputation.”

“Because beating the Nine wasn’t enough?” Tarquin asked sceptically.

“Reputation requires constant maintenance,” Vladimir broke in. “Most will keep your victories in mind, but there will always be some young upstarts who think the stories are exaggerated, that they can take you.”

“And you think smashing through a bunch of monsters will help with that?” Brian asked. “Actually, I retract my question, the answer’s obvious.”

“Precisely. So, hands up if you want to take a trip to Boston and smash a bunch of monsters, hands down if you want to stay here and keep an eye on things.”

Everyone but Dad put a hand up.

I grinned. “Fantastic. We’ll call up the Protectorate and New Wave to coordinate. I figure each group can send a couple of members and leave a few behind.”

 

 

Friday 30th June, PRT Headquarters

It took a lot of discussion before the three hero teams decided who would go to Boston and who would stay to protect Brockton Bay.

Lady Photon, Flashbang, Brandish and Glory Girl volunteered to go- the older heroes had helped out in the Boston Games and were familiar with the scene, while Glory Girl admitted she needed to blow off some steam. That left Laserdream, Shielder and Parian as the junior squad to keep an eye on things.

Armsmaster stepped forward to lead the Protectorate’s delegation. I’d half-expected him to stay put and help maintain the Protectorate’s authority, but he seemed to have something in mind. Miss Militia and Battery were going with him, while Dauntless and Gargoyle held the fort.

The Wards were stepping up too- Weld had started out in Boston, and was eager to head back and help his hometown. Gallant, Spitfire and Flechette were coming with him. Apparently Vista wanted to go, but her parents refused to give her permission, so she’d be staying behind with Clockblocker, Chariot and Aegis, who were recovering well from Cherish’s Master effect but still needed to be kept close for final observation.

I was going to Boston as the big gun, and Cerberus, Ironclad, Tattletale and Imp were coming with me. Grue wasn’t happy with his little sister leaving while he and Whirlygig stayed behind, but I pointed out that she might just sneak along anyway. Plus, I needed help to watch my back- Boston’s bad blood with the Butcher legacy was fresher than Brockton Bay’s, and having a friendly Stranger could help avoid problems. Dad wished me luck with a hug and a kiss, and I promised that I’d be home safe and sound.

We rode up to the PRT building bright and early on Cerberus’s dogs. The other heroes had arrived before us, assembled on the road next to several vans. Director Piggot was standing next to the extra truck we’d requested.

“Undersiders,” she said as we dismounted. “Thank you for coming.”

“We weren’t going to miss this,” I said, striding up to her. “Anything else we need to do before we head out?”

Piggot shook her head. “The Wards are saying their goodbyes, but that’s about it. I’ve got the troopers on alert for any problems, but the Think Tank confirmed that things should be quiet here.”

“That’s a relief.” I spotted Gallant having his armour fiddled with by Chariot, whose own suit looked rundown and worn compared to its usual gleam. A second later he had to back off as Glory Girl swooped down like a falcon and wrapped Gallant in a hug, much to his enjoyment and the amusement of his teammates. I saw Aegis and Clockblocker off on the sidelines, a little hesitant but standing tall.

“I’m glad to see the boys are recovering well,” Flinch said from the box I had tucked under one arm. Piggot glanced at it for a second before shrugging.

“We got one of the PRT’s best therapists in the shuffle, and Gallant helped detect any lingering effects. They should be fully cleared in a few more weeks.”

“Good.” I stepped a little closer and lowered my voice. “I talked with Mayor Christner about making a memorial for everyone we lost to the Nine- especially Triumph. Do you have any thoughts on that?”

Piggot worked her jaw for a second. “I would like to have something in Triumph’s memory. We’d have to be careful though- if we emphasise him too much, it might antagonise villains.”

“What villains?” Firecracker asked.

I tapped the box in agreement. “Bakuda’s skipped town, the Teeth have fled, and the Empire’s finished. All that’s left of them is Rune and- actually, what’s happening with Othala?”

“She’s responding to treatment, but the Empire’s defeat has apparently caused her considerable stress,” said Piggot unsympathetically. “The mass arrest of the Empire allowed us to find her civilian identity, so it’s essentially the end of the road for her. We’ve also determined Rune’s identity, but given that she’s escaped from prison before, we’re holding off on confronting her until we can develop countermeasures.”

“Reasonable.” I spotted what we’d been waiting for- the dogs were finally starting to shrink. “Looks like it’s almost time to set off.”

Piggot nodded. “Good hunting.”

Ironclad clambered into the spare truck and dumped the majority of his armour there, then climbed out again. There was a quick discussion of who would ride with who- Gallant quickly offered to sit with New Wave, while the rest of us were split between the other trucks.

Armsmaster and I would be in another truck, along with Ironclad, Flechette, and Cerberus. It meant that those of us with the metal body armour wouldn’t accidentally bump into Weld and get stuck- he was riding with Miss Militia, Battery, Tattletale, and against my better judgement, Imp.

I caught her by the arm as she stepped into the third trick. “Behave yourself.”

Imp gave me a look of wounded innocence that was completely ruined by her grinning devil mask. “Boss, when do I not behave myself?”

“Got your bullet?”

Imp sagged. “Yes, boss,” she groaned.

“Good. Did you use the bathroom?”

“What? No.”

“Well, go before we set off. It’s a long ride.”

Imp tossed her head in a way that implied she was rolling her eyes. “Yes, mom.” She hopped down and sauntered off towards the PRT lobby.

“You really are starting to sound like someone’s mummy,” Dirty Rotter sniggered.

“Fuck off,” I retorted, turning to help Cerberus coax her dogs into the truck and settle them down.

A few minutes later, everybody was loaded up, sat down, and belted in. Armsmaster knocked on the wall to the driver’s cab, and the trucks set off.

Quarrel started humming first- the other Butchers joined in, humming or singing the words, until I was tapping my foot to the tune.

“I’m shipping up to Boston, way-ey-oh, I’m shipping off, to find my wooden LEG!”

Chapter End Notes

So, full disclosure, I kind of missed Taylor's birthday. It's supposed to be the 12th, and I didn't realise I hadn't addressed that until after I'd alreayd posted the last chapter. Luckily, there's a mixup in canon where she says in court that her birthday's the 19th, so I'm going with that to technically still be accurate to the webserial. Hurrah!

Bringing in Callum's little brother Ezran is about as far as I'm going to take the Dragon Prince reference, but it is hilarious.

Anyhoo, roadtrip out of town to kick some ass. I hope people are ready for that!

If anyone has any tips or resources for writing about Boston, especially in Earth Bet, I'd be glad to hear it.

Chapter 142: Interlude 14.b

Chapter Notes

Shipping up to Boston, way-ay-oh!

This is another one of those big ideas that I had when I was putting New Boss together, so here's hoping it lands well.

See the end of the chapter for more notes

Friday 30th June, Downtown Boston

Ariel perched on her jetstick, observing the traffic below. All the trouble Blasto was stirring up had actually done what almost nothing else could and reduced traffic in Boston, if only because people were staying home to avoid the monsters.

An alert came up on her helmet’s visor, a change in the wind. She tweaked the jets on her flightpack and jetstick to compensate, holding steady as she waited.

There, at last- four trucks with diagonal purple stripes, green and white lights on top. The lights weren’t flashing, so no problems.

It struck Ariel as a little silly to be nervous. Here she was, a Ward with a suit packed with Tinkertech thrusters and a big stick, hovering a hundred feet in the air, and she was still feeling queasy watching four trucks make their way towards the PRT building.

She’d read the reports, seen the videos, celebrated Jack Slash’s death just like everybody else. Weld had called back a few times, letting them know what Elpis was really like, and Ariel believed him when he said that she wasn’t the Butcher; okay, technically she was the Butcher, but she wasn’t the thing at the head of the Teeth, a walking meatgrinder that randomly tore up the town when something set them off.

On the other hand, she’d crushed Burnscar’s skull and chopped Jack Slash into little pieces. Which, fair, they had it coming, but it was still pretty freaky.

The trucks came to a halt at a set of traffic lights. Ariel lowered herself a few feet in the air, clicking her radio on. “Ariel to Console, come in.”

“Console receiving, go ahead Ariel.”

“I’ve got eyes on the trucks from Brockton Bay, I’d say they’re about fifteen minutes out.” She checked her helmet’s GPS and added the location, then marked the trucks on her HUD to keep track of them.

“Thank you for checking in, Ariel. We’ll pass it on.”

Ariel shifted her grip on her jetstick and swung a leg back over it. Flying side-saddle looked cute, but it wasn’t the smart choice for serious movement. The smaller thrusters at the top of the handle increased to keep balance, and she gently eased herself forward as the trucks moved forward again. Her cloak and the brim of her pointy hat flapped in the wind as she slowly flew along, but they were both securely fastened.

An alert flashed up on her visor- the trucks were stopped at another set of lights. Ariel rolled her eyes- it had only been a couple of minutes since the last one. She came to a halt again, thrusters firing all over her suit to balance her. She dropped a little lower too- they weren’t too far from the PRT building now, and she preferred being closer to the ground in safe territory.

As she dropped down, something caught her eye. There were a bunch of people moving across the rooftops, jumping from building to building. She clicked her radio again. “Ariel to Console, I think I’ve spotted something. There’s people roof-running near my position, they’re-” She double-checked and swore, “They’re heading for the Brockton trucks!”

“We’re calling them now; hold position.”

Ariel could see things wrong with the people on the roofs now. Some of them had extra limbs, wings on their backs or four legs like a centaur. Some of their costumes looked more like parts of their bodies than clothes, cracked bark instead of skin, branches growing from their scalps.

“They’re Blasto’s creations,” Ariel reported. “Definitely. They’re almost at the trucks-”

One of the soldiers suddenly leapt- it propelled them fifty feet forward, off the roof and down onto the street, landing on the roof of a car. The metal caved in with the impact, and people on the street started screaming.

“They’re attacking!” Ariel tucked herself close to her jetstick and dove down, pulling up to skim over the roofs of cars as the creatures swarmed off the rooftops and onto the street. Civilians scattered in all directions; some locked their cars and hunkered down, while others abandoned them entirely.

The lead creature cackled madly and pointed a sharp finger at the truck, then flicked its hands. The fingers elongated into massive spindly things, tipped with black claws. Ariel signalled her tech’s offensive mode as the creature bent its knees to leap again-

An explosion of fire directly above it, and Elpis crashed down on the thing like an anvil. Unlike in those old cartoons, the creature didn’t shake it off- Elpis’s punch crashed into its head and knocked it to the ground. Without pause, Elpis turned and raised her left wrist, a fat barrel firing blasts of air at the creatures, while clouds of insects poured out of her armour and from under her cape. Ariel threw her jetstick around to come to a halt, pointed at the creatures.

The side of one truck disintegrated into powder, and Armsmaster leapt through, halberd at the ready. More capes poured out of the other trucks- Ariel spotted Weld running towards the creatures, and Flechette from New York hopping out of the hole Armsmaster had made, crossbow at the ready. One boy raced for the last truck and threw himself in through the doors.

Elpis drew a sword in one hand and an axe in the other. “Undersiders! Evac civilians first, then corral the villains! I’ll get their attention!”  She threw herself off the hood of the car, roaring.

“Ariel!” Weld shouted. “Get people out of here!”

Ariel hit the thrusters on her jetstick and shot forward, towards a man who’d fallen on his ass and was frantically scuttling backwards from a creature with pointed ears and a tail. She kicked the thing in the head as she swept past, firing her heel thruster for added damage, and came to a stop just next to the man.

“Take my hand,” she said, leaning sideways off her jetstick. He took it, and she flew up a foot, pulling him to his feet. “Get out of here, we’ll handle this,” she said, spinning around to get back to the fight.

On the bright side, the Blasto creatures weren’t lashing out at civilians like they often did. On the downside, that meant they were focused on the heroes with a lot more smarts than usual. The frontline fighters clashed with the initial wave while the long-range fighters wore them down with crossbow bolts and bullets, bolts of light and energy grenades.  A massive pile of metal flooded out of the last truck and arranged itself into a humanoid that threw itself against the monsters like an avalanche.

Armsmaster ducked a blow from a muscle-bound thing with fists wrapped in green forcefields and sliced its legs off at the knee. As it toppled over, he split it in half from groin to scalp and moved onto the next. Weld struck out with his arms changed into clubs, breaking bones and hammering flesh. There was a girl in a firefighter’s coat vomiting something like napalm that burned the creatures to ash.

Elpis was everywhere, teleporting into knots of enemies to break them up, blocking blows without looking, slicing creatures to pieces or caving their chests in with devastating punches. Insects buzzed around her, crawling up the creatures and getting in their faces.

Ariel flew up high to check- a flying girl in white and three big dog-lizard things were hauling civilians away, while a blonde woman was setting forcefields to fence the fight in. No more civilians in the danger zone- so time to join the fight. She steered herself over one particularly ugly creature and sent a specific command to her jetstick. The jetstick spun down, around, and up again as panels shifted and thrusters rotated- Ariel fell as the jetstick switched to what Reynard had called Malleus Maleficarum.

It had taken ages to find out what that meant, but once she did, she agreed that it was pretty cool to name her jetstick’s melee mode The Hammer Of Witches.

She hit the thrusters again just as the creature looked up in time to take a falling jet-propelled Tinkertech hammer to the face. Its skull caved in with a noise like mac and cheese, and Ariel pulled the hammer free as it toppled over, using her heel thrusters to land lightly.

Something whirred behind her, and she spun around to see another creature drop dead from the sword lodged in its head. Where had that-

“I think we got them all, everybody,” said a buzzing, rasping voice from every direction at once. Ariel jerked and almost activated her thrusters to fly off again. Did the insects just talk?

“You know, there was a door,” the blonde in purple said to Armsmaster, gesturing to the hole in the side of the truck.

“There were also a dozen biotinker creatures coming to kill us,” Armsmaster retorted, collapsing his halberd into a slim rod that he clipped to his back.

“Sometimes the only way out is through,” Elpis said, stepping over to the car she and the first creature had landed on. “Hey in there; I’m just going to fix your car, is that alright?”

There was a muffled reply from inside. Elpis nodded. “Okay then.” She set one gauntleted hand on the crumpled roof, and the metal popped back into shape at once.

Ariel shook herself and trotted over to Weld, jetstick slung onto her back. “Good to see you again, Weld.”

Weld turned his club arms back into hands and gave her his usual movie poster smile. “You too, Ariel. I just wish it wasn’t so messy.” He flicked a piece of green-brown gunk off his trousers.

Ariel nodded. “I know- Blasto’s things always splatter all over the place.” Out of the corner of her eye, she saw Elpis stride over to her sword and pull it free from the creature’s head, flicking bits of mess off it. She might have to thank her for the save later.

Weld frowned.  “The question is, how’d they know about this place? How did they know we’d be here, now?”

“I don’t know,” Ariel admitted, gripping her jetstick tight, “But I don’t think we’re going to like the answer.

 

 

Boston PRT Main Headquarters

Director Kamil Armstrong kept his back straight as the trucks reversed into the secure loading bay, one with a gaping hole in the side; Ariel drifted in after them on her jetstick, sliding past to land and join the rest of the Wards. Three massive dog creatures, one with a girl in an armoured coat riding atop, padded in after the trucks, followed by a massive figure made of miscellaneous metal objects. Cerberus and Ironclad, two of the Undersiders.

“Woah,” somebody said.

The engines turned off, the drivers came out and gave the necessary security codes, and the trucks were opened one by one. The Protectorate and Wards who’d gathered to greet the volunteers tensed up in various ways.

New Wave came out of the first truck- Lady Photon, Brandish and Flashbang were as he remembered, if a little older, and Glory Girl was a new face to him. They’d all just come from an ambush, but they all seemed fresh and alert despite that. Gallant was with them, standing obviously close to Glory Girl as she drifted to the ground. A couple of Boston’s heroes stepped forward to greet them, some having worked with them before. Bastion noticeably hung back- he’d managed to hang onto his position despite his recent scandal, but his transfer to another department was a certainty at this point.

The second truck opened, and a girl in a black jumpsuit and grey demon mask burst out. “Damn, and I thought the traffic back home was bad,” she declared, stretching extravagantly. That would be Imp, the Undersiders’ Stranger. They had protocols in place for her.

“That joke wasn’t funny the first time,” said a girl in a firefighter’s coat and helmet, nozzles peaking out of her sleeves- Spitfire, another of Piggot’s Wards. Miss Militia and Battery came out after the girls with more professionalism, then a blonde girl in a purple-black jumpsuit and goggles- Tattletale, the Undersider’s Thinker.

“Hi,” said Hunch, waving from the Wards group. “You’re Tattletale, right?”

“I am,” Tattletale confirmed. “And you must be Hunch, right? Boston’s precog?”

“Yup,” Hunch said with a grin.

Off to the side, Cerberus slid down from her dog, patting each beast in turn, while Ironclad settled into a more relaxed stance.

Last from the truck was Weld, the suspension rocking as he stepped out- the sight of him brought a smile to Armstrong’s face. Favouritism be damned, Weld was like the son he’d never had, ever since the boy had been found in Boston years ago. He’d watched him grow from a lost little boy into a strong young man, and it lifted his heart to see Weld come home safely.

“Good to have you back, Weld” Armstrong said as Weld approached.

“Good to be back, Director,” Weld replied with a winning smile. Armstrong clapped him on the shoulder before looking towards the third and final truck- the hole was facing away from them, but everyone knew who was in there.

The doors swung open, revealing several recognisable figures. Armstrong recognised Flechette from New York thanks to some training exercises their Wards teams had done together- smart girl, driven. Armsmaster followed them out, his signature halberd folded up on his back, barely scuffed from their fight.

And finally, Elpis. Armstrong made note of which of the heroes reacted as the girl stepped out of the truck in her graphite-grey armour. Stampede’s outline flickered for a second, while Coatl shifted from foot to foot. Briar Patch looked tense, but she didn’t have any thorns out; Frostfern had mist coming off her fingers though, and Leeward had his shoulders squared. Flipper ducked behind Weld as Elpis stepped heavily down from the truck and looked around, helmet sliding open to reveal a pale jaw with thin lips. If she had any emotions about walking into the midst of Boston’s heroes, she didn’t show it.

It was unfair, Armstrong knew. Elpis had proven herself as an upstanding hero over and over, fighting the villains of Brockton Bay, facing Leviathan, evil clones, the Slaughterhouse Nine, and running a refugee shelter of all things. Still, the legacy of the Butcher loomed large in Boston’s memory. At least he’d never personally encountered any of her predecessors, which made it easier to see her as she was.

Easier, but not effortless. The hint of fangs on her upper teeth and the weapons all over her body certainly didn’t help.

A dozen butterflies came out from under her cape and circled around her, colourful wings flashing in the air. It didn’t break the tension exactly, but it certainly made people pause as the Undersiders moved to flank their leader.

“Welcome to Boston, PRT Department 24,” Armstrong began. “For those of you who don’t know me, I’m Director Armstrong, head of the local PRT. I’m hoping we can work together in a coordinated response to the current crisis.”

Elpis set one hand on her belt buckle while the other popped a hidden catch on her shoulder. Her belt and all its weapons came away in one hand, and her quiver of arrows in the other. “Director Armstrong,” she said, holding both sets of gear out, “I’d like to surrender my weapons as a show of good faith while I’m in Boston.”

Director Armstrong barely managed to hide his surprise. “I appreciate the gesture,” he managed. “Doohickey, would you mind?”

Doohickey stepped forward in his pocketed overalls bulging with gadgets and gingerly accepted the weapons. “Thanks,” Elpis said.

The glass box at her hip, about six inches to a side and filled with insects, buzzed and clicked for a second before a shocking noise came from it. “Hey Doohickey, you feel like talking shop later?”

Doohickey took a sharp pace back. “What the hell is that?”

“I made this so the Butchers could communicate,” Elpis explained, tapping the top of the box. “That’s Tock Tick, Butcher VII, the Tinker.”

“…that’s horrifying,” Doohickey managed.

“You get used to it,” Ironclad said.

“I only figured it out a while back,” Elpis admitted with a shrug. “Anyway,” she stepped back and addressed everyone present, “I think I should start by apologising on behalf of the Butchers, because god knows they’ll never do it themselves. I know a lot of people in this room fought them and the Teeth, or had to deal with the aftermath, and I’m sorry about that. I’m here to help, and I hope you’ll all give me the chance to prove that.”
