Briar Patch stepped forward after a second. “I heard you helped patch me up after the Leviathan fight,” she said. “I don’t think the Butchers would have ever done that. You’re alright with me.”

Elpis frowned for a second, eyebrows drawing together, then snapped her fingers. “Shit, that was you, I didn’t realise. Glad to see you’re doing well.”

“So you can really hear the Butchers?” Flipper asked, peaking out from behind Weld. “in your head?”

“Yes I can…” Elpis faltered. “I’m sorry, I don’t think I caught your name.”

“Flippercanorius.”

“Gesundheit,” said the box of bugs.

“Beat me by one second,” Imp said.

“It means fantastic or wonderful,” Flipper explained. “You can just call me Flipper for short.”

“Got it. Nice to meet you, Flipper,” Elpis said with a small smile.

Armstrong cleared his throat. “We should take this to the briefing room. If you’ll follow me, please.”

“My dogs can’t fit up there,” Cerberus said. “Gonna need to wait for them to shrink down.”

“Do you want to stay here and we’ll fill you in later?” Elpis offered.

Cerberus shrugged. “Sure.”

Armstrong nodded. “Let the troopers know if you need anything. This way, please.” He gave the troopers stationed at the foot of the staircase a nod as he started up the steps. The heroes followed him, all manner of footsteps echoing up the staircase.

 

 

Boilerplate looked up from picking at a spot on her armour as the door opened, and a few dozen heroes trooped in. She felt pretty bloody small looking at them- Elpis and Armsmaster and Miss Militia for crying out loud! She’d heard about them getting ambushed on the way into town, but none of them looked even winded. For a moment, Boilerplate wondered how much use she’d actually be here.

She shook herself. She’d be more use here than anywhere else, so here she was. That was the whole point of this.

The new arrivals arranged themselves in the rows of seats while Director Armstrong fired up the projector. There was a lot of shuffling and creaking and a few muttered apologies as people in heavy armour and long capes squeezed past each other, but no big fuss. The Protectorate, locals and out-of-towners, took the first few rows. The Wards took one side of the aisle, and the Undersiders took the other. She saw Elpis tug her deep blue cape to the side as she sat down, a glass box full of insects on her lap. The unmasked capes in white grouped together, a fellow in armour sitting next to the blonde girl.

That just left Boilerplate at the back, with Super Magic Dream Parade on the other end. Bunch of weirdos.

The only people not sitting were Director Armstrong at the front, now holding a remote for the projector, and Bastion, who was leaning against the wall with his arms folded. Boilerplate glanced at him for a second, and then looked away. She didn’t have any sympathy for him- what kind of person bellowed slurs at a little kid?

“Okay, let’s get started,” Armstrong said. A click of the remote brought up a map of Boston, with various gang territories highlighted in different colours. Blastgerm’s territory in East Allston was green, and there were about three dozen green crosses planted on the map. Most were just outside of Blasto’s territory, but a few outliers popped up further away, in Cambridge, Charlestown, the South End, China Town, and even one in Mass and Cass.

“Yikes,” said the bug box on Elpis’ lap. “I didn’t know it was that bad.”

Boilerplate stared at the box. Nobody else seemed to react to it- okay, Super Magic Dream Parade were staring at it like she was, but nobody else seemed bothered.

“This is the current situation,” Armstrong explained, gesturing with the laser pointer in the remote. “Blasto, leader of the villain group Blastgerm, has been unleashing creatures on Boston, more powerful and unstable than his usual fare. We’re currently unsure as to his motives- it doesn’t seem coordinated enough for a territory push or settling a score.”

“How exactly are the creatures more powerful?” one of the maskless capes asked.

“Blasto’s creations have demonstrated minor abilities for years- increased strength, durability, various projectiles, flight,” Armstrong listed. “But now they’ve exhibited more extreme powers- pyrokinesis, teleportation, non-organic shapeshifting. Some have even displayed evidence of minor Thinker powers. It’s way outside of Blasto’s usual wheelhouse, and that’s concerning. The amount of materials they were able to successfully steal is also concerning, particularly here.” He circled the crosses at Franklin Park Zoo, and Boilerplate swore to herself. “Multiple incidents of zoo animals being sampled by Blasto minions. Bears, giraffes, tigers, and many others. Blasto’s acquired DNA from exotic animals before, but never this frequently and blatantly. He could very well be building something as vast as the Woad Giant.”

Boilerplate swallowed. She remembered the Boston Games, and the sight of the Woad Giant had shaken her to her core. The idea of that coming around again…

“Do you think he’s recruited another Tinker or Tinkers?” Armsmaster asked. “Someone whose speciality compliments his own, to augment his minions?”

“It’s a sound theory, but right now we don’t have any evidence to support it,” Armstrong admitted.

“Maybe it’s a Trump?” Tattletale suggested. “Granting minor powers to the minions for added effect.” She pushed the elaborate goggles she was wearing further up her forehead.

“Also a possibility,” Armstrong allowed. “Unfortunately we don’t have time to speculate; we need to deal with this situation now, before the situation escalates further. Blasto’s attempted attack on our volunteers from Brockton Bay proves that he’s aware we’re mustering a response against him. We’ve also got wind of the other villain groups preparing to address this themselves, so we need to handle this before they do. The collateral damage could be immense.”

“So what’s the plan to deal with this, sir?”

“The plan is to divide into smaller groups,” Armstrong said. “We’ll have a few mobile groups ready to respond to any further minion attacks or villains taking advantage of the chaos, while multiple assault teams head into Allston to locate Blasto’s base of operations.”

“Search and destroy,” Volpertinger said with a grin. “I like the sound of that.”

Elpis raised a gauntleted hand, waiting until Armstrong indicated to speak. Boilerplate noticed there was a symbol of a cleaver on the back of her hand. “Cerberus’s dogs can carry passengers and jump rooftops. They’d be well-suited for a response role- although you’ll want to introduce yourselves to the dogs first.”

Armstrong nodded. “That’d be greatly appreciated. Thank you.”

“So where are you going?” Bastion asked caustically. “Going to stroll around Downtown and show off?”

Multiple people shot Bastion hard looks. Elpis didn’t bat an eye. “I can move pretty fast, but if people see me teleporting around, they’ll still run on instinct. I’m probably better off with the assault teams. I mean, me, versus disposable minions?” She shrugged. “Grass meets lawnmower.”

Boilerplate mentally pictured the powers of the Butcher against non-sapient organic minions, and grimaced. They wouldn’t have to retrieve the bodies so much as hose them into the nearest drain.

“I’d still advise you to be careful. Remember, these minions are stronger than normal, with unexpected powers.”

“Got it.”

“You’ll also want to keep in mind the other gangs. Boston’s villains are known to keep to an informal peace, but I don’t want to risk it. We’ll go into detail on Dark Society, Midnight Mass, Morning Glory, the Ambassadors, and the various biker groups.”

Chapter End Notes

Most of the info about Earth bet's Boston is from supplementary materials, but some very nice people helped me find the info.

Most of the capes mentioned here, including Ariel, are OCs that I'll expand on later, but Boilerplate is actually canon, barely. She's an independent Boston hero who's got a particular grudge against the gang Mystic Mass, who are also canon. Honestly, I like her a lot- might have to write a larger part for her.

Chapter 143: 14.7

Chapter Notes

There's a lot of cameos and shout-outs in this chapter. Some are references to favourite series and so on, some are people I know. I'll leave it to you to find out which is which.

Friday 30th June, Boston PRT Building

“So they’re still just regular dogs under all that?” Stampede asked, adjusting his shoulder pads. His costume had been updated since the last time the Butchers had checked PHO for intel- a little less football player and a little more riot gear. I understood why they’d made his old costume like that- he created duplicates of himself as he ran, becoming a one-man scrum- but he looked more sensible this way.

“Yeah,” Cerberus explained as I double-checked Brutus’ saddle-collar and stepped back. “They’re trained before I use my power on them.”

“Cool.”

“How big do their treats have to be when they’re like this?” Flippercanorious asked with a grin, hovering in the air, leaving a trail of little silver sparkles from her cape and boots.

“Feeding them like this doesn’t work,” Cerberus explained.

“Which is a relief. Imagine the size of the bones you’d need,” Tock Tick snickered. “We’d have to raid a dinosaur exhibit!”

Flippercanorious giggled at that, although Cerberus just looked confused.

I double-checked all my weapons. Doohickey had given them back after the briefing, and right now we were just waiting to get everything in order before we began the assault on East Allston. The heavy hitters would take the fight to Blasto and his beasts, while the more mobile heroes kept the rest of the city in order. Tattletale would be staying in the building to coordinate us and try to figure out a pattern to Blasto’s actions, along with the Wards Hunch and Windchime.

The Undersiders were mostly in the assault team, seasoned as we were- and that thought stirred a little pride in me, that my team were hardened and experienced fighters who’d faced down S-class events and come through. Imp, though, would be in the patrol groups. She wasn’t built for a fight like this, and frankly I thought she’d prefer running around town and screwing with villains. She was bonding with Reynard, a Stranger like herself.

A bunch of extra independent heroes had turned up while we were briefing- I could see Rabbit Punch from the local Protectorate team talking to a man in a black coat, suit, and bandana mask, with a ponytail, goatee, and multiple swords strapped to him. Apparently his name was Clean-Cut; Muramasa wanted to talk to him at some point, see how he handled those swords.

Across from them was a guy called Smokescreen, in a trenchcoat and hat like an old private eye. The Butchers had heard of him, but never met him personally- apparently he was more concerned with white collar crime, crooked accounting and corporate coverups. He roamed back and forth through the financial district, digging up crimes. I noticed a patch on the shoulder of his coat, three diagonal arrows.

There was a kid dressed in crude red clothes, like a caveman, holding a stone axe bigger than his own body that he idly passed from hand to hand. I swore I saw him muttering to it.

A group of three off in the corner- a curvy blonde in a skintight blue suit, a big guy in a leather jacket and aviators, and a girl in a skimpy ninja costume.

“Check out the ass on that blonde,” Dirty Rotter grinned.

“And the ninja girl,” Anchorage agreed. “Hey Taylor, move your head, she’s got something written on her shorts.”

“I’m not going to ogle in the middle of a truce meeting,” I protested. After a second’s thought, I grudgingly moved a couple of flies around to get a look.

“Much obliged,” Anchorage said with a grin.

There was a girl with purple skin and white hair turning her hands into massive paws and back again, talking to Volpertinger of the Boston Protectorate. They seemed to be comparing their Changer powers. A girl in a costume with racing stripes was leaning against the wall and watching them- I thought her name was Momentum.

“Everyone hold on. We’ve got something,” Armstrong announced, coming through to the loading docks, a phone in hand. “Doohickey, do you have a speaker?”

Doohickey obligingly pulled a device from one of his many pockets and tapped it against the phone. “It’s paired. What’s going on, Director?”

“This phone was delivered to the front desk by a bicycle messenger on an anonymous job. It’s been scanned and confirmed to contain no explosives or other traps, and there’s only one number loaded into it.”

“Only one person this could be,” Quarrel snorted.

I agreed with her. Any other faction in Boston would have sent a cheap little burner phone or a written note to send a message. Only one villain would deliver an expensive smartphone to get in touch with the heroes.

Sure enough, when the call was picked up, I recognised the cultured tones that came through Doohickey’s miniature speaker, as polished and honed as a surgical scalpel. “Good morning.”

“Accord,” I said. The quality of the audio was impressive, very little distortion or garbling. It sounded like Boston’s top Thinker was right in the room with us. I saw people flinch.

“Indeed. And I suspect I am speaking to Elpis?”

“You suppose correctly,” I said, rolling my eyes at Armstrong. He gave an agreeing grimace.

“A pleasure,” Accord said. “I suppose we are technically familiar with each other already. May I offer my compliments on your work? You’ve made great strides on improving your city.”

“The funny thing is, he’s probably being honest,” Tactical admitted.

“Everything neat and tidy,” I agreed. Accord was known to be exacting, precise and picky. He was a large part of why Boston’s villains tended to negotiate rather than war with each other. Many people speculated that he had something similar to OCD, either as a result of his power or from before that. The Butchers had heard he’d once put out a hit on someone for peeing on the toilet seat, and they believed it.

“I appreciate the compliment,” I said with an even tone, while I gestured rudely to the speaker. Several of the heroes suppressed laughter as I continued, “If you’ll excuse my bluntness, why are you calling just now? Offering to cooperate on dealing with Blasto?”

“Somewhat, yes. I have… information regarding his recent developments.”

Tattletale hurried over and put her mouth to my ear. “He’s embarrassed,” she hissed. “There’s something going on he doesn’t want to admit.”

I nodded silently. Accord wasn’t the sort to hesitate.

Director Armstrong took over the conversation. “We’d appreciate anything you can give us.”

Accord was silent for a moment. “Some weeks ago, I approached Blasto about a possible collaboration. I had acquired an index of DNA samples from various parahumans, and I offered to give him the index to improve his creations, on condition that we split any territory gains between us.”

“He was planning to set him up to fail,” Tattletale whispered.

“Sounds like Accord alright,” Firecracker said. “Plans within plans.”

I gathered up bugs and spread them out on the floor, arranging them into words so Armstrong could see- ACCORD WAS SETTING HIM UP. Armstrong glanced at it and nodded.

“But something went wrong,” Armstrong said. “I assume Blasto went back on your deal.”

“Blasto was approached by another group just as I’d given him the index,” Accord stated. “A mercenary group from Canada- the Dragonslayers. You may have heard of them.”

“I have,” Armstrong confirmed. “They use mech suits for various activities, and they’ve clashed with Dragon multiple times- the name suggests some kind of grudge. They recently attacked the black market Tinker group Toybox and made off with a lot of technology. The PRT has been speculating on their goals.”

“I’m afraid I have no greater insight on their motives just yet,” Accord admitted.

“Notice the ‘yet’ in that sentence,” Needler pointed out. “I’m pretty sure one of his Ambassadors has some kind of Stranger power.”

“Most likely,” Vladimir agreed. “The trouble with Stranger powers is that they are by definition difficult to get confirmation of.”

Needler sighed. “God, I hate dealing with Strangers.”

Briar Patch stepped forward, raising a hand. At Armstrong’s nod, she joined in. “Briar Patch here. You think that the Dragonslayers provided Blasto with additional tech to augment his creations?”

“That would appear to be the case. Do you know what technology was stolen from Toybox? That may shed some light on his progress?”

Armstrong drew a circle on his phone and started flicking through menus. “The current known members of Toybox are Pyrotechnical, Big Rig, Bauble, Dodge, Toy Soldier, Glace, and Cranial. None of them are wet Tinkers- it’s hard to see a connection.”

“I can take a look, see if anything pops up,” Tattletale offered.

“Please do.”

“I will mull it over myself,” Accord said. “In the meantime, I would like to offer my Ambassadors as reinforcements, to ensure a quick end to this mess. If you’re willing to authorise a temporary truce, I will see about contacting other villain groups willing to assist.”

“Done,” Armstrong said with a scowl. “It’d probably be better if we keep our forces divided though- it’ll force Blasto to defend multiple fronts, and it’ll mean less chance of any misunderstandings between groups.”

“Acceptable,” Accord said. “I’ll begin preparations. I’ll call you again when I have more.” He hung up without another word.

“It’s rare to see Accord making a misstep,” Briar Patch noted.

“There’s always something unexpected,” I pointed out.

“We’ll deal with it,” Armstrong said. “This means we need to be ready to fight the Dragonslayers as well. They have three large, advanced suits of Tinkertech. That means an entirely different style of engagement.”

“I’d like to request taking point when it comes to the Dragonslayers,” Armsmaster spoke up.  “My halberd has an EMP emitter and my nanothorns can go through their armour.”

“Look how he’s clenching his jaw,” Bearskin said. “He’s ticked off.”

“He is friends with Dragon, remember?” Muramasa said. “This will be personal to him.”

“If we get in close, my power can go through their suits like wet clay,” Stoneknapper pointed out. “We’ll back you up.”

Armsmaster nodded firmly. “Thank you.”

“I’m afraid we can’t put this off,” Armstrong said. “If everyone is ready, we should begin.”

 

 

En-route to East Allston

Most of the heroes had loaded back into PRT vans, but the dogs could take a few more. I rode Judas with Miss Militia riding pillion, Cerberus was on Brutus with Flechette, and Brandish and Flashbang were awkwardly riding Bentley, with Lady Photon and Glory Girl flying overhead. Ironclad was down below with the vans, wheels spinning.

One of the other hero groups had already split off, to head in from the east. Our group would head up from the south, and the third would come from the west. If Blasto tried to run north, he’d be heading straight into Accord’s forces.

“I’m actually kind of hoping Blasto pulls out something new for us,” Butcher said through the streak of bugs I had flying alongside us. “That ambush was fun, but nothing challenging.”

“Butcher, for the love of god, are you trying to jinx us?” I asked tiredly.

“I’m starting to see why the new Butchers always went crazy,” Miss Militia admitted from behind me.

“Yeah, and he’s not even trying to be annoying,” I said. “This is him on a good day.”

“Fuck you.”

“See? That was pretty restrained for him.”

We were coming up on the end of Beacon Street now- from there we’d divide and begin the real push. Going over the rooftops would hopefully avoid any roadblocks or ambushes that Blasto had set up. He’d done it before- motion-triggered attack plants, soldiers in the sewer system, patches of toxic fungus blending into the road, exploding mushrooms. Tock Tick thought he might have taken inspiration from Plants vs Zombies.

I spread my insects out as we made the turn, splitting off from most of the vans and heading north. I loosened my bow in its quiver, ready for action.

The other vans were just out of sight when dark shapes burst up into the sky and shot towards us.

“Incoming!” Lady Photon said, throwing out forcefields.

“Get ready to take the reins,” I said over my shoulder, pulling my bow out and nocking an arrow. Insects flew from my armour to cloud the air.

I could make out details as the things approached- some had wings to fly, but others were flying without any visible assistance. One had fire burning in its hands and on its head, another was glowing in shifting patterns of light.

“Blasto’s definitely got something making them more powerful,” Flinch speculated.

The dogs pulled to a halt, and I loosed, aiming for the creature in front. It dodged to the side, and the arrow only clipped it in the leg, making it scream. I cursed and switched my bow out for axe and sword.

The other heroes opened up with lasers and bullets and arbalest bolts, cutting into the creatures’ ranks. I teleported off Judas’s back and up in the air, above them, as Glory Girl soared up below them.

“Come on!” Nemean roared as I dropped onto them.

The one with the burning hair died from the sword through the head, and I clipped one with writhing skin with the axe as I fell past. I shot my grappler out to snare a third and reeled in, grabbing its leg and stabbing into the leathery skin of its thigh. It shrieked and flicked a hand at me, triggering danger sense. I flung an arm up as multicoloured bubbles flew from its arm, bursting against my armour in puffs of smoke that kicked like fireworks.

Flechette’s shots were going through the creatures like a hot knife through butter, but they were reacting intelligently, bobbing and weaving while throwing long-range attacks towards her. Lady Photon threw up forcefields to protect her while Flashbang and Glory Girl chucked Brandish’s ball form back and forth between each other like a game of catch- every time she passed one of the creatures, she switched back into human form and sliced at them with a weapon.

I hit the creature I was grappling with a blast of pain and lopped its arm off with my axe, soaking the blood up with Vladimir’s power, then pulled my sword through its leg and disengaged the grappler, letting us both fall. I teleported again, onto another creature that was tanking bullets and lasers without flinching. It had a full set of antlers that I grabbed onto while I pressed my sword against the base of its neck as it bellowed and bucked. Rotter’s power oozed up the length of the blade and into the creature’s skin, rotting it away as I forced it in, between the vertebrae and out through the throat. It gagged and fell, and I leapt off as it crashed into the rooftop.

My insects were harassing the remainder, going for eyes and mouths and joints, and there weren’t many creatures left for them to fight. I pulled out my bow again and nailed a winged thing through the head, ducked a swooping attack from a thing with massive claws for feet, and punched a thing that charged at me with fists turning into clumps of rock. It reeled back, nose broken, its face turning into more stone, so I ducked to the side and stabbed the blade on the end of my bow into its armpit. It dropped to its knees, and I rammed the blade through its ear to finish it off.

“I think that’s the last of them,” Miss Militia said as I looked around.

“Should we check on the other group?” Lady Photon asked, dropping down to the rooftop.

“Probably a good idea,” I said, nocking another arrow. “These things were worryingly well positioned. The others might have got ambushed too.”

“Don’t wait for us, go,” Miss Militia said, gesturing. I nodded and broke into a run, teleporting in the direction of the other group.

Lady Photon and Glory Girl caught up fast, and then overtook me. I just grunted and pushed my muscles harder.

In a few more seconds, I caught sight of the other convoy through my bugs, and they were under attack too. Ironclad was struggling with a massive thing that looked like a ten-foot armadillo man with a wrecking ball for a tail, and Frostfern was exchanging blasts with a creature shooting lightning from its fingertips. Bastion was throwing up forcefields to separate civilians from the fight and keep everything contained, herding stranded people into a nearby music shop to take shelter.

“Asshole’s still useful for something,” Dirty Rotter snorted.

Glory Girl dove and slammed into the armadillo thing’s head with both fists, sending it staggering. Ironclad took the opportunity to bring his hammer around and smash it in the knee, then detached the hammer head from the haft and drove the sharp end up between its armour plates.

I spotted Clean-Cut from before, a katana in one hand and an arming sword in the other, slipping between them like he was skating, hacking limbs off with ease. One creature was split in half from head to groin, splattering him with green muck- it slid off him in an instant, and he moved on to the next.

“We must talk to him,” Muramasa insisted.

I teleported into the thick of it- these creatures didn’t seem to be flyers, but they were bigger, more animalistic. Some were thrown by the explosion- I drew my flail and whipped it around, breaking bones.

“Good to see you, boss!” Ironclad yelled, slamming punches into the armadillo thing’s face- despite the spear sticking out of its chest, it was still putting up a fight.

“Like I’d miss this!” I roared back, flicking a knife at the thing shooting lightning. The knife struck it in the back, and it staggered with a howl. Frostfern ran forward, throwing ice over its legs, then clamped her hands around its head. Ice spread over and through it, then she kicked it in the chest. When the head hit the ground, pieces broke off.

There was a crash of broken glass as one creature hit the window of the music shop, grabbing musical instruments like improvised weapons. Bastion created a thick forcefield to replace the glass, and more to box the creature in, slowly tightening them to constrict it.

Boilerplate charged into a knot of creatures, steam pouring off her armour, scalding the creatures. Smokescreen was shifting from solid to mist, letting blows pass through him before slamming punches into his opponent with impressive form.

“He’s got a pretty good jab for a guy who does detective work,” Tock Tick said admiringly.

I reeled the flail in and brought it down on a creature sneaking up on me, its skin changing colours to blend in. The blow reduced its skull to paste, and it crumpled. I pulled the flail free and continued.

Barking announced the dogs- they leapt down to street level and lashed out, biting and clawing, prehensile tails swatting the smaller creatures aside. Cerberus roared, spear in hand, shouting orders.

Some of the creatures turned and ran, some climbing up the buildings to get away, dragging whatever random stuff they’d picked up, including some stray instruments. I spotted Rabbit Punch, with his long-eared hood and knuckle wraps, leap three stories up to catch one that had somehow acquired a banjo - he landed a dozen punches in three seconds, then snapped its spine with a single kick. As the creature toppled over dead, he snatched the banjo out of its hands.

“Okay, we’re gonna try recruiting him, right?” Anchorage asked.

“He’s got my vote,” Firecracker said.

One creature didn’t run- a hulking mass of skinless muscle, overgrown to cartoonish proportions. The muscles even grew over its face like a mask, leaving sunken pits for eyes. It charged at me with a bellow, tendrils of muscle whipping out from its arms. Bloodsight showed it was humanoid inside the mass- a large, broad-shouldered man. Something about that was familiar in a vague way.

I skipped back, switching the flail for axe and sword again, and popped the blades out of my armour, slashing a few tendrils off as they got close. The muscle thing didn’t seem to feel it, swiping at me again, the fibres on its other arm growing into a single fat rope that it lashed at me.

I ducked and slashed through it with my sword, then hacked through the return swing with my axe. The muscle creature howled at that, more muscle fibres growing into place, swelling its size even more.

I hit it with pain, then stepped forward, Vladimir’s power rising up. The world went slow and tinged with red as I sprinted forward, gripped my sword in both hands, and rammed it through all those layers of dense muscle fibres into the pulsing scarlet knot of its heart.

The thing gurgled, its muscles unravelling from around it as it sagged. The muscles dropped from it piece by piece, pattering onto the ground.

“There’s something about this one,” Needler mused as the thing gurgled and gasped. I wordlessly agreed as I pulled the sword out.

The muscle creature fell to its knees, those sunken pits staring up at me. I could see a glimmer of eye at the bottom, disturbingly human.

“Butcher.”

And the thing toppled forward onto its face.

The sword fell from my hand. I dropped down and turned it over, clawing at the muscle fibres over its face and chest. Blasto’s creatures didn’t speak- they didn’t have the capacity for that. I’d just killed a person, not a creature- some idiot who hadn’t thought to identify himself as other than one of Blasto’s creatures.

The last few strands around his face snapped off, revealing ash blond hair and a square jaw. I stared through bloodsight as his brain greyed out, marking the transition from living person to cooling meat.

“Oh god.” Glory Girl was hovering behind me, hands over her mouth. “Is that…”

“Yeah,” I said heavily. “It’s a person.”

“Hey, look, this isn’t your fault, okay?” Bearskin said. “The guy either joined up with Blasto or got caught up in the fight, and he was too dumb to say ‘Hey, I’m not a monster, don’t kill me’, right?”

“Natural selection in action,” Quarrel said with a shrug. I pushed her down into the dark, turning off bloodsight- I couldn’t stand to look at the greyed-out mass of the man anymore.

The second bloodsight shut off, I got a good look at his face- and I didn’t believe what I saw. I grabbed his head in both hands and hauled him up to get a proper look.

“What are you doing?” Glory Girl demanded as I turned his head this way and that, looking him over. The jaw, the ears, the bushy eyebrows, the beady little eyes- all familiar from Needler’s memories. Except the last time she’d seen him, he’d only had one eye.

“I know who this is.”

“What the hell’s going on here?” BriarPatch asked, stepping through the carnage towards us.

I turned the corpse to face her, and people gasped. “This,” I said, shaking the corpse for emphasis, “Is Muscular.”

“You know him?” Briar Patch asked.

“Yeah, he was one of the Teeth back in the day.”

“Really? I never heard of him.” Briar Patch cocked her head. “Was he trying to kill you, inherit the Butcher powers?”

“He already tried that. Back in 1996. Needler carved his eye out for it. Then he joined the Slaughterhouse Nine, fled Brockton Bay, and got his head punched off when they attacked a summer camp. This man,” I said, shaking the corpse again, “Has been dead for fifteen years.”

Briar Patch’s jaw dropped.

“This is so much more fucked up than we thought,” Tactical said.

Chapter 144: 14.8

Friday 30th June, East Allston, Boston

“Call the other teams, warn them,” I said to Briar Patch. “They need to know about this.”

“On it.” Briar Patch already had a finger to her ear, relaying the information to the rest of the heroes.

“How is this possible?” Smokescreen asked, gesturing to the corpse.

“Blasto must have made more progress than we thought,” Tactical said. “If he’s creating actual capes, not just powered minions, then this fight just got a lot harder.”

“There’s also the ethical implications,” Flinch cut in. “If these are full clones of capes, then they’re sapient human beings- and Blasto must have some kind of control on them to make them do what he wants. They’re basically Master victims.”

I saw people wince at that. I wasn’t feeling too good about it myself.

“Muscular joined the Nine, for fuck’s sake- they’d have wanted him dead again anyway,” Firecracker pointed out.

“Yes, but we can’t assume any other clones will be so simple to judge,” I said, dropping the corpse. After a second, I crouched down and closed his eyes. I didn’t really respect the guy, I just didn’t want him staring at me. “What if Blasto clones lesser villains? Or heroes?”

Tock Tick signalled for me to keep his next words inside my head. “What if he clones back somebody big? Like Hero?”

I paused. “Damn. That’s a thought.”

“I can’t decide if it’s a good one or a bad one,” Tock Tick admitted.

“That’s assuming Blasto had the thought- or any kind of thought,” Nemean snorted.

“Armsmaster’s scanned some of the remains,” Briar Patch spoke up. “Fully human DNA. Actual parahuman clones.” Behind her thorn-spiked mask, I could see her face turning pale.

“So what do we do?” Ironclad asked. “Are we still fighting to kill?”

Miss Militia’s weapon shifted from a rifle to a cavalry sabre to a pair of uzis, before settling into a fat pistol. “If we can take them alive, then we should. But they’ve displayed a willingness to escalate to lethal force, so we need to be prepared to respond in kind.”

“Shit,” Boilerplate muttered.

My own earpiece beeped, and I tapped it. “Elpis receiving.”

“Boss, I heard about the clones. Same shit, different day, huh?” Tattletale laughed, a tinge of desperation in her voice.

“Sure seems like it. Any advice?”

“Not sure, but I double-checked the Tinkers the Dragonslayers robbed, and one stood out. Cranial specialises in neurology- brain scans, neural links, recording thoughts, removing memories. And that got me thinking- the other clones had the memories of their originals, and we never thought about that much, right? I thought it was just a side effect of the powers connecting. But what if we got it backwards? What if the memories are what makes the powers connect? Something like a Trigger event, or close enough, to make the power lock on to a brain with the right DNA?”

“No way they could have got Muscular’s whole brain scanned, he was dead way before Toybox started,” Dirty Rotter said.

Quarrel snorted. “So it’s a close-enough kind of thing- stick in memories that give the right Trigger event, and maybe the power itself fills in the rest- the fairy or whatever the fuck Glaistig Uaine was on about.”

“It’s plausible,” I said to all of them, “but right now we need to stop this before it gets any worse. Can you try and figure out if these things have some kind of weakness we can use? Maybe use their memories to break whatever’s making them follow Blasto?”

“I’ll work on it,” Tattletale promised. “Be careful.”

“I will. Elpis out.” I ended the call and turned to everyone else. Bastion had shuffled his forcefields around so that the civilians who’d been sheltering in the buildings around us could leave, and circled the heroes to give us some breathing room. “I’m all for pushing on and getting to Blasto, but what does everyone else think?” As I spoke, I directed my bugs to return to me, some of them wrapping silk thread around the knife I’d killed one creature with and lifting it towards my hand.

“We need to finish this,” Brandish declared. “Quickly.”

“She’s right,” Flashbang agreed. “If Blasto’s cracked human cloning, the stakes are even higher.”

Fresh vines sprouted from Briar Patch’s skin, with thorns as long and sharp as needles. “This ends today.”

The other heroes all made gestures or noises of agreement- Bastion nodded, Frostfern cracked her knuckles, Boilerplate smacked her fist into her palm. I noticed Clean-Cut drawing and checking each one of his swords with quiet focus.

“You know I’m down for smashing monsters,” Ironclad said, reassembling his hammer and slinging it onto his back.

“Right. I think one larger group would be more effective from here on out. I’ll teleport- who wants to ride on Judas?”

Rabbit Punch raised a hand. “I’ll give it a shot.”

“Rachel, that okay with you?”

“Just don’t hurt him.”

Rabbit Punch gave Judas a quick look. “I don’t think that’ll be a problem.”

I nodded. “Let’s get Blasto.”

It took only a few moments to check equipment, drag the bodies out of the way, mount up in the trucks and on the dogs, and set off North again. My bugs let me see people flinch as they heard the sound of my teleports echoing across the streets. That hurt a little, but six months was not enough time for people to forget the mayhem those explosions heralded.

I cast out with my bugs as well, scouting ahead for any more traps or ambushes. I didn’t pick up on anything else, but that wasn’t a comfort.

“We need to drop to the streets,” I called out after a while. “Lot of wooden houses around here, they won’t be able to handle the dogs.”

Cerberus whistled, and the dogs clawed their way down one the side of a brick building to bound along the road. Cars veered aside or braked sharply as the group continued.

“Do you think Blasto will survive this day?” Muramasa asked.

“I doubt it,” Vladimir said. “He already had a pre-signed Kill Order if he made anything that could self-replicate. Resurrecting Slaughterhouse villains? He’s a dead man walking.”

“Yeah, but wouldn’t the heroes want something like that on their side?” Bearskin asked. “Like Tock said, if he brought back Hero or somebody like that…”

“That’s a whole can of worms that I don’t think any of us would know how to handle,” Needler said. “Personally, I hope we get to give him a beating at least. Making me have to see Muscular again…”

“You still didn’t keep your promise,” Butcher cackled. “Remember? If he ever got more eyeballs than assholes-”

“Shove one up the other, yes, we know, Butcher,” I completed with a roll of my eyes.

The talk didn’t help me nerves. I’d fought with lethal force plenty of times- Noelle’s clones, Leviathan, the Nine, the Birdcage- but all of those times had been acceptable targets, insane or monstrous or already convicted. If I was facing off against opponents who were decent people, controlled by whatever the hell Blasto had cooked up, then I didn’t want to cross that line.

It might not be up to me though. Masters used people as weapons all the time- Heartbreaker was well know for it, the Fallen had done it a couple of times, and the Simurgh’s victims were the ultimate example. The thought sat in my stomach like a lead ball.

As we made it past Brighton Avenue and went straight down Everett Street, something brushed against the leading edge of my insect perimeter, made of the fastest fliers I could find. Something with spikes growing out of its skin.

“Heads up, I think we’ve got something up ahead,” I called through my bugs. Miss Militia gave me a thumbs up from Judas and tapped her earpiece to relay to the heroes in the vans. I switched to bloodsight, scanning ahead. There were things in the gardens up ahead of us, hiding in the trees and buried in the grass; I planted bugs on them as I told Miss Militia.

As soon as we reached that stretch of road, the ambush happened. Bursts of fire and smoke erupted from one side, a wave of some sort of purple slime from the other- if we hadn’t know already, they might have caught a few of us. As it was, Bastion’s forcefields went up to shield us, with Frostfern countering any fire that slipped through. I teleported up to the top of a nearby building, drawing my bow and looking down.

Sure enough, more creatures- and they were pretty human looking. Some had buried themselves in the grass and blended into the trees, while more were pouring out of the apartment building opposite my building, some leaping down from the balconies. The heroes responded in kind, leaping from the vans with weapons drawn.

Cerberus wheeled Brutus around to leap straight into the fray, while I sent my bugs towards the creatures, stinging and biting and wrapping silk threads around wrists and ankles to trip them up and hamper them. I kept them away from the figure of purple slime- the few insects I’d landed on them had already drowned.

“Feels like a surprisingly good matchup for your bugs,” Stoneknapper said. “Do you think Blasto know you’re after him?”

“Maybe,” I said, drawing my bow and firing an arrow down at a creature with ram horns charging at Flashbang. The arrow went through its calf, and it stumbled right into a concussive grenade that sent it flipping through the air into the branches of a tree.

“Sniping’s not going to be enough for this fight,” Anchorage said. “They need you on the front line.”

Down below, one of the van drivers threw it into reverse, backing up into a bunch of the creatures. They were flattened, but the back tyres burst, and the driver ducked down as a flyer swooped down, flicking sharp scales from its tail that cracked the windscreen.

I agreed with Anchorage, switching my bow for my flail as I teleported into the fray, swinging into a thing like a bear with thumbs. The blow sent it reeling back, jaw hanging loose, before it grasped its jaw and popped it back into place with a grunt of pain and a crunch of bone.

“Gross,” Firecracker said as I hit it with pain and smashed its knee instead, then its shoulder. A quick jab of the fingers with Rotter’s decay set the wounds festering- that’d keep it down for a while.

“Fall back to the parking lot!” I shouted, headbutting a too-tall figure with sharp teeth. “Get room to move!” We were too pinned in here, surrounded on both sides. I teleported again, into a group of things that were grappling with Briar Patch’s vines. Punches and kicks broke bones and crushed nerve bundles, disabling the creatures fast.

A fresh wave of purple slime burst from the side, only stopped by Bastion’s forcefields. The thing throwing it around drew the slime back into itself, swelling up in size with hammer-like fists.

“Wait a second,” Dirty Rotter exclaimed, “Is that Oozy Lover?”

I drew some insects together to get a closer look. I couldn’t get a clear look at the figure through the slime coating them, but there was an impression of a large gut- and the hammer-fists, those had been a signature move of the big fat brawler who had tangled with the Teeth several times back in 2003, before crossing Digger and his bikers.

“Son of a bitch, I think it is!” Anchorage exclaimed. This had been just before she’d inherited, and she had plenty of memories of how frustrating Oozy Lover was to fight, flinging his slime all over the place while using it to soak up damage from bullet and bludgeons and everything else.

“We need to try and get through to him,” Flinch said at once. “He’s not Muscular- maybe we can snap him out of whatever Blasto’s done.”

I agreed, even as I blasted a clawed thing with pain and cracked its kneecap. It clutched at its leg as it fell, claws slicing into its bark-like skin. “Oozy Lover,” I said as the heroes began a fighting retreat, fending off the creatures.

The mound of slime twitched, turning towards the bugs I’d made to speak.

“Oozy Lover, is that you? Can you understand me?”

Miss Militia opened up with a rifle full of rubber bullets, hammering into the horde. Flechette pulled one of her needles from her quiver and used it like a short sword to lop off a tentacle. Glory Girl and Lady Photon engaged the few fliers in the group, with Rabbit Punch occasionally leaping up from below to speedbag the enemy.

The slime bubbled around the head as the figure shrank down a bit, fists reshaping into smaller hands.

A centaur creature with a human torso on top of a tiger body barrelled forward, the ground rippling like water with every step it took. I leapt up and headbutted it, breaking its nose, then punched it where the tiger and human bodies met. It squealed and dropped, clutching the point I’d struck.

“Who…?” the slime figure gurgled.

“My name is Elpis. I don’t want to fight you. Can you remember yourself?”

“Oo-zee…”

We’d all retreated to the parking lot, forming a semi-circle. Bastion’s forcefields and Briar Patch’s vines formed decent cover for the ranged heroes to shoot from while the rest of us got stuck in. I had insects aim for joints and faces, making it more painful for the creatures to move and harder to see. Any time a hero started getting overwhelmed, I teleported in to break up the problem.

“Oozy… Lover…” the slime said. “That’s… my… name… It’s hard… to think…”

“Come on, keep trying,” I urged him while I elbowed a thing like a velociraptor in the chest and threw it into a group that were ganging up on Smokescreen. He turned to mist to slip away from them and gave me a nod.

The creatures were starting to back away as we pressed the advantage- I found the thing that had been spewing fire all over, all covered in dark scales, and followed Needler’s Thinker power to punch it in the armpit. It collapsed with a squeal, and I gave it a kick for good measure. The horde backed up further, retreating as I swung my flail around, hissing and snarling. A thing at the back with sharp quills growing on its arms flicked a wrist at me, and I slapped the quills out of the air before they could hit me.

Oozy Lover stepped forward from his place on the grass, purple slime dripping away to reveal a fat man with fair hair and beard. “Oozy Lover!” He bellowed. “That’s my name!” He slapped himself in the face once, twice, and shook himself like a dog shaking off water, eyes sharpening and focusing. “Oozy Lover’s back, baby!”

“Holy shit, he did it!” Tock Tick crowed. “Way to go, man!”

The quill creature turned at his words, hissed, and flung both arms out. A bunch of quills thudded into Oozy Lover’s chest and face. He gurgled wetly, and keeled over backward into his own slime with a splat. I saw his corpse already greying out in bloodsight- he was gone.

I bounded forward with a roar, shoving through the horde, and punched the quill creature so hard half its teeth came out. Claws scraped my armour- I turned and snapped the wrist of the thing that did it, then ducked a kick from a hoof and punched the next one in the groin. Every insect I had descended on the horde, attacking with renewed fury. Pain blasts lashed out, rapid-fire, throwing the creatures off fast enough for me to smash them senseless.

Some time later, every remaining creature was on the ground, groaning, mewling, or making little bubbling noises. “Help me drag them,” I snarled, grabbing two by the ankles and hauling them into the parking lot.

“What are we doing with them?” Clean-Cut asked.

“There’s containment foam sprayers in the vans,” Briar Patch said. “We’ll foam them and move on.” Vines burst from her skin to wrap some of the bigger ones. She used the movement to move closer to me. “Oozy Lover? Who was he?”

“Some minor villain years ago. He had a serious grudge against the Teeth, put up quite a fight. The Butchers were more impressed than angry. And the poor bastard came back from the grave just to get killed again in under a day.”

Briar Patch winced. “Yikes.”

“Yeah.”

“But now we know it’s possible to clone someone back from the dead,” Flinch said as I turned back to haul more of the creatures. “This is huge. If other villains find out about this, they’ll all want to try.”

Tactical shuddered. “Imagine fuckers like Dark Society with an army.” I dumped another creature in the parking lot with a grimace.

“Imagine if someone tries to resurrect the worst ones,” Nemean said. “It’s a good thing we made sure there wasn’t anything left of Jack.”

I almost vomited at the thought. “Oh fuck.”

My earpiece buzzed. “Armsmaster to all points, requesting urgent backup! At Rena Park!”

“East of here,” Bearskin said at once. “Down on North Harvard Street.”

“And right by Hooker Street,” Rotter snickered.

“Not the fucking time,” Quarrel snapped.

“Movers, go!” Briar Patch ordered at once. “We’ll finish up and follow in the van! Move, move!”

I dropped the creature I was carrying and drew my sword again. “Mount up! Undersiders, with me!” I pulled in my insects, cramming them into my storage compartments and in every spare crevice.

As soon as people were in the saddle, I gestured with my sword and teleported down the road, breaking into a sprint across the rooftops. There was one upside to Firecracker’s teleport being so distinctive- it made it way easier for me to lead the way, my team and allies following in my wake.

Rena Park was a little slice of grass and trees next to a library and a church. The Butchers had occasionally bought weed from a guy who hung around there.

It was a lot less pleasant with several dozen monsters converging on it, plus a tree that had sprouted teeth at the top of its trunk and several vines that were lashing out, snatching up anything in reach.

I teleported in and slashed the vine off as it made a grab for a member of Super Magic Dream Parade- I thought his name was Magic Knight Crash. The vine blew green sap for a second, then scabbed over, swelled, and burst with three new vines. I slashed again, only this time with Rotter’s decay, and the vine blackened and withered instead.

“Thanks!”

“His costume’s fucking stupid,” Butcher said. I agreed, even as I unleashed insects and started laying into the creatures. The guy had four belts, a top with no sides, and his weapon was a spiked shield mounted on an engine; all in green and purple. He revved the engine with one of the two handles, and then shot forward, slamming into something part giraffe and part bird.

I spotted Stampede in the middle of his crowd of duplicates trampling over a couple of creatures, and Loggerhead hurling harpoons at some of the creatures. The harpoons stuck fast, and Loggerhead hauled them in no matter how hard they struggled- once he planted his feet, he was effectively immovable.

“Elpis! Get him!”

I didn’t turn my head to look, too busy slicing through the vines and chopping at the tree that was dumping a dead creature into its mouth, but I drew insects together into an ‘eye’ to see what Armsmaster was shouting about.

Armsmaster was swinging from tree to tree with the grappling hook of his halberd, launching himself into the air to try and hit something flying through the air. At first I thought it was a flier with silver scales.

Then I realised the silver was metal armour, styled like a knight, with a frog’s mouth helm and a cross on the chest. The person aimed downward with both hands and fired off a volley of energy bolts.

“That’s Saint,” Muramasa said.

“The fool who got all this started,” Vladimir hissed.

I rammed my sword into the tree, pouring Rotter’s decay into it like oily poison. The tree convulsed and made a gurgling noise as its innards rotted inside its trunk, before I ripped the sword out again and sheathed it, turning to get my eyes on Saint as he buzzed through the air.

“Little man in a tin can,” Needler sneered at the Tinker.

“And we’re the can opener,” Stoneknapper finished as I flexed my claws and teleported.

Chapter 145: 14.9

Chapter Notes

After severe criticism, this chapter has been rewritten as of 08/06/2026.

14.9

Friday 30th June, East Allston, Boston

I teleported right above Saint in a ball of fire, claws out. I slammed into him like a meteor, clamping my hands around Saint’s shoulders as he jerked and spun in midair, trying to throw me off. Stoneknapper’s power fizzed in my palms, poured from my fingertips, and stopped. There was some kind of resistance around the armour, preventing me from affecting it. I tried his visor, his joints, and even the thrusters on his back keeping him aloft, but everything was blocked off.

“God fucking damn it!” Stoneknapper roared.

I bunched up a fist as Saint bucked and dipped, and slammed into the metal over his kidneys. There was a loud clang, and Saint yelled in pain. The armour hadn’t broken, but there was a small dent in the outer layer. Whatever Saint was using to shield himself from the matter shaping, it didn’t block kinetic energy. I set insects crawling from my armour to his, looking for any gaps at all- they struggled to cling to what felt like smooth glass, but enough stayed on.

“The old fashioned way then,” Butcher rumbled with vicious glee.

I managed to hook my claws around the edge of an armour panel as Saint threw himself around like a rodeo bull, and slammed another punch into his back. Saint howled in pain and flipped up, hands and feet pointing at the sky.

“Ah crap,” Anchorage said as Saint fired his thrusters, throwing us back down to the ground. I held on until the last second, teleporting away and into a knot of creatures that the others were dealing with. Claws and decay and pain made short work of them.

“Go help the others!” I shouted to Rabbit Punch and Mystic Knight Impaler. They both nodded and raced off, him with a super-strong leap, her brandishing the drill bits on each arm.

Armsmaster leapt on Saint as he climbed out of the crater he’d made and tried to get airborne again, the halberd reassembling itself into a wrecking ball that slammed into Saint’s stomach. Another grunt of pain came from him, and Armsmaster pressed the attack, shifting his halberd back and attacking with blade, point, hook and haft.

“Goddamn, did Saint say something about his mother?” Bearskin marvelled. Armsmaster had always fought with skill and reserve, but he looked furious now, snarling with every thrust and swipe.

“No idea, let’s kick Saint’s ass and find out,” I said, charging forward as I drew my flail.

Saint saw me coming and raised an arm to fire a burst of energy bolts at me. I weaved through them, an ant on his wrist letting me know where the shots were aimed, and whipped the flail forward. Saint was forced to throw himself backwards with his boot thrusters, and Armsmaster took the opening to ram the point of his halberd into the cross on Saint’s chest. I saw it leave a gash as Armsmaster pulled back.

“He’s taking damage, get in there!” Quarrel shouted.

I reeled the flail back in as I closed, whirling it around in fast arcs. Saint gave ground again, firing at me and Armsmaster, firing his thrusters again, rising off the ground.

A glowing rod tumbled end over end through the air and exploded in a cloud of fire and sparks, knocking Saint back to the ground. Dynamite Warrior Dash Fantastic formed another couple of sticks in her hands, tossing another at Saint and the other at a creature that had unhinged its jaw to snap at Smokescreen. Saint shot the stick coming at him in midair, detonating it with a bang, while the other stick stuck in the creature’s throat. It had just enough time to stick its paws in to try and fish it out when the explosion took its head off.

“Woah-ho-ho, brutal!” Firecracker laughed.

I teleported behind Saint and swung the flail into his shoulder, then ducked low and grabbed his ankle as he stumbled, flinging him head-over-heels. Armsmaster leapt and stabbed down as Saint hit the ground, driving the point of his halberd into the back of Saint’s hand. Saint howled; bloodsight showed that the point had just barely broken through the armour and gone into his flesh.

“Call off the creatures!” Armsmaster snarled. “It’s over, Saint!”

Saint pawed at the halberd with his good hand. “You’ve no idea what’s at sake!” He yelled back, tugging fruitlessly at the halberd’s shaft.

“What could possibly be worth all this?” I demanded, reeling the flail back in and raising it. If he tried anything, I’d break his leg.

“The world,” Saint growled. He let go of the halberd and flicked his wrist- a glass vial fell from a compartment on his wrist into his hand, and he crushed it in his hand, clapping his palm to his helmet and smearing the liquid all over himself.

“What’s that smell?” Nemean asked as I caught a whiff of something. “It’s delicious…”

A chorus of screeches, howls and bellows echoed off the buildings as every single creature disengaged from their fights and charged towards Saint in a mad rush.

Pheremones. Blasto used them to keep his creatures controlled. That vial must have contained some kind of attack signal, to protect Saint and kill everything around him.

“Keep him pinned!” I barked, dropping the flail to draw my sword and my axe, setting them to maximum vibration. I met the charge head-on, pulling in every insect I had to assist me.

I tried to avoid lethal force on anything human enough, but most of the creatures were strange mixes of mammal and bird and reptile and plant. I lopped the head off a thing with eyes on its shoulders, pushed off its corpse as it dropped, and spun to cut down a few more. I popped the blades from my armour to cut as much as I could, and blasted the troublesome ones with pain. Something caught on my cape, and I let it go, kicking backwards to crush a skull, before revving the saw on my leg as I kicked forward to lop off a leg.

“Hell yeah!” Tock Tick crowed, uncharacteristically bloodthirsty. “Let’s shred these fuckers!”

There were too many for me to handle them all, but Saint’s gamble had concentrated all the creatures into a single point and given the heroes a second to rally, which they did magnificently. Lady Photon, Bastion and Briar Patch threw up barriers between Saint and the horde, and the rest attacked from the flanks, the dogs tearing great chunks out of the scrum.

Blood splashed across me all over, and Vladimir’s power absorbed it all, leaving me clean as I used the speed boost to spin on one foot, shredding everything around me, then split a crocodilian creature from head to groin with my axe and beheaded something with three arms and a narwhal horn.

It was a meat grinder of a fight, and that was the perfect environment for the Butcher.

One creature broke through the line, even as Brandish hacked one of its legs off. It stumbled forward, bleating from its goat head, and threw itself at Armsmaster. I had insects chewing at its eyes, and Brandish cut the other leg off as it leapt, but it came close enough that Armsmaster had to lean backwards to avoid its hoof-like fist.

That changed the angle of his halberd, and Saint grabbed it again, pushing up with a yell of pain, firing both his guns. Armsmaster took the bolts right in the chest and fell back with a bellow, armour scorched, while Saint’s thrusters engaged again, rocketing him away. Armsmaster rolled to his feet with a curse, hurling his halberd after Saint. The shot was wide, and the weapon teleported back to his hand a moment later.

I stabbed behind me to kill another creature and teleported after him with a roar, putting myself in his path. Saint swerved to avoid me, my axe glancing off his shoulder as I fell. I landed on the roof of a building, cracking the concrete on the edge. I broke into a sprint, sticking my weapons back into my belt to keep my hands free as I chased after him.

“Elpis!” I focused insects above rather than waste precious momentum turning my head. Glory Girl was catching up, one arm outstretched. “Take my hand!”

I veered to the side and leapt off the side of the building, clamping my hand around her forearm. She grasped back, hard enough to leave fingerprints in my armour, then poured on the speed to close the gap. Saint had a good lead, but one hand was injured, and that affected his stability, forcing him to take it slower or risk crashing.

I pushed my claws to their limit, keeping an eye on Saint as he raced over the rooftops of Allston, trying to lose us. “I’m teleporting on three. Hit him as soon as you can, don’t wait for me.”

“Got it,” Glory Girl replied.

“One.” Saint took a sudden turn, and Glory Girl followed, me swinging out to the side like a pendulum. “Two.” I readied my grappler, the panels on my forearm folding aside to let the mechanism out. “Three!”

I aimed the teleport ahead of Saint again, right in his flight path. He tried to swerve away again, but this time I fired the grappler, catching him on the waist. I grabbed the line with both hands and hauled myself up, simultaneously reeling it in as Saint dipped in the air- I didn’t want to be dragged across the road. Saint clawed at the grappler with his hands, trying to pry it off as I swarmed up the cord towards him, but I got a hand on his wrist before he could break it off.

I hit him with pain, and Saint shrieked, arms and legs flailing. We suddenly tumbled through the air, slamming into the side of a building. I had a brief thought that it might not have been the best idea to hit the person controlling the flight with a taser, before we veered back the other way. I grabbed Saint’s other arm and hooked a foot around his knee, blades grinding against his armour, then smashed my head into that stupid tin-can helmet of his.

Saint cried out, and we veered again, not as bad as before. He turned his legs, and we did a barrel roll as we shot down a street.

“Whee!” Dirty Rotter cackled.

Glory Girl was catching up, almost close enough to touch Saint. I couldn’t let go of his arms to try and break his thrusters, so I squeezed my fingers as hard as I could, trying to break his armour through sheer grip strength. The feeling of buckling metal and cracking polymers was my reward. It had been a long time since any Butcher had to muscle through a physical object instead of sculpting it aside, but it was always an option.

Saint roared and threw himself to the side, slamming me into another building. We clipped a window, and I heard glass break and a woman scream. All it did was make me angry- I headbutted him again.

“Aargh! Enough!” The cross on Saint’s chest suddenly lit up with blue light. Danger sense flared.

It felt like being slapped by a giant hand- I was smashed backward into the brickwork, my armour dented. It definitely felt like a rib or two had broken as well. I just headbutted him again as Glory Girl finally caught up and slammed a haymaker into Saint’s helmet.

Saint dropped out of the air like a stone, and Glory Girl grabbed me by the arm before I could plummet. I slapped a hand to my armour, popping the dents out with Stoneknapper’s power. The ribs would take a bit longer to fix. “Thanks.”

“Let’s get this asshole,” Glory Girl said, taking us down to street level.

Civilians were fleeing the area at once, cars racing away or turning back the way they’d come, while those on foot ducked into stores or down alleyways. In a matter of seconds, the street was clear, although I spotted people sticking their phones up from behind cover to record everything.

Saint struggled to his feet woozily. “This is too important,” he ground out, “For you to stop.”

“You’re crazy,” I scoffed.

“And going down,” Glory Girl snarled, shifting into a floating fighting stance.

Saint’s arms came up, but we’d already started moving. Glory Girl’s forcefield stopped the shot that hit her, and she ducked behind me as I powered forward to claw at Saint’s helmet. He dodged back, sloppily, still firing. I heard glass shatter and metal dent as cars around me were hit.

“Three!” I shouted, hoping Glory Girl would understand as I teleported behind Saint, hooking my arms around his elbows and yanking them behind his back, keeping the guns angled away from me. Glory Girl took the opportunity to zip forward and clamp her hands on either side of Saint’s helmet. She planted her feet on top of his boots too, pinning him in place as she started slowly pulling the helmet off. Bits in the neck of the armour popped and clicked as they gave way.

“Bet she can squeeze hard enough to make his brains come out like toothpaste,” Butcher urged.

“You’re disgusting,” Flinch said.

“Tear some of his armour off at least,” Needler chimed in. “Those guns should come loose.”

I agreed, quickly shifting one hand to the barrel of the gun and twisting. Saint’s arm was forced along with the movement, and he yelled in pain even as he thrashed in our grip. I felt the metal giving way, warping and bending, and then all at once it tore off. Suddenly the metal of it all popped into my senses, the fine alloys and wiring and circuit boards.

Unfortunately that meant I wasn’t holding Saint’s arm anymore. He whipped his arm forward, palm lighting up, and shot Glory Girl in the chest.

That did nothing, her forcefield tanking the shot- then he flexed his hand and a blade popped out from his wrist. Glory Girl quickly flew upward, still holding onto his head like she was a tethered balloon, but that let Saint twist around and try to fire at me with his palm. I grabbed his hand in mine and squeezed as hard as I could, even as the blast went off and heat scorched my fingers. Judging by Saint’s scream, he still got the worse of it.

“Both hands hurt, possible concussion, and the damn fool still won’t let up,” Vladimir snorted. “Knock him out properly and have done with it.”

I grabbed the other gun and twisted a lot harder. Saint yelled as his elbow was forced almost to the breaking point, and as soon as the second gun was torn away, I grabbed his wrist again so he couldn’t try another palm blast.

“God damn it!” Saint bellowed. “Fine, take this!”

The thrusters on his back gave off a whine as they glowed with sudden light- then they detached from his armour and clattered to the ground, the whine growing in pitch and volume. I felt a rising throb from danger sense.

“They’re bombs!” Vladimir yelled.

“They’re gonna blow!” I yelled, stomping on the backs of both Saint’s knees to force him to the ground and blasting him with pain as I slammed a haymaker into the side of his helmet. He went over with a scream, clutching at his head, but my focus was on the thrusters. If they were strong enough to let a grown man in armour jet around, they could have enough force to turn the street into a crater.

“I’ll get them in the air,” Glory Girl said, snatching them out of my hands and rocketing straight upward. I could still hear the rising whine as she got to fifty feet and hurled the thrusters straight up. I followed the thrusters as they went up, up, up, reached their peak and started to fall-

The blast blinded me for a second, a flash of blue-white light and a colossal boom. Car alarms went off all around, people screamed, dogs and cats started yowling. I blinked rapidly to clear my vision as Glory Girl landed beside me. “Holy crap, that was close.”

Saint groggily raised a hand and pointed it at me- I snarled and grabbed his fingers, then rammed them backwards. Something broke, and he screamed. “Help me get him out of his armour,” I said to Glory Girl, drawing my sword.

“Let’s pop this oyster,” Dirty Rotter growled.

Glory Girl nodded and put her finger to her ear. “One sec. This is Glory Girl with Elpis- we’ve got Saint pinned, we’re peeling him out of his armour now- I don’t know our address, it’s right over where that explosion was.”

I pinned Saint to the ground with one booth and set my sword to maximum vibration, slowly pressing it into the top of the cross on his chest and dragging it down. I knew the blade was going to be wrecked after this, but my strength let me guide it straight down, and Saint was finally holding still. Maybe he was afraid of what would happen if he moved too much right now.

When I reached the bottom of the cross, I pulled the sword away, and Glory Girl leapt in, digging her fingers into the cut and pulling the sides apart with a squeal of tortured metal. Broken circuits popped and sparked as the chestplate slowly opened. I checked the sword’s edge- absolutely ruined- and sheathed it again, before crouching to place a hand against Saint’s armour.

There was still the same resistance blocking Stoneknapper’s power from working- then Glory Girl heaved another inch, some component let out a loud crack and a puff of smoke, and suddenly I could feel Saint’s armour under my fingers.

“Gotcha,” Stoneknapper grinned.

I poured the fizz into the metal and peeled the metal off Saint’s right arm like the skin off a banana. “All over now,” I said, dropping the peel on the ground and starting on the other one.

“You have no idea what’s at stake here,” Saint said, almost pleading, as I shucked the armour off his left arm and began tearing chunks off his torso. “I have to finish this, to protect everyone.”

“You’re delusional,” Glory Girl said, crushing a hunk of circuitry in her hand.

My insects picked up the approach of Cerberus on her dog, along with a rider in armour. Armsmaster didn’t even wait for the dog to land before he leapt off, rolled as he landed and came up running over to us. “Saint,” he growled.

“He really is furious with him,” Vladimir noted. “I suppose Saint got under his skin somehow.”

By this point all that was left of Saint’s costume was his dented helmet and the jumpsuit he’d worn underneath, lined with circuitry and connectors. “Armsmaster,” he said with a groan. “Did she send you?”

Armsmaster’s snarl deepened. “No. But you and I are going to have a very long talk, and you are going to give me some answers, even if I have to squeeze them out of you.”

“Okay, wow, that sounds like something we’d say,” Quarrel admitted.

“I’ll call for a transport and take him back to HQ,” Armsmaster said. “The three of you should go and rejoin the fight. The Ambassadors are closing in on Blasto’s lab.”

“Anyone else feel like Armsmaster’s going to try and beat Saint up as soon as we’re out of sight?” Tock Tick asked with a nervous laugh.

“He’s in control,” Tactical shrugged. “Anyway, we don’t have time to worry about it. If Blasto’s almost finished, he might try something desperate. They’re going to need us for whatever big sack of ugly he turns out.”

I nodded, agreeing both inward and outward. “Let’s get cracking. Can’t let the Ambassadors have all the fun.”

Chapter 146: Interlude 14.E

Chapter Notes

See the end of the chapter for notes

Friday 30th June, East Allston, Boston

“Shit shit shit shit shit!” Rey chanted to himself as he checked the security cameras for the umpteenth time.

Accord’s Ambassadors were basically right on the doorstep- he recognised Lizardtail, massive reptilian arms tearing into the minions he’d set to guard his lab, and Cassiterite, hurling black stars that bounced around until they hit something, where they turned into big spikes that shish-kebabed whatever they hit. There was a guy popping up out of the ground, spikes of rock following him to corral and impale the creatures.

Fuck, this had got so out of control. At first it had felt like everything was coming up Blasto; first Accord’s deal to provide him with an index of parahuman DNA- who’d have refused that? With such powerful samples, his creations could advance to levels beyond anything he’d ever created- stuff that’d make the Woad Giant look like a child’s plaything.

Then the Dragonslayers had come to him, asking for help, with full copies of the Bonesaw files that had got leaked onto the web. Rey had only managed to get a couple of pages before they got scrubbed, but the full documents were like promethean fire to his power. Trigger event studies, the effects of key memories, how powers could vary between different subjects- he could imbue his creations with full powers, full intelligence, make them properly loyal to him instead of training them with pheromones.

And the Dragonslayers had brought the tech to get started, stolen from that smug bitch Cranial at Toybox. The thought of getting one over on the stuck up cow who’d sneered at his own attempts to implant memories into homunculus servants had been too good to resist.

On screen, one of those homunculi, a thing made of a mix of his own DNA and chimpanzee, was caught in a bubble of golden light by a woman in a yellow dress and mask. In seconds, the air inside the bubble filled with heat, and the homunculus caught fire.

Okay, so he’d gone a little overboard, a little too eager to stretch his muscles and push the envelope. And maybe he’d been distracting himself from his latest breakup with Apple, and sort of hoping that she’d come back if he did something really impressive.

But that shouldn’t have been enough to bring the fucking Butcher back to Boston! And not just the old Butcher, oh no- the shiny new Butcher who’d plucked out Jack Slash’s eyes and fed them to him! He’d panicked then, looking for any advantage. The Dragonslayers had offered to run interference, but that hadn’t felt like enough.

And then one of Accord’s subordinates had called, offering for some Thinker support- help with a guided ambush against Butcher and her crew, so long as he tried to target Tattletale the Thinker in particular. Sounded easy enough- except it hadn’t worked! And when he’d tried to get in touch with Coil again, his phone was disconnected!

He’d thrown everything he had against the Butcher and the other reinforcements- the regular minions, the upgraded minions, even the few full clones he’d managed, specially picked from the few people he could think of that had managed to give the Butchers a hard time, like Muscular and Oozy Lover. Saint himself had taken the field to coordinate the defence while the other two checked on their payment.

And then they’d abandoned him! Bastards! Rey cursed in a mixture of English and Spanish as he watched helplessly on the monitors as the Ambassadors wore down his creatures. He still had a few more growing in tanks of high-nutrient solution, every two or three seconds another week of growth, a year every two or three minutes. If he could hold out a little longer, then the big ones could save his ass, or at least give him an escape route. Fly him out, burrow a tunnel, create a bubble of air and escape down the sewers and into the river-

The security screens suddenly darkened, like a cloud had moved in front of the sun. A second later there was a burst of fire, and then a figure in metal was hacking through the remaining minions with sword and axe, swarms of insects biting and stinging everything else. The Ambassadors fell back to mop up the edges, putting some distance between themselves and the thing carving a swathe of destruction through Blasto’s army.

Butcher was here. Rey backed away from the console, hands trembling.

He had to leave. Run away from Boston, set up somewhere Butcher wouldn’t come for him- maybe down south where the weather was warm- good climate for growing weed. He hustled around the lab, stuffing samples and seeds and scribbled notes into the many pockets of his labcoat. The index was too damn huge to take all of it, and that broke his heart, but it’d be better than Butcher breaking his spine.

The creatures in the vat were almost ready- not fast enough to help him escape, but maybe they could buy him some time. He grabbed a bottle of attack pheromones and unscrewed the spray head, splashing it thickly over the doorway. No time for half measures- first thing through that doorway would get pounced on and mauled.

For a second he hesitated- what if his creations killed the Butcher? Would he inherit?

He shook the thought away. Nah- Butcher had smashed through everything he’d thrown at her. Maybe if he’d made that Myrddin-Bastion mashup he’d thought about- that thing could have pulled a real “You shall not pass!”

He grabbed the headset the Dragonslayers had brought, cramming it into a bag along with the best samples. He could probably recreate it now that he’d seen it and used it, but it’d take forever.

The secret entrance had a hidden handle- press in on one of the bricks, let it slide out, pull it open- and there lay the long, dark, dank-smelling tunnel that was his ticket to freedom-

It was like getting hit in the face with a hot mattress. Rey fell back on his ass, bag spilling, clutching at his face. “Argh, shit, what the fuck-”

His brain made the connection to an explosion going off right in his face just as a hand grabbed him by the collar and hauled him up off his feet.

The new Butcher stared him right in the face, helmet open to show silver lenses and teeth like a shark. “There you are, you little shit.”

 

 

A couple of hours later, Rey sat in an underground cell, still damp from the shower they’d put him through to make sure he wasn’t hiding any chemical or biological substances, mind endlessly running through the same thoughts, over and over.

He was fucked. Fucked with a capital F. He was caught, disarmed, all his work destroyed. They’d found the index and the creations he’d been cooking up, and while the heroes were pissed that he’d got his hands on that index of DNA, they’d been even more pissed that he’d got his hands on Bonesaw’s research.

It wasn’t like he’d been planning on doing anything really nasty with it! He never did stuff like cut two people apart and stitch them together and implant control mechanisms into them to turn them into a puppet! Sometimes he combined people’s DNA to create a weaponised creature, but that was a very different situation!

Although he got the feeling that no matter how well he phrased it, that particular argument wouldn’t do down very well.

And now here he was. What were they going to do to him? The Birdcage? They’d eat him alive in there. Maybe they’d just send him to a regular prison- Tinkers were a lot easier to contain than other capes, provided that their cells were regularly checked for any materials they might have sneaked in.

Oh god, he’d go the rest of his life without ever really Tinkering again. Stuck in a tiny cell, in a crappy prison jumpsuit, eating shit food and being afraid to use the showers. Never to concoct some incredible fusion of DNA, never to take territory and rule it, never to lick Apple’s tattoo just one more time…

Footsteps broke him out of his miserable thoughts. Two troopers with foam sprayers, and Director Armstrong between them- Rey recognised him from TV.

“Rey Andino, aka Blasto,” Armstrong began with a face like thunder, “You’ve committed enough crimes in the past week alone for us to justify locking you up somewhere so deep and dark that you’ll never see natural daylight again.”

Rey got to his feet. “Please, god no, don’t send me to the Birdcage, I’ll never survive! I’ll do anything!” he babbled. “I can give you information on the Dragonslayers! Saint won’t talk, but I heard him say a bunch of stuff-!”

Armstrong held up a hand. “You’re not being sent to the Birdcage. Your crimes fall just short of the usual requirements. In fact, you are being offered a deal. We found copies of the Bonesaw files when we searched your lab, and while that is a mark against you, it also presents a possibility. The Chief Director thinks you might be useful in helping us to understand them and develop counters for the possibilities, preferably before some other Biotinker tries what you did on an even worse scale.”

Rey almost didn’t dare to hope. “Uh, sure, yes, absolutely. I’d be happy to help.”

“Good. But let me make something clear, Blasto.” Armstrong leaned forward, a little closer to the glass separating them, glare cranking up a few notches. “You disgust me. You and your creatures have terrorised this city for far too long. The amount of damage you’ve done over the years is enormous. If it were up to me, you’d already be on your way to a para-max prison. As it happens, I was overruled. However, you set so much as one toe out of line, and I will use that to recommend you be put somewhere extremely uncomfortable. Do you understand?”

Rey nodded rapidly. “You’ve got me by the short and curlies. Got it, message received.”

Armstrong straightened up, still scowling. “Good. We’ll send someone in later to get as much information as you can give on other supervillains in Boston- particularly the Dragonslayers. You’re right that Saint isn’t talking- although I’m sure you wouldn’t guess why.”

 

 

Boston PRT HQ, Downtown Boston

“How do you feel?”

Dragon considered the question carefully. “Conflicted,” she said at last.
