Elpis never announced her outings, presumably to give villains less time to attack Brockton Bay while she was away, but eventually March got an alert on social media showing that Elpis had just helped take down a drug ring in Rhode Island. Based on what she’d worked out by stalking Elpis’s media appearances, she’d be occupied giving a few quick soundbites to the press, making sure the criminals were locked up, and touching base with the local heroes, before setting off back to Brockton Bay. That gave March a good six hour window when the city was guaranteed to be Elpis-free, maybe more if there was traffic.

Of course that would be reduced significantly if the Undersiders managed to get a message to their leader, who would probably hit triple digit speeds on her way back to her home to deliver terrible violence to whoever was stirring up trouble in her home territory.

And there were the other heroes to handle- New Wave had several fliers, the Undersiders had their dogs to ride on, and one of the Wards was apparently a speed Tinker who’d upgraded all the PRT’s vehicles for faster response times. She’d accounted for that, but it would still be best to avoid them.

No time to waste then. March got up off the motel bed and grabbed her go-bag as she headed out the door. A quick slide down the banister instead of taking the stairs saved her a few seconds, and she jogged to her little moped, swinging herself onto the seat and starting the engine in one practiced movement.

She briefly stopped in an alley along the way to put on her hat and mask, and clip her new rapier to her belt. She already had the rest of her costume on under her civilian clothes, because no way was she going to strip down in an alleyway in February. In total it took her seven minutes from the motel to the little shop just off the newly rebuilt Boardwalk, right next to a cute little coffee shop and a jewellery store.

The bell over the door jangled as March shouldered it open. The girl behind the counter looked up, all black curls and pretty eyes. “Good-!” She stopped mid-sentence at the sight of March, of her military uniform and feathered cap, rabbit mask and drawn sword.

Three mannequins lunged at March all at once, all wearing fashionable outfits. March sidestepped one and slashed its leg, cut along the arm of another, then flicked the tip of her rapier across the chest of the third, stepping around them to advance further into the store. The mannequins wavered for a second, holes in the fabric interfering with Parian’s power, before they sealed up, extra thread concealed inside repairing the damage. They straightened up, ready to continue the fight.

Then they exploded- leg, arm and chest. The blasts tore them into scraps, and Parian stumbled back with a yelp. March took two steps forward and pressed the tip of her rapier under Parian’s chin.

“You’re going to pull out your phone and call Flechette for me,” March said sweetly. “You’ll tell her to meet us at a specific address, and then leave it here. You won’t try to fight me or signal anyone. Do that, and you’ll get out of this alive.”

Parian’s big dark eyes flicked from the sword to March’s mask, and narrowed angrily. “You’re March.”

“I am,” March said cheerfully. “Did she tell you about me?”

“She said you’re the crazy stalker who went through every villain group in New York trying to attack her.”

“Hm.” March shrugged. “Well, there’s more to it than that.”

“…I notice you’re not denying the crazy part.”

“Well, I can see how people might think that from an outside perspective,” March conceded.  “But in a very real way, I’m incredibly sane. Now, enough stalling. Take your phone out. Slowly.”

 

 

The Trainyards

March flicked her sword along the wall as she ran past, slashed another mark into the ground as she turned the corner, and then sprinted along a straight run. A few seconds later she heard the explosions right on cue, one after the other, with the largest at the end.

Unfortunately there weren’t any shouts of surprise or screams of pain, which meant that her mine marks hadn’t managed to catch her pursuit. Possibly they’d found some way to detect her marks, or maybe they were just being cautious after she’d managed to blow Ironclad’s foot off. Hopefully their caution would make them fall back and let her get some distance to think of her next move.

Her next move was increasingly starting to look like retreat. The heroes had responded far faster than she’d expected, and had cut through her countermeasures and misdirections with disturbing ease. She’d covered her tracks, laid false trails, searched Parian for tracking devices, and yet they kept homing in on her!

She glanced up at a crane nearby. Maybe she could just cut the whole thing down and use the distraction to run.

Barking off in the distance informed her decision. She could certainly kill Cerberus’s dogs, but Whirlygig and Grue were a bad match up for her- she couldn’t slice her way through Whirlygig’s storm, and Grue’s darkness would throw off her timing. She burst from cover, sprinting towards the crane.

A steel bolt embedded itself in the ground right at her feet, at just the right angle and height to catch her feet as she ran. She tripped, tucked and rolled, sprang back to her feet, and despite the pain of little bits of gravel digging into her shoulders and arms, March was grinning now. That was one of Flechette’s bolts- she’d come after all. Maybe there was still a chance to steal her away.

Another bolt planted itself in front of her, but March knew Flechette’s timing from all their old battles- how long it took her to draw another needle, crank her arbalest, load and aim and fire. She had the rhythm down, and jumped a little higher to clear it. Almost at the crane now.

“Gotcha!” Someone shouted. March glanced up and saw Newter crawling down the crane towards her, orange skin glistening with sweat. She’d seen him work- one droplet would put her down.

She dragged her sword through the gravel, flicked some of it up at Newter. He backed up, using his tail like an extra limb to climb, which saved him when the little bits of gravel detonated, just enough that they would have maimed him if he’d been near.

Next bolt from Flechette coming right now- March spun to the side, slashing her sword across the crane’s leg as the third bolt landed right where her foot had been. She turned the spin into a run, perpendicular to before, slashing another leg of the crane as she did.

Three, two, one, first mark detonated, two, one, second mark detonated. There was a groaning and creaking of metal as the crane’s legs gave out and it began to slowly overbalance, struts buckling as it tipped towards the ground. Even better than she’d hoped for- loud and slow meant that the heroes would take notice of it and move to clear the area. If it had been fast and quiet she might have killed a few, but deterrence was better for now.

Might kill Newter if he didn’t jump off fast enough.

There was an almighty crash as the crane fell on top of an empty train car- the car buckled, the crane broke in two over it. March kept running, heading for a little gap between two more train cars. Past that were a couple of buildings, and past those was the nearest road. Fight past whoever was watching the perimeter, steal a car, disappear into the city, get out of town and plan the next attempt. Maybe next time she’d just wait for Flechette to leave town on a mission and snatch her up then.

There was an explosion off in the distance. A few seconds later there was another.

March recognised the timing of those explosions as a third echoed across the trainyards. She’d studied videos to know what to listen for, but she’d thought she had at least a couple more hours!

A low buzzing joined the explosions, like strings beneath a drumbeat. March pushed herself to her limit, panting as she ran as fast as she could. Just get to the cars, then the buildings, then the road-

Something shoved hard at her back, knocking her off balance. At the same time, a metal rod jammed itself into the ground right by her foot. She was off-balance, off her rhythm- she went over like a tree, barely managing to catch herself on her arms instead of getting a face full of gravel. Her sword slipped from her grip and clattered over the ground.

There was a louder explosion from a few feet behind her, and then a voice with a metallic echo said, “Time to stop running, rabbit.”

March pulled a punch dagger from a hidden pocket in her costume and rolled over to face Elpis. Butcher XV had the air cannon on her left arm extended out, pointed directly at March. Despite her helmet being closed, March got the impression she was scowling.

A thick cloud of insects caught up to her, buzzing and clicking as they formed into a handful of human silhouettes on either side of Elpis, fireflies lighting up in their faces to simulate eyes. Past that, a ring of insects formed up in the sky, with an arrow in the centre pointing down.

“Well, congratulations,” said one silhouette in a New York accent. “You’re the first one to try anything this stupid in our town.”

“Did you really think we didn’t have plans for this crap?” said another in a Boston accent.

“How the fuck did you get here so fast?” March demanded, scrabbling to her feet, palming a handful of gravel as she did so.

“Broke a lot of traffic laws,” Elpis said offhandedly. “Beyond that, I’m not telling the details.”

March slipped her power into the gravel. “Well, then I guess this conversation’s-” She hurled the handful of gravel at Elpis and ran as fast as she could toward the train cars, drawing her other punch dagger as she ran.

Overlapping explosions from behind her- the rapid crackle of the gravel and the thunderclap of Elpis dodging it. It took her a few seconds between teleports, that gave March just enough time-

The space between the train cars was filling up, the metal walls turning to marble with intricate engravings. The walls extended down to the ground- no sliding under the cars. This had to be Labyrinth. March glanced up, looking for a handhold, and saw Newter perched above, hair in a mess and a colourful bruise on his shoulder. He stuck his tongue out at her.

March cursed and rammed her punch daggers into the marble wall, slicing a square shape out of the wall, the explosive mark bleeding into it. She turned and stepped back to a safe distance, keeping an eye on Elpis, who had drawn a sword.

The marks exploded, but instead of the sound of stone cracking and breaking, there was a single loud explosion. March looked back in time to see the entire structure vanish from existence, leaving a white void in its place. There was no depth or dimension to it- it could only be perceived by the edges. She could feel a gentle breeze as air was sucked into it.

“What the hell did you do?” March heard Newter shout from behind the void.

“That’s a very good question,” Elpis said from right behind her. She spun around, daggers lashing out-

Pain hit her- agonising, excruciating pain through every part of her. It was like being electrocuted, or set on fire, or having her blood turn to acid. She screamed, knees giving out as she fell to the ground. Something hit her in the head, and everything went black.

 

 

Friday 3rd February, PRT Headquarters

“So now there’s an interdimensional portal in the Trainyards,” Director Piggot said, leaning back in her seat. “There doesn’t seem to be any way to close it, and word is already getting out. The good news is that it leads to an alternate world that appears to be uninhabited, so we don’t have to worry about diplomacy, and there’s already talk of moving people throughto take advantage of a literal planet’s worth of resources. It’s been designated Earth Gimel.”

“The bad news,” she continued, “Is that there’s now a literal planet’s worth of resources sitting on the other side of the portal we can’t close. I can imagine plenty of villains might want to disappear into the wilderness for a few weeks to escape justice.”

Sabah had a sudden image of some villain, all black leather and spikes, sitting by a campfire toasting marshmallows on a skewer. The thought almost made her smile.

Now wasn’t the time for that though. Besides Director Piggot and Dauntless at the end of the table, there was Elpis and Grue on one side, Sarah- Lady Photon, Brandish and herself on the other, and the mercenaries Faultline and Shamrock at the other end.

“There might also be groups that would want to set up permanent settlements there,” Lady Photon pointed out. “We saw how Lost Garden were essentially living in their own little forest- I can imagine plenty of people might want to isolate themselves from the rest of civilisation.”

“Probably some groups would want a bit of both,” Elpis said, sipping her bottle of Legend-berry drink. Sabah wasn’t sure if she was drinking it just for the irony or if she actually liked the taste. Getting to know the girl beneath the armour, and to a lesser extent the other Butchers, had given Sabah more insight, but sometimes Elpis was just as much of a puzzle as the day she’d first walked into Sabah’s shop. “Whether they’d actually survive or just die of exposure is another matter. Regardless, we’re going to need to sort out security for the portal. The Undersiders are willing to help. Cerberus’s dogs would be excellent for scouting the new Earth.”

“New Wave will likewise help,” Lady Photon agreed. “The portal’s an enormous opportunity for the city.” Brandish nodded agreement.

Director Piggot nodded. “Thank you. As for Faultline, the PRT is officially extending an offer for you to create further portals in other cities. I understand you’ve recruited another member who’d be able to help.”

“Eraser, yes,” Faultline said. “Tattletale and Elpis checked- his power works across dimensions, so combined with Labyrinth, he should be able to open more portals.”

Piggot nodded. “Good. We’ll contact you with further details regarding which cities, specific locations, and of course pay, but I can assure you that you’ll be well compensated.”

Since nobody else seemed to be wondering, Sabah cautiously raised a hand. “Um. How did they confirm his power works across dimensions? Did they create another portal already?”

“No, not yet,” Elpis said. “Eraser’s power looks like matter deletion- random spherical bursts around him that remove whatever’s in the area. But Tattletale noticed they weren’t affecting the ground- the burst should have scooped a chunk out of the ground, but it didn’t. When we pried up a chunk of asphalt, we found totally different rock underneath. His power doesn’t delete matter, it swaps it for an empty space in another dimension, with a caveat for keeping level ground intact. So, cutting and switching areas of space, plus Labyrinth’s power blending parts of different dimensions, equals easy portals.”

Sabah nodded slowly. “Right.” It still sounded utterly crazy, but she felt like she understood somewhat better.

Was nobody else feeling as thrown by this development as she was? They all seemed to be taking it in stride that there was a door to another world in Brockton Bay. Maybe it was just her. Even after months of training with New Wave, sparring and a few real fights, even the Endbringer battles, she still felt like the new girl, helplessly trying to catch up.

It was a familiar feeling- coming to America as a child, having to learn English, lagging behind everyone else when they talked about American TV and music and films. And when she’d become a cape, she couldn’t understand everyone else’s insistence on fighting, on lashing out. She’d just wanted to make clothes.

She understood now, after the Empire had attacked her over and over, threatened her family. But still she was trailing behind. No wonder March had come after her- she was the most vulnerable. She hadn’t thought of the security measures that had saved her- New Wave had suggested the panic button hidden under the counter, with a little ragdoll to push it for her; Panacea had given her the little vial of pheromones to make a scent trail for Cerberus’s dogs and Elpis’s insects to track. It just didn’t come easily to her.

“There’s the wildlife to consider,” Elpis was saying. “If it’s a world with no humans, there’ll be a lot of big animals that won’t know to avoid us. Bison for instance. And extinct animals too- I don’t think woolly mammoths lived in North America, but it’s possible.”

“Dodos,” said the box in front of Elpis. She’d changed it from transparent glass to plain grey metal, which was fine by Sabah- seeing all those insects crawling around in there gave her the creeps.

“We’re not crossing into another world just so you can see how they taste, Firecracker,” Elpis replied with what seemed like a roll of her eyes- at least the way the metal eyebrows on her helmet moved suggested that.

“Spoilsport.”

“Any settlers will be well briefed on possible dangers,” Director Piggot said without batting an eye at the byplay. “Research teams will go in first to confirm Earth Gimel is safe for human habitation- after that, work can begin. It shouldn’t take long- Congress is moving fast on this.” She glanced at the papers in front of her. “I think that’s everything. Any other questions?”

Lady Photon glanced at Sabah, subtly nodding towards Piggot with a questioning look. Sabah slowly nodded back. They’d discussed this in advance, and she was ready for it.

“What’s happening with March?” Lady Photon asked directly.

Piggot didn’t blink, but she saw Dauntless grimace slightly. There was a faint crackle of plastic as Elpis gripped her bottle tighter. “March is headed to a paramax facility under heavy guard. Given the long list of her crimes, the nature of her powers, and her psychological profile, she’ll be going away for a very long time. If she causes any more trouble, it’s the Birdcage.”

Under the table, Lady Photon gently patted Sabah’s hand. It helped a little.

“We’d like to discuss further security measures for Parian’s shop, if that’s possible,” Brandish said. “The silent alarm and the pheromone trail helped, but we’d prefer something more preventative. Our teammate has the right to go about her business undisturbed.”

And un-kidnapped, un-tied up with steel cable, un-forced to listen while a lunatic in a rabbit mask dreamily explained that she and Flechette were destined to be together. Sabah had lied through her teeth when March had asked if she and Flechette were dating, but March hadn’t seemed to actually care. No anger, no jealousy- the way she talked, it seemed like she viewed Sabah as a temporary distraction. The sheer oddity of it had only made a horrible situation more horrible.

“We’ll look into it, but I think March was an outlier,” Piggot pointed out. “More rational villains have steered clear of Brockton in general.”

“The fact that March got dogpiled by every hero in town will certainly warn off anyone else,” Dauntless pointed out. “Reputation is important to villains.”

“Parian doesn’t have much of a reputation on her own,” Grue said, unfolding his arms and sitting forward. “No offence,” he added, black helmet turning her way, “But I think you’re mostly seen as a part of New Wave.”

“So I’d have to, what, get in more fights to get people to leave me alone?” Parian asked despairingly.

“Not necessarily,” Elpis said, giving Grue a nudge. “Like Dauntless said, March going down hard and fast will make people reconsider. But beyond that, I don’t know. Maybe extra training, new techniques; is there anything about your power that you think could be expanded on?”

Sabah considered. Her puppets were strong and durable, and they could be quite fast- but they needed the right materials, and once they were damaged they went down fast. She also couldn’t see or hear through them, which meant she had to command them up close. More than that though, she felt like there was some material that would work better for her power. Wool and cotton were decent, silk was better, leather was best of all, but it still felt like there was another step that could be taken.

“I might have some ideas,” she admitted. “I’ll get back to you.”

“Fair enough. In the meantime, I could upgrade the security systems in your shop? Maybe an emergency exit?”

“I already have a fire door.”

“I meant more like a secret trap door to an escape tunnel,” Elpis admitted.

“Really?” Brandish asked flatly.

“Yep. For now we can run some patrols through the Boardwalk- now that the portal’s a thing, a visible hero presence is going to be more important than ever.”

“Agreed,” Director Piggot said. “On that note, Elpis; how did Chariot’s emergency teleport go?”

Elpis pulled something from her belt and set it on the table. It was a metal cylinder, blacked like it had been in a fire, and the outer casing cracked open. Through the gaps Sabah could see wires and circuitry. “It got me pretty close to Brockton Bay. Wrecked the bike’s engine though, and I’m pretty sure anyone who wasn’t a Brute would have problems. So it works fine for me, but I think it’ll need a lot of tweaking before anyone else uses it.”

Piggot nodded. “We’d like to formalise the arrangement- we provide the teleport module as partial payment for the silk quota.”

“Works for me. We can sort out the exact numbers later. If there’s nothing else, I’d like to get going. I promised to help with moving some of the train tracks.”

Chapter 155: 15.9

Thursday 17th May, Montreal, Canada

“Final comms check.”

“Cleodolinda, check.”

“Dobrynja, check.”

“Sigurd, check,” Frank finished, sitting within the cockpit of his suit. It was a hell of a lot different from when the Dragonslayers had first woken him up- the whole chassis had been rebuilt to be more compact, more agile, and the HUD had a reworked interface for him to work with.

The three suits, each 12 feet tall, were holding position two hundred feet in the air over Montreal, specifically over a neighbourhood in the suburbs. The camouflage systems he’d been working on still weren’t field-ready, but projectors installed in each suit could distort the wavelengths of the visible light around them, rendering them and the space around them a blur.

Ironically, despite the fact that they still called themselves the Dragonslayers for recognition, it was Dragon who’d led them to this moment- especially Frank. The backdoor to her systems had let him peak at her code, and from there he’d been able to understand what tech she was working on, what cases she was pursuing, what leads she’d found. Eventually he’d built an add-on to display the files she accessed rather than her internal code- far less disturbing than looking into the raw substance of a person.

Not that he was admitting that he was convinced of Dragon’s personhood in front of Mags and Mischa. Even months later they still blamed Dragon for Saint’s death, and challenging their grief could tear the team apart. Instead he’d channelled their rage into rebuilding, upgrading their suits with his tech instead of getting by on Teacher’s scraps and the occasional hired Tinker help. Propulsion systems, energy weapons, comms and shielding- it wasn’t like the old days, when Hero had had the Protectorate’s budget and resources to play with. On the other hand, a lot of mundane tech had advanced, and that made things a hell of a lot easier.

It had made it much easier to, for example, copy a complex program Dragon had got from Armsmaster and load it into a couple of compact earpieces for him and Steve. When they’d sat down with the other Cauldron members to ask what the hell that Echo girl had meant about cloning the original Wards team back to life, Doctor Mother, the Number Man, Alexandria and Eidolon had assured him that she must have been delusional. After all, she’d gone through a lot of trauma, and she’d committed suicide right after that. She was hardly a reliable witness.

Checking the program’s recordings had confirmed everything they’d said was a lie. Legend had almost fallen apart over it. Frank had just felt numb. They’d made such a show of respecting the kids, just because they knew he’d object. And if they were willing to do that, what else were they doing? Dark thoughts had occurred to them, like the Cauldron symbol on the Case 53s. Doctor Mother had always said it might be William Manton, running around and experimenting on people, framing Cauldron for it, but now they had to wonder…

“Neighbours are off to work,” Dobrynja said, helmet tilted down to watch the houses surrounding the target area. “School bus has taken the kids- Guillame, Nicholas, and Samuel are onboard.”

“Alright- follow them from above, don’t move until they’re out of reach of any potential hostages. We’ll use the jammer to make sure they don’t get any warning.”

“Copy that,” Dobrynja said, breaking formation to follow the bus. That left Frank and Mags to hover over the house.

Eventually, he and Legend had pulled themselves together and decided how to proceed. Cauldron was too powerful for them to really stop- Doormaker’s portals alone made them essentially untouchable. But there were things they could do nonetheless.

Legend could feed him intel from the Protectorate, analysis from the Think Tank, files on villains and their weaknesses. Frank, renamed as Sigurd, could return he favour with what he learned from dealings with other capes as he rebranded the Dragonslayers into whitelisters- heroic mercenaries. Both of them could keep an eye on Cauldron’s clients, and the Case 53s.

It took time, for the Dragonslayers. Their former reputation worked against them. But simple guard work and taking out minor villains became search and rescue jobs or backing up independent heroes, which turned into big legitimate jobs and cooperation with the authorities. Elpis ending the Slaughterhouse Nine had opened the door, and the Dragonslayers were following.

It was strange for Frank, to go from being one of the most famous people on the planet to being a relative unknown, but it was satisfying. Less paperwork, no politics- clear and simple objectives.

Like now. This wasn’t a job they’d been hired for, but it was a job that needed doing. It took a lot of long-range surveillance through telescopes and Tinkertech drones, a lot of analysing people through the lie detector program and other algorithms, a lot of building a web of people who’d need to be handled in a hurry, but it was finally doable. Legend had quietly contacted people in the Protectorate and Guild, as well as some thoroughly vetted police officers, and they were just waiting for the signal.

The houses on either side were empty of people- the kids were at school, the adults were at work. Minimal chance of innocent bystanders getting caught in the crossfire. Frank took a deep breath, then brought up a series of files in his HUD and sent them off to key contacts.

“Lists sent,” he said. “Mission start, mark.”

He and Mags dropped down to only 50 feet in the air, activating the tiny drone they’d slipped down the chimney. Sonar pulses mapped the house and its many occupants, revealing the one person they were looking for- a tall man with a lanky physique and long hair, currently having his feet rubbed by two women while he sipped a glass of wine. The sonar was precise enough to make out the string of wedding rings around his neck.

A targeting reticule came up, centred through the ceiling on Heartbreaker’s head, the wavelength calculated so that the beam would go through shingles and insulation and wood and plaster and stop right in the centre of his skull.

Sigurd took a deep breath and let it out slowly. Then he pulled the trigger.

A golden beam lanced out of the barrel on his right arm and into Heartbreaker’s head, boring through his skull and cooking his brain. The corpse slumped in its chair, wineglass falling to the floor.

Sigurd was already moving as the women began to scream, crashing through the roof on the other side of the room. Two cannons popped out of his shoulders, loaded with specialised stun grenades. He hired one at the women pawing desperately at the corpse of their master, begging him to come back. The burst of light was designed to overload the visual cortex and induce immediate unconsciousness without permanently damaging the eyes. They slumped over unconscious, and he charged out of the room, looking for more.

“We’re under attack!” screamed a young girl, sprinting out of a room to the right. Facial recognition threw up a name- Catena, aka Juliette Vasil. Ability to paralyse others so long as she remained motionless. A pre-programmed motion fired a stun grenade at her, and she dropped without a sound. Sigurd snapped a hand out and caught her before she could crack her head on the banister, then fired another grenade into the room she’d just come out of. Two more for each bedroom- the sonar overlay showed women and children slumping to the floor.

Mags had crashed through the living room window into the ground floor, and from the sounds of screaming and breaking furniture, she was winning handily. Anti-Master shielding, again borrowed from Armsmaster and Dragon, was keeping the Heartbroken’s powers at bay.

Another girl was coming up the stairs, carrying a leather bullwhip of all things. Downfall, aka Chastity Vasil. Ability to inflict feelings of hopelessness and despair on people she touched. A thin laser sliced the whip in two as she brandished it, and another stun grenade knocked her out. Sigurd had to lunge to grab her before she fell down the stairs.

Someone slammed into his back, and he lost his footing. Thrusters fired at once, keeping him aloft, and he steered back onto solid footing, before spinning around to throw his attacker off him.

The woman fell to the ground- she was wearing nothing but lingerie, and she was crying, her pretty face twisted in rage and grief. She must have been hiding in the bathroom. Sigurd fired another stun grenade at her feet as she tried to raise, caught her too, then lais both the girls on the carpet before thumping down the stairs.

“Sigurd, we’ve got runners!” Mags shouted over the comms. Several women were running out the front door, one carrying a little boy.

“I see them!” Sigurd fired a stun grenade after them, the effect catching them in the back, but they only stumbled, not falling. A second grenade arced over their heads and detonated on the sidewalk, which did the job- they slumped onto the front lawn. Sigurd quickly stepped outside to pull the little boy out from under the woman who’d been carrying him.

“House is cleared,” Maggs said over the comm. “Sigurd, can you help me move them?”

“Coming,” Sigurd said, hauling the fallen women and boy in his arms, servos in his suit whining. “Dobrynja, status?”

“I’ve got the targets,” Dobrynja replied after a moment. “Accidentally stunned a couple of their classmates though.”

“They should be fine,” Sigurd said, carrying his burden through the door. “Authorities will be here soon- let’s clear up and get the restraints on before then.”

 

 

“The Kill Order’s been backdated to yesterday. You officially have the credit for taking down Nikos Vasil, and the reward is yours to collect.”

Frank nodded. “That’ll be useful. Although mostly I’m just glad the bastard’s dead.”

The two of them were sat on top of a rooftop in Montreal, having a sandwich. Steve was in plain clothes instead of his Legend getup, and Frank had left the suit back at the Dragonslayers hideout.

“How’d it go with his moles?” Frank asked, taking a sip of his coffee.

Steve grimaced. “We got all the confirmed moles in time, but there was a police officer we missed. He shot three others and then himself. Two of the victims should recover, but the third was just getting off shift, didn’t have his Kevlar on…”

“Fuck,” Frank cursed.

Steve sighed heavily. “Yeah.”

The two men stared out over Montreal for a long while. “It could have been worse,” Steve said eventually. “If there’d been bombs, or if they’d been in public-”

“I know,” Frank said. “I just… Fuck.” He finished off his sandwich in a few angry bites and crumpled the wrapper into a ball. “What’s going to happen to the victims? Is there any way to deprogram them?”

Steve waved his hand in a so-so gesture. “We’re looking into it. We think the best way might be to get Cranial from Toybox to remove the memories of their time under his control, but that’s not a certainty. We can check other capes, but there’s not a lot of heroes with emotional Master powers. Still, hopefully we can at least reduce the effects. It’s a good thing you restrained them all- right now they’re having to be tied down so they don’t hurt anyone, or themselves. One of them tried to bite her wrist open when they took her cuff off.”

Frank winced. “Christ. And his kids?”

Steve grimaced. “That’s harder. There’s some talk of getting them as probationary Wards, but considering their records, that’d be difficult. Even with round the clock monitoring, we couldn’t necessarily trust them around other children, or with civilians. Maybe put them on a containment zone. We’d have to split them up too- they’re too dangerous together.”

Frank nodded. “Makes sense.”

Steve floated off his seat and into the air, stretching with a grunt. “Well, at any rate, we’ve got one of the biggest bastards of the North-East off the board. That’s a win. It’ll raise the Dragonslayers name too.”

“Yeah. I think they’re actually starting to enjoy the hero work.”

“That’s good,” Steve said with a small smile. “Anyway, I should get going. Take care of yourself.”

“You too,” Frank said sincerely.

Steve dusted himself off and turned in midair. “Door to New York.”

A small square of blue appeared in front of him, quickly lengthening and widening into a large opening to the New York skyline, right on another rooftop. Steve stepped through with a wave, and the portal snapped shut.

 

 

Saturday 26th May, Foster Home, Chicago

“Oh my gosh, she’s adorable!” Ava gushed as Aster stared up at her, her teddy bear clutched to her chest.

Theo felt a great rush of relief that Ava liked Aster. She’d cooed over pictures of Aster that Theo had showed her, but everyone thought babies were cute in pictures. When they needed potty training? Less so. At least Aster was finally making progress on that.

Aster pointed one little hand at Ava. “Gull,” she said.

“That’s how she says girl,” Theo explained, crouching to Aster’s level. “Aster, this is my friend Ava. Do you want to say hello?”

Aster gave him a wide-eyed look, then looked back and Ava and waved her hand. “Haah,” she said.

“And that’s how she says hi,” Theo added.

“Awww,” Ava cooed.

“Aster, you want to play with your ball?” Theo asked. Aster perked up at that and toddled off to the striped ball next to the armchair. Theo followed, sitting cross-legged on the carpet as Aster tried to pick up the ball without letting go of her teddy.

“So how long’s she been walking?” Ava said, sinking onto the carpet perpendicular to Theo as Aster squashed both ball and teddy to her chest, before the ball slipped loose again.

“About nine months,” Theo said as Aster set a hand on the ball and started rolling it along as she toddled towards Theo. “Talking took a little longer though.”

“So what was her first word? Was it you?” Ava asked.

“No, it was ‘ball’,” Theo admitted. “Although she said my name eventually. Hey Aster, can you say Theo?”

Aster stopped the ball at Theo’s feet and pointed at him. “Feo,” she said. “Ball.” She pointed at the ball.

“Close enough,” Theo said with a smile. He set a hand on the ball and rolled it over to Ava. Aster shrieked with delight and toddled after it, teddy now dangling from one hand. She smacked the top of the ball with her hand and said “Ball!”

Ava bemusedly rolled the ball back over to Theo. Aster giggled and followed it, hitting the top again.

“She can do this for ages,” Theo admitted, rolling the ball to Ava again. “She loves that ball as much as her teddy.”

“It’s cute,” Ava said, beaming as Aster smacked the ball and looked at her expectantly. “I always wondered what having siblings would be like.”

“I guess it’s different for everyone,” Theo admitted as he caught the ball. “I mean, I was old enough to take care of Aster most of the time. I don’t think a lot of other siblings do that much.”

“True,” Ava said as Aster smacked the ball.

“Feo! Ball!”

“Don’t worry, I’m playing,” Theo said to Aster, rolling the ball again. She giggled and chased after it.

“Still, it’s cool that you’re so good with her,” Ava said. “I mean, between school and the job, I feel like I’ve never got enough time, you know?”

“Yeah, I get that,” Theo agreed. Being a Ward in Chicago was a pretty decent life- he’d made friends with the rest of the team, he was doing well in school- it felt completely different to his old life in Brockton Bay.

Not that he could completely leave that behind, no matter how much he’d like. Faultline and her crew had created a portal to that empty Earth a few months back, and Elpis had passed through Chicago back in March to crack down on some of the Folk who were causing problems around the portal.

Luckily, she hadn’t given Theo much notice- and he’d preferred it. With the list of defeated villains she was racking up, she only seemed more intimidating to him.

Ava rolled the ball back to him, breaking him out of his thoughts. Aster managed to pick the ball up and hold it out to him. Theo gently took it and bounced it in his hands, then tossed it over Aster’s head to Ava. Aster shrieked with delight and charged after her ball.

Being good with Aster wasn’t even a choice, really. She was his only family, innocent and sweet, and if Theo had anything to say about it, she’d stay that way as long as possible, untouched by their parent’s crap.

Watching her grow up was how he knew he was doing something right.

 

 

Tuesday 5th June, Alternate Earth

Genesis crashed through the window, unfolding her armoured wings from around herself and stabbing the points on the ends into the people inside. Her momentum carried them all to the floor, and she pulled her wings free, looking around the room with keen eyes. This form was a mixture of hawk and bat, four wings and no legs. She tip-toed on the points toward the desk and grabbed the silver briefcase in her teeth, then awkwardly turned and hauled herself out through the shattered window.

Down below, the rest of her teammates were dealing with the rest of the compound. Ballistic had made his way to a crate of ammo and was launching handfuls of bullets at the few remaining soldiers, along with loose bricks and other debris, while Perdition moved to flank them with his own gun, barely bothering with cover as he rewound any head that popped up. Sundancer’s sun was busy melting the vehicles over at the motor pool into slag, preventing anyone from driving out.

Screams came from the bunker off to the side, before Chimera re-emerged into the daylight. He’d clearly taken on the powers of other capes down there, judging from the way his Changer form had advanced. He was at full strength, with three heads, six arms and six legs, each third a crude imitation of one of the capes he’d copied. One was still a version of Ballistic, black and red angular armour and helmet, but another was a woman in black and grey fatigues, multicoloured swirls of light around her hands, and the third was a figure made of bluish liquid that had spread its arms out into a thin layer shielding the other two.

As she watched, a couple of bullets hit the goo and stopped dead. Chimera quickly swivelled, the woman raising an arm. The multicoloured swirl whipped out, and where it hit, the concrete wall turned into multicoloured foam that fizzed and popped. Where droplets of the foam hit, they hissed and ate into the ground, or the body of the poor soldier who’d been caught in the attack.

Perdition caught the last few soldiers from the side, and Chimera used the opening to push forward, using the goo arms to scoop up ammo for the Ballistic third to fire with. In seconds, everyone was dead.

Genesis made it to the ground as Sundancer came over, finished with the vehicles. “Clear the area,” she said, her sun floating high overhead, the heat beating down on them even worse than the actual sun in the sky. The rest of the team quickly scrambled back, and Sundancer brought her sun down on the remains of the compound. Everything burst into flames as the sun lowered, and then burned and melted to nothing as it touched down. The sun swept slowly from side to side, scouring everything, until all that was left was an irregular glassy crater and a few smouldering bits of broken buildings.

Genesis held up the briefcase. Ballistic took it and said, “Mission complete.”

A portal immediately opened for them- a small one, just large enough for the briefcase, showing a steel table in a white room. Ballistic slid the case through onto the table, and the portal closed.

The team turned as one and began walking back towards the exit point where Genesis’s body was stashed in a beaten-up van. Chimera shed his transformation as they went, returning to plain old Oliver, maybe a little more handsome than he'd been before he got powers. He opened the van door and helped Ballistic wheel Genesis’s real body out in her wheelchair. A second portal opened, large enough for them to walk through, and they stepped into the large windowless concrete room beyond.

The portal snapped shut. Their mission was complete. Their conditioning cut out.

Marissa dropped to her knees, wrapping her arms around herself. Oliver ran for the toilet, making it just in time to puke. Luke just pulled off his helmet and threw it in a corner with a curse.

Jess let go of her power, her constructed body dissolving into nothing, and opened her eyes. With some effort, she hauled herself out of the chair and worked her way over to the table. Even after Panacea had fixed her spine, and after months of building up her leg muscles,  walking was still difficult for her- but she did it every chance she got.

Cody dropped into a chair, not even bothering to take any of his costume pieces off. “Fuck,” he said at length.

Jess poured herself a glass of water, slopping a lot across the table as he hands shook, and gulped the water down. “Fuck,” she agreed.

Luke crouched down to gently pull Marissa to her feet. “Come on Mars, it’s over,” he said softly. “It’s all over.”

“They’ll send us out again,” Marissa mumbled. “They’ll say the words and we’ll be puppets and they’ll send us out to kill people again.”

“You didn’t kill anyone, Mars,” Luke said. “All you did was burn the place- if anything you were cremating them, being respectful.”

“Yeah, we did all the hard work,” Cody muttered.

Luke rounded on him. “Cody, shut the fuck up, I am not in the mood.”

Cody sank further into his chair. “Sorry,” he mumbled.

“Cauldron killed those people,” Jess said, pouring herself another glass, more carefully this time. “We didn’t have a choice in the matter- they controlled us.”

Marissa sniffed. “We still saw it and heard it, and the smell…”

Jess winced. They all knew the smell of burning bodies by now. It was hard to eat meat these days.

Oliver shuffled out of the bathroom, looking pale. Jess wordlessly poured him a glass and passed it to him.

“Let’s just rest while we can,” Luke said. “We don’t know when they’ll send us out again, but it’ll be easier to get through it with a full stomach. Let’s see what food we’ve got.”

Oliver gulped down the last of his water and wiped his mouth. “I’m not hungry,” he muttered.

“I know man, but you gotta eat something. Especially if you just upchucked your last meal.”

Cody pulled himself out of his chair. “So it’s my turn to cook, right?”

“Yeah,” Luke said, guiding Mars over to the couch and gently sitting her down. Jess sat down next to her and started taking her helmet off for her, then letting down her hair.

“I hate this,” Marissa mumbled.

“We all do,” Jess said. “So we’ll get through this together.”

Privately, Jess wondered if they’d be stuck here for the rest of their lives. Ever since Cauldron had snatched them up and put that Master conditioning in their heads, they’d just gone from one mission to the next, fighting and stealing, delivering power vials to Cauldron’s clients or, like today, taking them back from people who’d somehow pissed Cauldron off. And then they came back to a set of rooms with no outer doors, no windows, no contact with the outside world. Their food and clothing was delivered by portal, and anything else came from what they managed to snag during missions despite the conditioning propelling them onwards.

Lately it seemed like there were more deliveries than anything else- sometimes several in one day. Like Cauldron was trying to flood the market or something. Deep down, Jess wondered if something was coming.

Chapter 156: 15.10

Saturday 13th April 2013, Mathers Fallen Compound, Outside Wichita, Kansas

“The Crowleys are asking for transfers.”

Elijah hummed. “Anybody in particular?”

Christine shook her head- or rather, her fragment did. “Not really. They just want some muscle, or some brains. Maybe Ahrima- she’s useful, but not particularly necessary. And they need more eyes with the heroes getting bolder.”

The Crowleys also wanted to show off and get their names out there again. Leviathan’s attack last week had emboldened them like usual. They were reaching out to the McVeays as well- poor fools had never been the same since Behemoth’s death, although some insisted that the First would rise again.

“Well, they can’t get something for nothing,” Elijah pointed out. “We’ll have to see what they’re offering.”

Christine smiled. “Very good, dear.”

The rest of the compound was doing well, as far as she could see. Those that saw and heard her allowed her to see and hear through them, and thus she watched over them all. Over in the barn that served as a chapel, the preacher was speaking to the faithful, decrying the sins of the unworthy outside their gates, those that spoke of God but not Jesus, those that read from the Koran instead of the Bible, the gays and the trannies and the mutants and the so-called heroes that protected their godlessness. In other buildings, other followers went through all the business of keeping their little community alive, cooking and cleaning and repairing, sharpening blades and polishing guns.

The Mathers branch of the Fallen kept themselves apart from civilisation, unlike the McVeays and Crowleys. It made it easier to keep people close, and when they found people to bring into the fold, it was easier to find them a place in their family. Normally isolation would make them vulnerable, but Christine was their counter to that. Nobody could look upon her or sense her without a fragment of her blooming in their mind, and then she could know all that they knew, and twist their senses to betray them. A few times she’d sent would-be Thinkers to the looney bin for trying to find her, spending months thinking that the walls were bleeding spiders.

“Maybe Belial?” Elijah asked. “He’s been getting bored, wanting to go out and have some fun.”

“That’s a possibility,” Christine said. “I’ve been thinking he’d be good at a construction site- there’s probably a few in the city.”

Elijah smiled, the fang tattoos on his lips twisting into a grimace. “I’ll tell him that next time I see him- or are you already telling him?”

Christine smiled. “I’ll let you say it. Besides, he’s busy right now.”

Elijah nodded, putting his hands behind his head and tilting his head back. “Damn fine day…”

They both noticed it at the same time- something was falling out of the sky up above, little black dots.  They weren’t birds, the way they moved- they looked more like-

“Parachutes,” Elijah said, dumbfounded.

Christine immediately reached out to everyone in the compound that she could. “Everybody grab weapons now! There’s people coming at us! Now! Now!”

Everyone reacted, but not all well. A lot started panicking, especially the folks inside the church, with the preacher bellowing for calm. The soldiers and capes at least started arming themselves, hastily donning costumes and armour. Belial dashed to his pile of rocks to start forming them into his usual form, while Xaphan started oozing molten lava from his body.

Eligos was rushing outside, most of his armour on. Christine appeared before his eyes, pointing upward. “Shoot them down!” she demanded.

Eligos followed her finger and spotted the parachutes. “Like shooting skeet,” he grunted, pulling a hand back. She felt through his hand as air condensed into a blade between his fingers; then he whipped his hand forward and sent the blade hurtling up towards the lead parachute.

The parachute tried to move in midair, but Eligos’s blade sliced through the fabric and half the cords. The person went from drifting to plummeting, torn fabric streaming behind them.

“One down,” Eligos grinned, preparing another air blade.

The falling person suddenly disappeared, and a ball of fire appeared way off to the side with a thunderclap. The hero fell out of the fire, shedding the remains of the parachute and diving. The sunlight glinted off grey metal.

Christine felt her heart seize. Everybody in the states knew that exploding teleport by now. “Butcher,” she hissed. “It’s Butcher! The Butcher’s coming at us! We can’t kill her!”

People panicked some more at that- she started organising them through her fragments, speaking to Elijah in particular. “My son, I’m going to get people to try and hold Butcher down. I want you to try and ensnare her. If we can get something like that to our cause, we’ll be unstoppable.”

The thought of the Butcher as a believer, as a weapon, maybe even as a slut to bear children for the clan- that would be a true blessing. But only if they could catch her and make her theirs. They’d have to be careful.

Butcher was still falling, using her teleport to move sideways through the air. Every teleport also briefly stopped her fall, keeping her from going too fast. At least she wouldn’t die from hitting the ground- then who knew what would happen to all that power?

The other parachutes spread out, dodging Eligos’ blades now that they knew what to avoid. And through the eyes of people looking out past the fence, she could see other forces approaching, some in cars and on bikes, others riding on the backs of monstrous creatures. She recognised the dogs of Butcher’s minion, all bone and muscle, charging towards the west side with barks like cannon blasts.

What were the Undersiders doing all the way out here? They stayed on the East Coast mostly, everybody knew that. They travelled for Endbringer battles and for some big stuff, but what had the Fallen ever done to them? Kansas was a full day’s drive away from the coast.

Butcher teleported one last time, landing on top of the chapel barn. The explosion cracked the timbers, her weight broke them, and she plunged down through the roof to crash onto the empty stage.

Christine saw through the eyes of the flock as they turned to stare with mute horror as Elpis the Butcher pulled her legs from the shattered remains of the stage, brushing off splinters and dust as her cape unfurled from her back. She raised her head, haloed by the light from the hole, and pulled a pair of metal rods from her boots. She flicked them out to full length, and the tips crackled with electricity.

“Catch you fuckers at a bad time?” she roared.

Bless their hearts, the flock drew weapons- pistols and knives and clubs and whatnot. Not a member of the Fallen went without a weapon.

Against the likes of Elpis, they might as well have been children’s toys. Elpis threw herself into the crowd, insects erupting from her armour to sting and bite while she waded through with fists and feet and clubs. Blades skated off her armour, bullets flattened themselves against her, and the Fallen were helpless as she snapped wrists and crushed ankles, smashed ribs and broke noses. The preacher pulled a snub-nose revolver- Elpis snatched it off him, crushed it like putty, then knocked him unconscious with a headbutt.

Elijah was waiting outside, dressed as Valefor with his corset and feathers to resemble the Simurgh, sheltered behind Belial’s rocky bulk. Elpis crashed through the doors in a spray of splinters and a roar, tossing a follower aside and joining her rods into a double-ended spear. Insects swarmed around her as she sprinted towards Belial.

Then she disappeared, and her beautiful son screamed as fire and steel slammed into his back. Elpis spun him around, and through her son’s eyes, Christine saw the thick metal plate that had slammed down to cover Elpis’s eyes, preventing eye contact.

Christine felt fear slam into her. They’d prepared for this.

Stiff fingers rammed into Elijah’s throat, choking him before he could say a word, and then an armoured fist smashed into his ribs, then his jaw. Bones cracked and teeth flew, and Elpis threw him aside like a sack of potatoes.

Belial, that dumb slow bastard, had taken a whole two seconds to turn and face Elpis, but his fists were faster, striking down at the Butcher. Elpis simply leaned out of the way, grabbed his arm, and tore a huge chunk out of it, then threw herself at Belial, claws sinking into the rock that made up his chest and ripping more away. Belial frantically tried to pull her off, but agonising pain shot through him, and then Elpis’s hand clamped around his face and dragged his body halfway out. Her touch was painful, not through pressure but something else, and Christine felt Belial falter with weakness.

Elpis backhanded him and pulled him free, the rock body collapsing into rubble. Christine tried to see through Belial’s flickering vision, but the man was slipping into unconsciousness already.

The defenders on the fence were firing at the invaders with bullets and powers, bolts of lightning and gobs of burning oil, but the attackers dodged and blocked them well. One raised a hand and let out a cloud of darkness that swept forward over the Fallen- Christine hissed as her vision there went totally black.

Something hit Eligos as he was throwing another blade- the shot went wide and cut the corner off a house. Through the pain, Christine saw Elpis again, clawing the armour off Eligos’s belly and punching him hard enough to fold him in two. Then she was gone again.

Without Eligos trying to shoot down the parachutes, the heroes swooped in to land. One was a man made of metal, shirtless and snarling as he landed hard enough for his feet to sink into the ground. He tossed the parachute aside and started attacking, his hands lengthening into clubs.

One girl with black hair came down near the fence. Her arms unfurled into ribbons that yanked the defenders off the fence and threw them into each other.

Another girl in sporting pads and massive black boots landed on the other side, took a running start and leapt over a building, drop-kicking the gunman perched on top. Christine lost track of her as the gunman fell.

On the east side, Christine recognised the people attacking- members of Haven, a team of heroes who called themselves Christian without the fire. A woman in a red robe with gold edges flicked a hand, and the fence dissolved into petals that swarmed over the Fallen. Her teammates followed after, one creating a golden hoop that fired lasers around. Another spun a sling in his hand and loosed a shot that shattered a wall.

A wall of dirt approached the south side, soaking up every bit of firepower the defenders threw at it. Heroes fired from behind its cover- a bolt of black-and-white zigzags, a lash of blood-red. Something charged through the wall like a ghost, ragged purple cloak caught on bony spikes, and bodyslammed a Fallen to the floor.

The last parachute landed in the midst of a knot of soldiers- not a person, but a crate. It fell to pieces as it touched the earth, and thousands of insects poured out, flies and wasps and hornets and all manner of bugs. Butcher teleported in and drew the bugs in around herself, flattening the soldiers ruthlessly. Some were hit with pure pain, some were overcome with rage- Christine’s fragments were untouched, which only meant that she was helpless to watch as her followers broke themselves on Elpis and each other.

The fences were broken on all sides as heroes crashed through the weakened defences- giant dogs, total darkness, a massive metal figure that picked people up and bashed them together. Haven stormed across the compound, tearing apart entire buildings, while the earth wall pulled down the fence and freaks poured through the gap. One boy with white skin and shockingly yellow hair let forth some birdlike creature of yellow goo from his chest, while a whip-thin greenish freak zipped forward, handing out slaps and punches like Halloween candy.

Beasts and darkness, twisted freaks, heathens, and a monster that wore a plague of insects like a cloak. It felt like Judgement Day for the Fallen.

Christine slapped herself. No. No! Judgement would come for the unworthy- their path was righteous! The Fallen would survive this  as they would survive Armageddon.

Surely.

Xaphan bore down on Elpis, his magma coating burning through her insects. Christine felt hope as Elpis fell back, not even daring to touch him. Xaphan might have been a brainless oaf from the McVeays, but damned if he wasn’t effective. Butcher wouldn’t be able to touch him, let alone strike him, without her weapons melting to slag-

Pain arced through Xaphan, and he faltered to scream. Elpis whistled high and sharp, and nearby heroes diverted towards him.

A rock crashed into Xaphan’s shoulder, bursting the magma off. Lasers cut into him, soil rose up around his legs, bands of glowing white locked around his middle. A girl in a striped yellow suit and cape stepped forward with the slinger from Haven- he shot another stone at Xaphan, the girl gestured, and an entire car hurled itself at Xaphan too. The sheer mass ripped his magma body apart, and he tumbled across the grass, legs broken and wailing girlishly in pain.

The last thing Christine saw through his eyes was Elpis’s fist coming down like the hammer of God-

Christine stood up from her bed, grabbing the shotgun off the wall. The bastards would come for her sooner or later, and she wasn’t planning on making it easy for them. Filthy unbelievers hurting her people, hurting her son, because they didn’t understand the truth of the Endbringers. She might go out, but she’d take a few with her- and when they looked at her, she’d give them visions from the bowels of hell itself.

She ripped her dresser drawer open and grabbed the box of shells, hastily loading them into the gun. They wouldn’t all be bulletproof.

Something pressed against the back of her neck, and then every muscle in her body seized at once. Pain ripped through her like wildfire, the gun dropping from spasming fingers as a scream forced its way out through her gritted teeth.

Then her body gave out- she toppled forward and slammed her head into the dresser before slumping to the carpet.

The pain came again, and this time the darkness claimed her.

 

Christine woke standing up, arms pressed to her side and head against the wall. Thick bands of wood had been drawn out of the wall to bind her in place, leaving her unable to so much as wiggle. She gasped for breath through sore ribs- although everything else was sore too.

The barrel of a pistol was pressed against her forehead. Elpis stared at her from the other end, snarling through sharp teeth.

She reached out at once to her followers, checking on them. Plenty were unconscious, but all of them were tied hand and foot, some of them gagged or bound with heavier restraints. Elijah was still alive, praise be, but her baby boy looked terrible, his jaw bloodied and throat bruised, with one of those freak monster capes standing over him. The big spiky one that had run through the fence- he wore a metal helmet that covered everything but the eyes, and a ragged purple cape that had been swept clear of the spikes that jutted from his shoulders and forearms.

“Elijah, sweetheart,” she breathed. “Right hand for yes, left hand for no- can you speak?”

Elijah flexed the fingers on his left hand- no.

“They tell me your name is Mama Mathers,” the Butcher said. “They say you’re the one in charge, and that you’re the reason Thinkers go nuts when they try to look for you freaks. Your people have been beaten, bound, and the PRT’s arriving any minute to throw them in jail. There’s no way out of this for you. The only question is how badly this goes.”

Christine contacted all her Fallen, asking for help. Xaphran was buried up to his waist in a pit, Belial was wrapped in ropes, Eligos was out cold. She tried reaching out to the other branches, but it had been too long, the connection had grown weak.

“Option one- you surrender, we stuff you in a bag so you can’t use your power on anyone, and the PRT tosses you in a deep dark cell. Maybe even the Birdcage. Option two- you resist, try to use your power to escape. And because your power is so damn dangerous, we will be forced to kill you.”

Butcher pressed the gun a little harder against Christine’s head. “So. Are you going to cooperate?”

Christine was hurting all over, stiff and sore with a murderous headache. But she wasn’t beaten.

“Elijah, my dear son, my sweetheart,” she breathed in his ear, “Remember your mama loves you. Keep the faith, no matter what.”

She lashed out at Elpis, invading her sight and hearing with every horrible thing she could think of- screams of agony, devils ripping people apart and devouring the flesh, maggots and worms crawling out of the eye sockets of babies, blood gushing from the walls.

“Unfortunate,” Elpis said.

 

 

There was a gunshot from upstairs, and the vision of Mama disappeared from Elijah’s sight. The Fallen capes and soldiers flinched at the sound.

Elijah jerked and thrashed, trying to haul himself upright, to grab and fight and kill- his hands were bound but he could still strangle.

The big freak guarding him pressed a boot down on him and forced him to the floor again. Elijah struggled, but the monster cape was unmoved. Elijah had to stop for breath, and once he sucked a breath in through his aching jaw and ribs, he started to sob and couldn’t stop.

Heavy footsteps thudded down the stairs, and then a voice he’d heard on TV said “Mama Mathers refused to surrender. Nobody go in there- it’s a mess.”

Elijah moaned and thrashed his head from side to side. He tried to force words out through his throat, to control the fuckers and make them kill each other as recompense for killing his Mama, but it was a struggle just to breathe. His throat seized and he started coughing weakly.

“Wraith, you got a handle on him?” Elijah managed to turn his head, still coughing, to look at Elpis. She had dirt streaked here and there, but her armour was still a clean dark grey. It wasn’t fair- she should be torn up and wounded from fighting them, not looking all neat and tidy.

“Yeah, I’ve got him,” the big freak said, lifting his foot slightly. “What’d you do to him anyway?”

“Hit him in the throat,” Elpis said with a shrug. “I’ll put a blindfold on him later- his power needs eye contact and speech, so as long as we keep one out of the equation, we’re good.”

“Ruthless of you, boss,” said a girl in black with a grey demon mask, appearing out of nowhere behind Elpis. Several people flinched- one of the girls screamed.

“Imp,” said the Butcher, unruffled. “Good job on taking her out. You left the room before the shot, right?”

“Absolutely. I wouldn’t want to be there for that,” Imp said solemnly, resting her hands on her hips.

“Good.”

“Yeah, I wouldn’t want to get bits of cultist brain all over me,” Imp continued with a cackling laugh.

Elijah jerked towards her with a gurgling groan, weeping with fury. How dare she?! How dare she make jokes about his Mama’s death?! His Mama, who’d raised him right and taught him the truth of the world and welcomed people into the family of the Fallen. How dare they?!

Wraith’s boot pressed down harder on him again. “Woah, what’s with him?” Imp asked.

Butcher gave Elijah a considering look. “Were you related to her?” she asked.

Elijah managed another gurgling noise.

“I’ll take that as a yes. Sorry for your loss. I did give her the option to surrender.”

Elijah slumped again. Mama never would have surrendered. Not to heretics who fought the divine Endbringers, who denied the truth of the world. Tears fell from his eyes.

Elpis clapped her hands with a metallic clank. “Right. PRT should be arriving soon, let’s not get cocky. Assume they’ll try to break out, be ready for trouble. Can someone tell Gully to clear the road so the trucks can get in?”

“I’ll go,” said a thing that was broomstick-thin, skin stretched so tight over his skull that his eyes bulged out.

“Thanks, Whippersnap,” Elpis replied. As Whippersnap zipped out the door in a blur, Elpis continued “Any injuries left? Sanguine?”

“Doing okay,” called a voice from another room. “Blesk got caught by a lucky shot, but he’ll be fine.”

“I sure as fuck don’t feel fine!” said another person in a voice that sounded like a radio with bad distortion.

“He’s just being a baby,” Sanguine said confidently.

“Uh, Elpis?” This one wasn’t a mutant like most of the others- a dark-haired girl in big boots, helmet and kneepads and whatnot like she was going skating down at the roller rink. She was standing in the doorway to the big meeting room, cradling something in her arms. “I found them,” she said in a low voice. “They were mounted on the wall.”

Elpis’s head whipped around, and she strode over to the girl. “Let me see,” she ordered.

The girl held out her arms, revealing something like wooden sticks. Elpis traced a hand over them gently, then nodded sharply. “Good work, Vortex.”

“Are they going to be okay?”

Elpis sighed. “Panacea‘s healing them up, so they’ll be alright physically. Emotionally…” She trailed off. “PRT’s coming up the road. Let’s get these guys hauled outside. Wraith, hold Valefor up, I’ll blindfold him now.”

Elijah struggled, but Wraith pulled him to his feet anyway, and no matter how he tossed his head, Elijah couldn’t stop the Butcher from sliding a strip of black cloth over his eyes.

 

 

Ascension Via Christi St Francis Hospital, Wichita, Kansas

“Knock knock,” said a voice from outside the tent. “Can I come in?”

Reconciliation glanced at the kids, who exchanged looks. “Okay,” chirped Fen, hopping out of bed.

The flap was pushed back, and Elpis strode in, carrying a canvas bag in one hand. She stopped and dramatically clasped a hand to her chest. “My goodness, you recovered fast,” she said in a dramatic voice. “How could this ever have happened?”

“Oh, stop being a comedian,” Panacea said from her seat on the other side. “The kids are doing well though- big lunch and lots of snacks, and there was enough for me to work with.”

“Yup,” Fen said, bouncing in place. She did look a lot better- the swollen eye was back to normal, wide and violet; the scrape on her cheek was gone, leaving her fine blue-grey coat unmarred, and even her missing tooth had come in again. The stumps of her horns just above the eyebrows were now rounded nubs, without the crude saw marks from the attack, hopefully to slowly grow back. She was still stick-thin, but that was apparently what she always looked like- stretched out and narrowed, so any clothing looked baggy and draped on her. “My head feels better too!”

“Your work, I’m guessing?” Elpis said to Reconciliation, raising an eyebrow.

“I didn’t need to do much,” Reconciliation said, folding his arms over the clasped-hands symbol on his chest. “The kids are pretty resilient- all they needed was a little dose to get them back to normal.”

Peat nodded, still sat on his bunk. He was the quieter of the two, although privately Reconciliation thought that might have been because he’d got hurt worse. Both eyes blacked, nose broken, cuts and bruises everywhere. All the discarded bandages made a small heap at the foot of his bed, along with the neck brace and the sling for his arm. Still, Reconciliation and Panacea had fixed him up, even working around his bark-like skin and leaves for hair.

Honestly, he could understand why Elpis and the other Case 53s had responded so quickly, and so fiercely. Case 53s reached out to one another, to commiserate about their problems and offer mutual support- he’d heard a couple of them mention a group chat, even. Peat and Fen were the babies of the bunch, and with the added problems of needing to move constantly, phobias of vehicles and a distrust of the PRT. They had a decent online following, sending them money or offering places to stay, setting them up with tutors and the like- which meant the story of them getting attacked by some Fallen biker had spread like wildfire within their community.

“Well, I’m glad to see you’re both doing better,” Elpis said. “Is the tent alright?”

“It’s good,” Peat said. “We’re gonna have to move it soon though.” He indicated a patch of grass next to his bed that was sprouting tiny shoots and saplings, Peat’s power slowly accelerating the plant growth. And in another corner, Fen’s power was bleeding into the ground, turning it from dry lawn to soggy marsh. If they hung around a few more days, the hospital’s lawn would turn into a marsh.

“No problem,” Elpis said. “I know this one’s a bit larger than you guys need, but I was thinking we could go shopping later if you like, get you some stuff? New tents, new phones, all the essentials. It’ll be a lot easier to travel with the right equipment.”

“You don’t have to do that,” Fen said in the embarrassed tone of a kid who didn’t want to be spoiled.

“No, but I want to. Anyway, helping a couple of kids is a good use of money.”

“Just let her,” Panacea said with a roll of her eyes. “She’s not going to stop trying to help- it’ll be easier if you just go with it.”

“Hey,” Elpis said in a wounded tone that was undercut by her grin.

“I’m up for it,” Peat said, sliding off his bunk.

“Great.” Elpis paused, then took a knee, moving the bag around in front of her. “There’s one other thing,” she said in a softer tone of voice. “I wasn’t sure if you two wanted to see this, but I figured I should give you the option. When we took down the Fallen… We found these in their compound.”

“Found…” Fen trailed off, staring at the bag, trembling.

Peat walked up, looking nauseous. “Our horns?”

“Yes.”

Peat swallowed. “I wanna see.”

“If you’re sure. Fen? Do you want to leave?”

Fen jerkily shook her head.

“Okay then.” Elpis unzipped the bag and gently drew out the horns that some bastard had chainsawed off for trophies.

It was immediately obvious which belonged to who- Fen’s horns were like a gazelle’s, gently curved, black at the base and reddening towards the points. Peat’s were a double pair that spiralled up like a goat’s, and they looked woody in texture.

Fen reached one thin hand down to touch a finger to one of her horns, then yanked it back like she’d been scalded. “Bury them,” she managed, stepping back.

“Yeah,” Peat said, putting an arm around Fen’s shoulders. “Bury ‘em somewhere.”

“Alright.” Elpis repacked the horns into the bag and zipped it shut again.

 

 

Sunday 14th April, Private Chartered Plane, en-route to Brockton Bay

Aisha turned off her game with a groan. After fifteen levels of building towers and mulching goblins, the shine had worn off. She’d brought books that Taylor had recommended, but she wasn’t in the mood for any of that either.

With a shrug, she hauled to her feet and stretched extravagantly, groaning as her butt protested all that time sat on an uncomfortable seat. When she’d heard they were taking a private plane to go kick some cultist ass, she’d imagined a swanky jet with comfy seats and a mini-bar- not a cargo plane with netting on the walls and seats that felt like they’d been scientifically designed to prevent anyone from sitting comfortably.

She had to turn her power back off- damn thing had slipped while she was gaming. The others looked up as she walked around, taking big lunging steps to wake her legs back up.

“You alright?” Brian asked, pausing the music he was listening to through one earbud. Next to him, Isabella pulled the other earbud out.

“Yeah, just bored.”

“We crossed state lines and flattened most of a cult less than a day ago, how are you already bored again?” Isabella asked.

“With my mighty ADHD brain, I get bored much faster than you plebs,” Aisha said loftily.

“Pretty sure that’s not how you use that word,” Lisa said, sprawled across three seats with an eyemask on. Somehow she had cushions to keep her comfortable, rather than wearing out her spine like the rest of them.

“Whatever,” Aisha said. “Anybody got anything fun to do?”

“I’ve got a bag of gummy bears and comic books,” Tarquin volunteered, holding up the bag.

Aisha pointed at him. “You. You get me.” She strutted over and held out a hand. “Gimme.”

“I don’t understand how you can eat so much junk food and stay skinny,” Isabella commented as Tarquin gave Aisha a handful of gummy bears.

“High metabolism,” Amy said without looking up from her phone. She was stretched out across multiple seats too, but in her case she had Taylor’s lap for a pillow as well as cushions. Taylor was watching something on her phone, earphones firmly in, occasionally stroking Amy’s hair. Her multibook contraption was also set up a little way down, with several books mounted on stands for Taylor to read through Insect-o-Vision, a clockwork mechanism turning the pages at the flick of an ant. Apparently it was a good way to maximise Butcher satisfaction.

“It’s true,” Aisha agreed. “Besides, I think we deserve a treat. We did just crush a bunch of crazies and help a pair of cute little kids. Another successful mission for the Undersiders!”

“I hope they’re okay,” Isa said, leaning into Brian’s shoulder. “They went through so much.”

“Haven said they’re looking after them for a few days, letting them rest,” Brian said. “They’ll put the kids in touch with a therapist too, one who does phone appointments.”

“Their horns will grow back in time,” Amy said, glancing up from her phone at last. “I added a little accelerated growth, so they’ll have something noticeable in a few months.”

“And we’ll keep an eye on them just in case,” Taylor said, eyes still focused on her phone. “I offered to set them up if they’re ever near our range, so we might see them in person again.”

“That’s sweet,” Tarquin said.

“They’re good kids,” Taylor said, frowning slightly. “They didn’t deserve any of that.”

Chapter 157: 15.11

Friday March 28th, Abernathy Studios, New York City

“This is such a dumb idea,” Butcher complained.

“Butcher, for the last time, shut up,” I growled, checking my armour over again one more time.

“No, seriously! We’ve got three months until the big day comes! We should be out there cracking skulls, tracking leads, something! Instead we’re doing this shit?”

“We need to pay attention to the public-facing stuff too,” Tactical pointed out. “This will reach millions at once- there’s value to that.”

“And the fact that Nora’s going to be tuning in is no factor at all?” Needler asked with a teasing smirk.

“I’m not denying that,” Tactical admitted. He and Nora stayed in touch through emails and calls and the occasional visit, and he’d given her a heads-up about tonight. The Butchers liked to tease him about it, but only lightly- they all liked the little girl too.

“It’s kind of nuts, right?” Rotter pointed out. “Like, I know we’ve done some crazy shit, but this is still something we never would’ve got a chance to do before.”

“Last thing for this evening,” Kevin Yarrow said from his desk onstage, toothy grin growing even wider. “We’ve got a very special guest with us tonight; so special in fact that we couldn’t give any heads-up. Tonight we’ve got a famous hero, well-known for her philanthropic efforts-”

There was a rumble of oohs from the audience. I straightened my cape one last time and tucked all my extra bugs away.

“-for her work in rehabilitating former villains-”

The oohs were louder as a few people in the crowd seemed to catch on. Kevin’s smile hit maximum wideness.

“-and for ending the Slaughterhouse Nine! All the way from Brockton Bay, please welcome Elpis, leader of the Undersiders!”

The studio audience burst into excited screaming as I walked from my little hidden waiting area at stage left onto the thick blue carpet. I’d polished my armour and touched up the paint, and left the bigger weapons in a locked box back at the dressing room. A few butterflies fluttered around me for effect as I strode along, waving to the audience with a practiced smile. The studio lights were blinding, but I didn’t let that phase me.

Kevin stood up from his desk to shake my hand, still grinning. Up close I could see he was sweating slightly under the hot lights- I wondered how much product he needed to keep his swept-back hairstyle intact. I pumped his hand a few times, grinning back, before sinking into one of the plush armchairs he gestured to. The audience were still yelling and cheering as I flicked my cape out over the backrest and let the butterflies settle on my shoulders.

“So, Elpis, welcome to the show,” Kevin began, leaning sideways on his desk. “We really appreciate you coming all this way.”

“Oh, it’s no problem,” I said with a wave of my hand. “It’s great to be here.”

That was mostly true- I’d already planned a mission in New York when I’d agreed to appear on Tonight! With Kevin Yarrow, but I was actually happy to be here. It definitely spoke well of my career that I’d got an invite to appear on one of the nation’s biggest talk shows. The rest of the team had had opinions on coming along, but the studio had politely pointed out that Elpis was the one they wanted.

Personally I’d just been glad that I wouldn’t have to worry about wrangling Imp on live TV.

“Well, I think everyone in the audience is happy to have you too. You’ve done some great work in New York.” More cheers and whoops- someone yelled ‘You rock, Elpis!’ and got a couple of laughs.

“I’d like to think so- It was definitely satisfying to take down the Hardshells.”

“Not exactly hard though,” Tock Tick said with a sneer.

“Not exactly hard though,” I echoed, buffing my knuckles against my breastplate dismissively. Kevin laughed.

“Well, I think we’ve got a few pictures from the press release, if we can get them up?” The screen behind changed from the stylised New York skyline to a picture from the last time I was in town.

Honestly, it was pretty good. I’d just pried Crabcake out of her armour, and I stood atop the remains, holding her by the collar in one hand while I held the torn-off hydraulic claw of her suit over my head. The photographer who’d snapped it had managed to frame me dead-centre, and the light caught my roaring face just right.

“Looks like something off a metal album cover,” Bearskin noted with approval. He had a point- all that was missing was lightning and a mountain in the background.

“Honestly, they were badly matched against me,” I said with a shrug. “Once I could physically touch their armour I could pull chunks off it or just rust it all to uselessness.”

“I understand you made use of the leftovers once they were arrested?” Kevin said leadingly. I nodded.

“Yeah, most of it got passed to the Protectorate for study, but there was a lot of scrap metal too damaged or not important enough to bother with.
